=== PAGE 11 ===
SUMMARY
This summary aims to give you an overview of the information contained in this
prospectus. As this is a summary, it does not contain all the information that may be
important to you. You should read the entire prospectus before you decide to invest in the
Shares. There are risks associated with any investment. Some of the particular risks in
investing in the Shares are set out in the section headed ‘‘Risk factors’’ in this prospectus.
You should read that section carefully before you decide to invest in the Shares. Various
expressions used in this section are defined or explained in ‘‘Definitions’’ and ‘‘Glossary of
Technical Terms’’ in this prospectus.
OVERVIEW
We are an integrated prefabricated steel structure building (‘‘PS building’’)
subcontracting service provider in the industrial sector of PS building market. We offer
integrated services for construction projects across industries, covering project design and
optimization, procurement, manufacturing and installation. We are primarily engaged in
the construction of PS buildings in the PRC, and to a lesser extent, overseas. By leveraging
our technology and expertise, we have built a reputation in China’s industrial sector of the
PS building market. According to the F&S Report, we ranked third in China’s industrial
sector of the PS building market in terms of revenue in 2024, representing a 3.5% market
share; and the top two players capturing a market share of 35.8% and 6.5%, respectively.
According to the F&S Report, the industrial sector of the PS building market involves
the design, production, and installation of steel-based construction components, offering
superior efficiency, strength, and adaptability across industrial, commercial, and residential
applications. In the industrial sector, PS buildings are especially valued for their ability to
accommodate large spans, enable rapid assembly and installation and provide scalability,
making them an optimal choice for modern industrial construction. We are recognized for
delivering integrated PS building subcontracting services tailored to diverse project
requirements and our brand of ‘‘USAS’’ has gained recognition within the industry and
market.
– 1 –

=== PAGE 12 ===
SUMMARY
Our Business Categories
Our business is organized into three business categories, defined by revenue
recognition models and operational characteristics: (i) PS building subcontracting
services, (ii) general contracting services, and (iii) industrial environmental equipment.

SUMMARY
PS building subcontracting services
PS building subcontracting services are the cornerstone of our business. This business
category integrates design, manufacturing, on-site installation, and quality assurance to
deliver comprehensive subcontracting services tailored to diverse industrial project
requirements. Our revenue from PS building subcontracting services decreased to
RMB1,293.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2023 from RMB1,770.7 million for
the year ended December 31, 2022, primarily attributable to the completion of substantial
construction work for certain large projects in 2022. Our revenue from PS building
subcontracting services decreased to RMB1,240.5 million for the year ended December 31,
2024 from RMB1,293.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2023. The decrease was
primarily because a significant portion of our PS building subcontracting projects
commenced construction in the fourth quarter of 2024 and generated limited revenue
during the year. Our revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2025 increased to
RMB1,247.3 million compared to RMB442.2 million for the same period in 2024, primarily
due to the capacity expansion needs of our major customer in the automotive and auto parts
sector during late 2024 and 2025. Leveraging our long-standing cooperative relationships
with such major customer, we successfully secured a number of large-scale PS building
subcontracting projects with them. Our gross profit margin for PS building subcontracting
services during the Track Record Period remained relatively stable at 13.6%, 15.5%,
13.3%, 12.0% and 10.7% for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six
months ended June 30, 2024 and 2025, respectively. For the six months ended June 30, 2025,
our gross profit margin decreased slightly to 10.7% primarily because we undertook certain
large-scale projects with our major customer with relatively low gross profit margins to gain
market share.
General contracting services
In addition to our core PS building subcontracting service business category, we have
expanded into general contracting services. As a general contractor, we oversee the entire
project lifecycle, including project implementation, construction of primary structures,
quality control, scheduling, safety, and budget management. Our revenue from general
contracting services decreased to RMB89.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2023
from RMB100.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2022, primarily due to the
completion timing of one project, given that the total number of projects in this business
category is in the single digits. Our revenue from general contracting services increased to
RMB182.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 from RMB89.9 million for the
year ended December 31, 2023 primarily driven by the increase in the number of our general
contracting projects from three in 2023 to eight in 2024. Our gross profit margin for general
contracting services increased sharply to 8.3% for the year ended December 31, 2023 from
1.4% for the year ended December 31, 2022. The primary reason for the low gross profit
margin for the year ended December 31, 2022 was that we started to generate revenue from
our general contracting services business category in 2022. As a new market player, our
strategic focus was to engage clients and foster business development. Our gross profit
margin decreased to 3.8% for the year ended December 31, 2024 from 8.3% for the year
ended December 31, 2023, primarily because we carried out the general contracting work
for four PC building projects that did not involve PS building components in 2024. As these
– 3 –

=== PAGE 14 ===
SUMMARY
projects did not involve undertaking major PS building construction components by
ourselves, but subcontracting to third-party subcontractors, we recorded relatively lower
margin for these projects. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, our revenue increased
sharply to RMB141.5 million compared with RMB21.1 million for the same period in 2024,
mainly attributable to the general contracting projects we secured in 2024 and the revenue
generated from these projects in 2025. Given the original scale of our general contracting
business was relatively small and the revenue base was low, with the continued growth of
this business category, the growth rate has been comparatively high. Our gross profit
margin for this business category remained relatively stable at 3.2% for the six months
ended June 30, 2025 compared to 4.3% for the six months ended June 30, 2024.
Industrial environmental equipment
Our industrial environmental equipment business category was established to address
the rising demand for specialized products in industrial manufacturing environments. This
business category primarily focuses on the Machinery Filtering and Acoustic Systems
(‘‘MFAS’’) line, which currently generates the vast majority of our revenue. The MFAS line
provides customized intake, exhaust, and dust filtration systems, as well as noise reduction
equipment specifically designed for gas turbines. In addition to MFAS, we are developing
and commercializing the Air Pollution Control (‘‘APC’’) product line. The APC line offers
advanced flexible dust control products and services that are versatile and adaptable to a
wide range of industrial facilities.
During the Track Record Period, revenue from sale of industrial environmental
equipment was predominately derived from overseas orders. Our revenue increased from
RMB31.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2022 to RMB69.4 million for the year
ended December 31, 2023, and further increased to RMB100.0 million for the year ended
December 31, 2024. The increase of revenue was primarily driven by the increase of overseas
orders, reflecting growing demand for industrial environmental equipment overseas. Our
revenue decreased from RMB46.2 million for the six months ended June 30, 2024 to
RMB35.3 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025, primarily attributable to a
decrease in the number of orders received by us in the first half of 2025. Given the relatively
high value of individual orders in this business category, a reduction in order volume had a
significant impact on overall revenue. Our gross profit margin for industrial environmental
equipment increased from 1.3% for the year ended December 31, 2022 to 9.5% for the year
ended December 31, 2023 mainly due to the travel restrictions for the pandemic in 2022,
resulting in the inflation of our shipping costs. Our gross profit margin for industrial
environmental equipment increased to 18.9% for the year ended December 31, 2024 from
9.5% for the year ended December 31, 2023, primarily because (i) a long-standing customer
awarded us two orders with high margins in 2024, reflecting their recognition of the quality
of our products and services; and (ii) we engaged an Australian customer, who awarded us a
high-margin order. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, our gross profit margin
increased to 20.7% from 13.9% for the same period in 2024. This was primarily because all
sales were derived from the sales of MFAS products to two existing customers, the high
similarity of which enabled us to achieve effective cost control.

COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE
The competitive landscape of China’s industrial sector of the PS building market is
represented by a highly concentrated structure with the largest player holding a dominant
position in the industry. According to the F&S Report, we ranked third in the field,
representing a 3.5% market share in 2024 and the top two players capturing a market share
of 35.8% and 6.5%, respectively.
STRENGTHS
We believe that the following strengths contribute to our success and differentiate us
from our competitors: (i) distinctive business model and service advantages; (ii)
comprehensive professional certifications and qualification profile; (iii) strong design and
research and development capabilities; (iv) robust production and product distribution
management capabilities; (v) advanced information management system empowering
efficient operations; and (vi) highly experience core team. For details, please refer to
‘‘Business — Strengths’’ in this prospectus.
– 7 –

=== PAGE 18 ===
SUMMARY
STRATEGIES
Guided by our green building vision, we plan to implement the following targeted
strategies to strengthen our market position and drive long-term growth, building on our
commitment to innovation and sustainability: (i) strengthen core business competitiveness
and achieve multidimensional growth; (ii) foster synergy across business categories to drive
diversified growth; (iii) deepen overseas market expansion and strengthen international
presence; and (iv) drive transformation with digitalization and intelligent technologies.
OUR PRODUCTION AND EXPANSION PLAN
Our production capabilities are currently supported by our advanced production
facilities located in (i) Shanghai, (ii) Suzhou, Jiangsu Province and (iii) Jiangmen,
Guangdong Province. Our production facilities are equipped with advanced production
lines to support production of PS building components as well as industrial environmental
equipment to efficiently meet diverse needs of our business. For the years ended December
31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2025, the utilization rate for (i) our
PS building components was 128.3%, 88.1%, 101.7% and 158.7%, respectively; and (ii) our
industrial environmental equipment was 50.9%, 72.7%, 85.9% and 82.7%, respectively.
To support expanded production capacity and better serve both domestic and
international markets, we plan to expand and upgrade our current production facilities
as well as construct new production facilities in Thailand to support local projects in
Southeast Asia. For details, please refer to ‘‘Business — Our Production — Production
Facilities — Expansion plans’’ in this prospectus.
OUR PROJECTS
For the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30,
2025, the tender success rates for (i) our PS building subcontracting projects were 27.8%,
30.3%, 22.7% and 32.1%, respectively; and (ii) our general contracting projects were
25.0%, 20.0%, 35.3% and 18.8%, respectively.

RISK FACTORS
We believe that there are certain risks involved in our operations. The more significant
risks relating to our business and industry include: (i) we may face challenges of limited
market acceptance and slow adoption of the PS buildings in China’s industrial sector, which
could materially affect our financial condition, operational performance and grow
prospects; (ii) we operate in the highly competitive industrial sector of the PS building
market and failure to compete effectively could harm our business, operating results, and
financial condition; (iii) our financial condition and results are affected by global and local
economic and political conditions that are beyond our control; (iv) a large portion of our
revenue during the Track Record Period was derived from projects awarded by our major
customers and customers in automotive and auto parts industries and our contracts are
typically awarded on a project-by-project basis, which are non-recurring in nature. Any
substantial decrease in projects from our major customers could materially affect our
financial performance; and (v) disruptions or damages to our production facilities may
materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
For details, please refer to the section headed ‘‘Risk Factors’’ in this prospectus.

LISTING AND DELISTING ON THE NEEQ AND PREVIOUS PREPARATIONS FOR
POTENTIAL LISTING
On December 27, 2022, we were listed on the NEEQ by way of public transfer, and the
stock code was 873980. Having taken into account of our business development and
long-term strategic plan, we have carried out the termination of the listing of our shares on
the NEEQ to further expand and consolidate our resource channels and enhance the
financing efficiency. We further consider that, for enhancing our international profile and
accessing the global market with a wider range of international investors, Hong Kong is a
more suitable venue for the listing of the shares of our Group for it serves as a gateway
between the Chinese and international market. In view of this, on November 29, 2024, we
applied for the termination of its listing on the NEEQ with effect from December 10, 2024.
We had also previously submitted an application to the CSRC for the listing on the
Main Board of the Shanghai Stock Exchange on April 28, 2014, and an application for
pre-listing tutoring to the Shanghai Regulatory Bureau of the CSRC in relation to the
proposed listing on the Beijing Stock Exchange on November 7, 2023. For details, please
refer to ‘‘History and Development — Preparations for Potential Listing on The Shanghai
Stock Exchange and The Beijing Stock Exchange’’ in this prospectus.

DIVIDEND
We allow for dividend distributions to shareholders in cash or shares, in accordance
with our articles of association. We do not currently have a formal dividend policy or any
pre-determined dividend distribution ratio. Any final dividend declaration is subject to
shareholder approval before implementation. In making any dividend distribution, our
Board shall also consider various factors, including, among others, retained surplus and
distributable reserves, operating capital requirements, capital expenditure and future
expansion plan, liquidity position, macroeconomic conditions, business cycles, potential
business impacts, and other internal or external factors affecting financial performance.
There is no guarantee that dividends will be presented or announced at any given time.

million to our shareholders, all of which had been paid by October 31, 2025 in cash.

SUMMARY
IMPACT OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted global industries, including the PS building
market, with supply chain interruptions, labor shortages, and production delays. Our
operations in the PRC were minimally impacted due to robust supplier relationships that
ensured a steady supply of materials and the strategic location of our projects in industrial
zones, which were less affected by travel restrictions. In 2022, due to international travel
restrictions, the overseas demand for our industrial environmental equipment declined. As a
result, the revenue from our industrial environmental equipment in 2022 was RMB31.8
million. After the pandemic situation improved in 2023, the revenue of our industrial
environmental equipment business category rebounded to RMB69.4 million. For details,
please refer to ‘‘Business — Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic’’ and ‘‘Financial
Information — Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic’’ in this prospectus.
RECENT DEVELOPMENT
As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had 119 projects on hand, with an aggregate
unrecognized revenue of approximately RMB789.2 million.
In October, we successfully obtained the EU Fire Rating Certificate EN 13501–5. This
certificate is the core certification standard for the external fire performance of building
roofs in the European Union, facilitating our products’ access to the European market.
From October 13 to 15, 2025, we participated in the 9th Member Congress of China
Steel Construction Society (‘‘CSCS’’) and the 2025 China Steel Construction Conference
held in Nanning, Guangxi Province. We were honored with the ‘‘Technological Innovation
Award’’ by CSCS, reflecting the industry’s recognition of our research and development
achievements.
On July 2, 2025, we declared an interim dividend of RMB27.8 million to our
shareholders, all of which had been paid by October 31, 2025 in cash.

SUMMARY
IMPACT OF U.S. TARIFF MEASURES
The United States has in recent years implemented a series of trade measures, including
the imposition and escalation of tariffs under Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act of 1974 and
Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962. In March 2025, the U.S. government
announced an additional 25% tariff on various categories of steel products, followed by
further policy actions in April 2025 and a temporary suspension of certain prior tariff
measures. In May 2025, after their trade meeting in Geneva, the Chinese and the U.S.
government released a joint statement announcing, among others, the removal of the 91%
tariff announced in April 2025 and a 90-day pause, leading the effective tariffs on imports
from China to 30%, down from 145%; and China will reduce tariff imposed on imports
from the U.S. since April 2, 2025 to 10%, down from 125%. In August 2025, the United
States announced to extend the suspension of tariffs on China for another 90 days. In
October 2025, the US authorities announced an escalation of tariff measures against
imports from China. Pursuant to such announcement, an additional 100% tariff will be
imposed on all PRC-origin goods exported to the US with effect from November 1, 2025.
However, a new round of economic and trade consultations was held in Malaysia during
October 25 and 26, 2025 between the U.S. and China. The U.S. and China reached a ‘‘very
substantive framework agreement,’’ under which the U.S. will no longer consider imposing
an additional 100% tariff on Chinese goods. As advised by PRC Legal Advisers, the latest
applicable tariff imposed by U.S. on Chinese imports related to steel products listed in the
Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 primarily include: (i) 20% of general tariff;
and (ii) 50% tariff on the value of the steel and aluminum components in the steel products.
These developments have heightened geopolitical uncertainty and prompted retaliatory
trade measures from other economies, including China, the European Union, Japan and
South Korea. During the Track Record Period, we recorded small portion of revenue from
the U.S., primarily from sales of industrial environmental equipment.
We believe that our future business operations and financial performance are not
expected to be materially and adversely affected, having considered the following: (i) our
direct export to the U.S. market have been limited. For the years ended December 31, 2022,
2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2024 and 2025, our revenue from U.S.
accounted for approximately 1.6%, 3.6%, 4.4%, 4.5% and 2.0% of our total revenue,
respectively. Under our typical sales agreements, transactions are conducted on a FOB
basis, implying that we are able to transfer tariff-related financial risks to customers as they
are usually responsible for arranging transportation and bearing the associated costs; (ii) to
the best knowledge of us, none of our major customers during the Track Record Period
have strong presence in the U.S. nor materially and adversely impacted and to be impacted
by the U.S. tariff measures; (iii) to the best knowledge of our Directors, none of our
material suppliers have been materially and adversely affected by the increased tariff
imposed on steel products; (iv) our PRC Legal Advisers are of the view that our current
business operations in China have not been materially and adversely affected by changes in
U.S. tariff policies; and (v) we have adopted various measures to mitigate the potential U.S.
tariff measures and tackle any such geopolitical risks. For details, please refer to ‘‘Business
— Impact of U.S. Tariff Measures’’ in this prospectus.

GLOSSARY OF TECHNICAL TERMS
This glossary of technical terms contains definitions of certain terms used in this
prospectus in connection with our Group and our business. Some of these may not
correspond to standard industry definitions or usage of these terms.
‘‘Accessories’’ components like doors, windows, and skylights designed to
enhance functionality and efficiency in prefabricated building
‘‘Air Pollution Control’’ systems developed to control industrial emissions, ensuring
or ‘‘APC’’ compliance with environmental standards
‘‘BIPV’’ building-integrated photovoltaic systems, designed to maximize
energy efficiency in new and retrofit building projects,
supporting energy independence through renewable solar power
while maintaining structural integrity and aesthetic appeal
‘‘Curvet Dual-Wave a proprietary series of PS buildings tailored for smart
Arch Warehouse agricultural storage products and services
Series’’
‘‘enclosure systems’’ primarily including roof enclosure systems, wall enclosure
systems and steel deck systems
‘‘Machinery Filtering specialized systems for industrial noise reduction and air
and Acoustic filtration, particularly in turbine applications
Systems’’ or ‘‘MFAS’’
‘‘prefabricated buildings whose components are produced in a factory and
buildings’’ assembled on-site, including prefabricated steel and concrete
structure
‘‘prefabricated concrete a type of prefabricated building that uses concrete as the primary
structures load-bearing material
building(s)’’ or
‘‘PC building(s)’’
‘‘prefabricated steel a type of prefabricated building where steel is the primary
structure building(s)’’ load-bearing material
or ‘‘PS building(s)’’
‘‘primary structure’’ part of the essential framework of a building, providing core
load-bearing support
‘‘secondary structure’’ the structure that connects the primary framework to other
systems, ensuring stability and functionality
‘‘steel deck system’’ structural systems that enhance stability and load distribution in
multi-story applications

China’s industrial sector, which could materially affect our financial condition, operational
performance and grow prospects.
Our business primarily operates in the industrial sector of the PS building market,
which still holds potential for growth. While the penetration rate of the PS buildings in
China remains highest in public buildings, the industrial buildings rank second, offering
room for further development. Comparatively, China’s adoption of PS buildings remains at
an earlier stage compared to major developed countries such as the United States and
Japan. For details, please refer to ‘‘Industry Overview — Analysis of China’s Prefabricated
Steel Structure Building Market — Comparisons of Penetration Rates of Prefabricated
Steel Structure Buildings across Different Countries and Building Types’’ in this prospectus.
However, as China’s industrial sector of the PS buildings market evolves, the extent
and pace of its adoption remain uncertain. If market acceptance falls short of expectations
or progresses more slowly than anticipated, our ability to realize the growth potential may
be limited. Such challenges could impede our long-term growth strategy, adversely
impacting our competitive position, financial condition, operational performance, and
growth prospects.
We operate in the highly competitive industrial sector of the PS building market and failure to
compete effectively could harm our business, operating results, and financial condition.
We operate in the highly competitive industrial sector of the PS building market. Our
competitors may hold advantages through advanced technical capabilities, broad service
offerings, and robust industry experience, positioning them well to capture market share
and respond swiftly to evolving customer expectations. For details, please refer to ‘‘Industry
Overview — Analysis of China’s Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market — Business

Fluctuations in the prices and availability of raw material, particularly steel plate, may
significantly affect our operations.
Steel plate is our primary raw material, essential to our fabrication processes, and its
price is subject to volatility influenced by global and local supply and demand, competitive
pressures, and regulatory policies, many of which are beyond our control. According to the
F&S Report, prices of medium and thick steel plates experienced a significant fluctuation
between 2020 and 2024. In 2021, prices surged by 37.5% to reach RMB5,449.7 per ton,
fueled by strong domestic demand in construction and infrastructure, as well as global
supply chain constraints and raw material shortages. However, as supply chains gradually
recovered and global demand slowed, prices adjusted downward in 2022, 2023, 2024 and the
six months ended June 30, 2025, declining by 13.2%, 10.4%, 13.1% and 0.15%,
respectively. For further details on the historical price trend of steel plates, please refer
to ‘‘Industry Overview — Analysis of China’s Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market
— Key Raw Material Price for Prefabricated Steel Structure Buildings’’ in this prospectus.

production costs considerably. Additionally, potential shortages, delays, or quality issues in
the supply of raw materials could disrupt our production schedules, impacting project
timelines and customer satisfaction.

can we guarantee that future price increases will not lead to substantial, unexpected rises in

RISK FACTORS
Potential mismatch in time between receipt of progress payments from our customers, payment
of project up-front costs, and payments to our suppliers may adversely affect our cash flows.
We may experience net cash outflows due to project up-front costs at the initial stage
of a project. The up-front costs of our projects generally include cost of materials and other
operation costs. Depending on project scale and complexity, these up-front costs usually
represent approximately 15% to 45% of the total contract value of the respective project.
After signing the agreements with customers, we are typically entitled to receiving advance
payment, generating ranging from 20% to 30% of the total contract value of the respective
project. We will commence the procurement of raw materials, contracting with outsourced
product providers and the arrangement of in-house production capacity, incurring up-front
costs. According to the agreement with customers, we are entitled to receive progress
payments upon achievement of certain key milestones as stipulated in the agreements,
which would enable us to start billing at an agreed percentage of the total amount of work
we performed. The advance payments received by us may be insufficient to meet the funding
need of our up-front costs. Consequently, there is usually a gap before we receive the
progress payment per project milestones from our customers. The liquidity needs of our
projects would therefore impose a constraint on the number and/or scale of the projects
which we could undertake concurrently if we solely rely on our operating cash flow to
support our expansion.
Accordingly, our cash flow typically turns from net outflows at the early stage of a
project into accumulative inflows gradually as the project progresses. This results in a cash
flow gap and in the event that we have more projects at the initial stage at any given point of
time, our liquidity may be materially and adversely affected. Furthermore, If we are unable
to secure additional financing or effectively manage the timing of cash flows, our ability to
undertake new projects or expand our operations may be limited.

Our project backlog is subject to fluctuations, modifications, and terminations, and may not be
a reliable indicator of our future results of operations.
Our project backlog represents the aggregate remaining contract value of projects
awarded to us at a specific point in time, based on the contractual terms. The contract value
reflects the expected revenue under the contractual terms, assuming full performance of the
contract. However, as backlog is not a measure defined under generally accepted
accounting principles, it may not accurately predict our future revenue or profitability.
For details on the movements of our project backlog during the Track Record Period and
up to the Latest Practicable Date, please refer to ‘‘Business — Our Projects — Project
Movements’’ in this prospectus.

million. However, this figure assumes that all contracts will be executed as planned. In
practice, backlog value may change due to factors such as project adjustments, cost
variations, and client-initiated terminations. Any modification or termination of one or
more significant contracts could materially and immediately reduce our backlog value,
potentially impacting our revenue recognition and cash flow. Moreover, we cannot
guarantee that the backlog value will be fully realized, recognized within the anticipated
timeframe, or generate the expected profitability. Certain projects may experience
unforeseen delays, scope changes, or cost overruns that could impact margins.
Additionally, economic conditions, regulatory changes, or client financial constraints
may result in deferred or canceled projects, further affecting backlog conversion into
revenue. As a result, our backlog may not reflect our business performance, revenue, or
profitability in future periods.
We are subject to credit risks in relation to contract assets and trade and bills receivables,
which could result in delayed payments and liquidity issues.
Our business model involves credit risk associated with contract assets and trade and
bills receivables. Contract assets represent our right to consideration from customers in
exchange for the provision of services and products transferred to our customers that is not
yet billed. Contract assets are transferred to trade and bills receivables when the rights
become unconditional, typically when we obtained the certification of the completed
construction work from our customers.
As of December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and June 30, 2025, our contract assets amounted
to RMB313.0 million, RMB297.2 million, RMB352.5 million and RMB607.2 million,
respectively. As of December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and June 30, 2025, we recorded provision
for contract assets of RMB18.8 million, RMB17.0 million, RMB21.4 million and RMB30.7
million, respectively. There is no assurance that our customers will settle our progress
payments on time or that we will be able to recover our contract assets in full or at all in the
future.

We may be exposed to liquidity risk due to a long cash conversion cycle.

broader macroeconomic conditions. A long cash conversion cycle may increase our reliance

Tensions in international trade and rising political tension may negatively affect the operations
of our customers and suppliers, thus indirectly adversely impacting our business, financial
condition and results of operations.
Our operations rely on continuous customer demands for PS buildings and stable
supply chain of raw materials. Tensions in international trade and rising political tension,
including imposing trade protection measures, tariff controls, export controls and economic
or trade sanctions, may negatively affect the businesses of our customers and suppliers. For
instance, the United Sates imposed additional tariff of 25% on steel products in March 2025
and further announced a series of measures to strengthen tariffs in April 2025. In response,
impacted economies such as European Union, China, Japan and Korea implemented
retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods and introduced additional trade measures. The United
States then announced a temporary suspension of certain tariffs, creating increased global
uncertainty. In October 2025, the U.S. authorities announced an escalation of tariff
measures against imports from China. However, a new round of economic and trade
consultations was held in Malaysia during October 25 and 26, 2025 between the U.S. and
China. The U.S. and China reached a ‘‘very substantive framework agreement,’’ under
which the U.S. will no longer consider imposing an additional 100% tariff on Chinese
goods. Increased tariffs and intensified trade tensions among major powers may result in
economic instability, market volatility and regulatory changes, which could adversely affect
the business operations of our customers and suppliers. If their operation and production
are negatively impacted, the demand of our products and services and supply of materials
may be indirectly and negatively impacted as well.
During the Track Record Period revenue from the U.S. were primarily derived from
our sales of industrial environmental equipment. The revenue derived from the U.S.
accounted for approximately 1.6%, 3.6%, 4.4%, 4.5% and 2.0% for the years ended
December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2024 and 2025,
respectively. While the amount of revenue directly attributable to the U.S. remained
relatively limited, any future escalation of tariff rates or trade protection measures targeting
Chinese exports, particularly steel-related products, may increase our cost, reduce our price
competitiveness, and affect our profitability. We cannot assure that future developments in
global trade or geopolitical tensions will not materially and adversely affect the demand
from our overseas customers, supply chain continuity, or our international pricing
strategies. Any significant deterioration in the international trade environment may
adversely affect our operations, profitability and prospects. For detailed analysis of U.S.
tariff measures, please refer to ‘‘Business — Impact of U.S. Tariff Measures’’ in this
prospectus.

RISKS RELATING TO DOING BUSINESS IN THE JURISDICTIONS WHERE WE

We may be subject to additional regulatory requirements under new laws and regulations on
overseas offerings and listings issued by PRC government authorities.
On July 6, 2021, the relevant PRC government authorities issued the Opinions on
Strictly Cracking Down Illegal Securities Activities in Accordance with the Law《( 關於依法
從嚴打擊證券違法活動的意見》). These opinions emphasized the need to strengthen the
administration over illegal securities activities and the supervision on overseas listings by
PRC-based companies and proposed to take effective measures, such as promoting the
construction of relevant regulatory systems to deal with the risks and incidents faced by
PRC-based overseas-listed companies. For details, please refer to ‘‘Regulatory Overview —
Laws and Regulations of the PRC — Other Regulations relating to our Business —
Overseas Listing’’ in this prospectus.
On February 24, 2023, the CSRC, the MOF, the National Administration of State
Secrets Protection of China, and the National Archives Administration of China published
the Provisions on Strengthening Confidentiality and Archives Administration of Overseas
Securities Offering and Listing by Domestic Companies 《( 關於加強境內企業境外發行證券
和上市相關保密和檔案管理工作的規定》) (the ‘‘Archives Rules’’), which came into effect on
March 31, 2023. The Archives Rules require that, in relation to the overseas securities
offering and listing activities of domestic enterprises, either in direct or indirect form, such
domestic enterprises, as well as securities companies and securities service institutions
providing relevant securities services, are required to strictly comply with relevant
requirements on confidentiality and archives management, establish a sound
confidentiality and archives system, and take necessary measures to implement their
confidentiality and archives management responsibilities. The interpretation and
implementation of the Archives Rules may keep evolving, failure to comply with which
may materially affect our business, results of operations or financial conditions.

Non-PRC resident individual holders of H Shares whose names appear on the register
of members of H Shares (‘‘Non-PRC Resident Individual Holders’’), are subject to the PRC
individual income tax on dividends received from us. Pursuant to the Circular on Questions
Concerning the Collection of Individual Income Tax Following the Repeal of Guo Shui Fa
[1993] No. 045 (Guo Shui Han [2011] No. 348) (關於國稅發[1993]045號文件廢止後有關個人
所得稅徵管問題的通知（國稅函[2011]348號）) dated June 28, 2011 and issued by the SAT,
the tax rate applicable to dividends paid to Non-PRC Resident Individual Holders of H
Shares varies from 5% to 20% (usually 10%), depending on whether there is any applicable
tax treaty between the PRC and the jurisdiction in which the Non-PRC Resident Individual
Holder of H Shares resides, as well as the tax arrangement between the PRC and Hong
Kong. Non-PRC Resident Individual Holders who reside in jurisdictions that have not
entered into tax treaties with the PRC are subject to a 20.0% withholding tax on dividends
received from us. In addition, under the Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC (中華人民
共和國個人所得稅法) (the ‘‘Individual Income Tax Law’’) and its implementation
regulations, Non-PRC Resident Individual Holders of H Shares are subject to individual
income tax at a rate of 20% on gains realized upon the sale or other disposition of H Shares.
However, pursuant to the Circular Declaring that Individual Income Tax Continues to be
Exempted over Income of Individuals from Transfer of Shares (關於個人轉讓股票所得繼續
暫免徵收個人所得稅的通知) issued by the Ministry of Finance and the SAT on March 30,
1998, gains of individuals derived from the transfer of listed shares of enterprises may be
exempt from individual income tax. As of the Latest Practicable Date, none of the aforesaid
provisions had expressly provided that whether individual income tax shall be levied from
non-mainland the PRC resident individual holders on the transfer of shares in mainland
China resident enterprises listed on overseas stock exchanges. To the best of our knowledge,
the PRC tax authorities have not in practice sought to collect individual income tax on such
gains. If such tax is collected in the future, the value of such individual holders’ investments
in H Shares may be materially and adversely affected.

RISK FACTORS
Under the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the PRC (中華人民共和國企業所得稅法) (the
‘‘EIT Law’’) and its implementation regulations, a non-PRC resident enterprise is generally
subject to enterprise income tax at a rate of 10% with respect to its income sourced from the
PRC, including dividends received from a PRC company and gains derived from the
disposition of equity interests in a PRC company. This rate may be reduced under any
special arrangement or applicable treaty between the PRC and the jurisdiction in which the
non-PRC resident enterprise resides. Pursuant to the Circular on Questions Concerning
Withholding of Enterprise Income Tax for Dividends Distributed by Resident Enterprises
in the PRC to Non-resident Enterprises Holding H-shares of the Enterprises (Guo Shui Han
[2008] No. 897) (關於中國居民企業向境外H股非居民企業股東派發股息代扣繳企業所得稅有
關問題的通知（國稅函[2008]897號）) promulgated by the SAT on November 6, 2008, we
intend to withhold tax at 10% from dividends payable to non-PRC resident enterprise
holders of H Shares (including HKSCC Nominees). Non-PRC resident enterprises that are
entitled to be taxed at a reduced rate under an applicable income tax treaty or arrangement
will be required to apply to the PRC tax authorities for a refund of any amount withheld in
excess of the applicable treaty rate, and payment of such refund will be subject to the PRC
tax authorities’ approval. For details, please refer to ‘‘Regulatory Overview — Laws and
Regulations of the PRC — Other Regulations relating to our Business — Enterprise Income
Tax and Value-added Tax’’ in this prospectus. If any PRC income tax is collected from the
transfer of our H Shares or on dividends paid to the non-PRC resident investors, the value
of your investment in our H Shares may be affected. Furthermore, the Shareholders whose
jurisdictions of residence have tax treaties or arrangements with the PRC may not qualify
for benefits under such tax treaties or arrangements.
We are subject to the currency exchange regulatory system.
The remittance of currency in and out of the PRC is subject to various laws and
regulations. Considerable amount of our revenues and expenses are denominated in
Renminbi, and the net proceeds from the Global Offering and any dividends we pay on our
H Shares will be in Hong Kong dollars. Under the PRC’s existing foreign exchange
regulations, following the completion of the Global Offering, we will be able to make
current account foreign exchange transactions, including paying dividends in foreign
currencies without prior approval from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange
(‘‘SAFE’’). Foreign exchange transactions under our capital account are subject to foreign
exchange controls under relevant regulations and require SAFE’s approval. These
limitations could affect our ability to obtain foreign exchange through offshore financing.
Furthermore, the net proceeds from the Global Offering are expected to be deposited
in currencies other than Renminbi until we obtain necessary approvals from relevant PRC
regulatory authorities to convert these proceeds into onshore Renminbi. If we cannot
convert the net proceeds into onshore Renminbi in a timely manner, our ability to deploy
these proceeds efficiently may be affected as we will not be able to invest these proceeds on
Renminbi denominated assets onshore or deploy them in uses onshore where Renminbi is
required. All of these factors could affect our business, results of operations, financial
condition and prospects.

RISK FACTORS
There exist uncertainties in effecting service of process, enforcing foreign judgments or
bringing original actions against us, our Directors, Supervisors and senior management.
We are a company incorporated under the laws of the PRC, and a substantial majority
of our assets are located in the PRC. In addition, most of our Directors, Supervisors and
senior management reside within the PRC. As a result, the service of process, investigation,
collection of evidence, ratification, and enforcement procedure inside the PRC should
follow the rules set forth in the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China as
well as other applicable laws, regulations and interpretations 《( 中華人民共和國民事訴訟
法》). On July 14, 2006, the Supreme People’s Court of China and Hong Kong entered into
the Arrangement on Reciprocal Recognition and Enforcement of Judgements in Civil and
Commercial Matters by the Courts of the Mainland and of the Hong Kong Special
Administrative Region Pursuant to Choice of Court Agreements between Parties
Concerned (關於內地與香港特別行政區法院相互認可和執行當事人協議管轄的民商事案件
判決的安排) (the ‘‘2006 Arrangement’’). Pursuant to the 2006 Arrangement, a party with
a final judgment rendered by a Hong Kong court requiring payment of money in a civil and
commercial case according to a choice of court agreement in writing may apply for
recognition and enforcement of the judgment in China, and vice versa. However, it is
subject to the parties in the dispute agreeing to enter into a choice of court agreement in
writing under the 2006 Arrangement.
On January 18, 2019, the Supreme People’s Court of China and Hong Kong entered
into the Arrangement on Reciprocal Recognition and Enforcement of Judgments in Civil
and Commercial Matters by the Courts of the Mainland and of the Hong Kong Special
Administrative Region (關於內地與香港特別行政區法院相互認可和執行民商事案件判決的
安排) (the ‘‘2019 Arrangement’’) and the 2019 Arrangement was issued on January 25, 2024
and became effective on January 29, 2024. The 2019 Arrangement has superseded the 2006
Arrangement and afford greater clarity and certainty for reciprocal recognition and
enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. The 2006 Arrangement will
remain applicable to a ‘‘choice of court agreement in writing’’ entered into before the 2019
Arrangement taking effect. However, there remains uncertainties as to the outcome of any
specific applications to recognize and enforce such judgments and arbitral awards in the
PRC.

control of foreign exchange, regulatory regime, government policy on public order and
allocation of resources.
Factors that may adversely affect the Southeast Asia economy, whether directly or
indirectly, include global economic conditions, exchange rate fluctuations and the exchange
control policy of the local banks, a prolonged period of inflation, deflation, economic
stagnation or an increase in regional interest rates, changes in taxation, natural disasters,
including tsunamis, earthquakes, fires, drought and similar events in Southeast Asia or the
region and other regulatory or economic developments in or affecting Southeast Asia.
Moreover, Southeast Asian countries, such as Thailand, may have a wide variety of
local laws and regulations in relation to, among others, restrictions on foreign ownership
and investment, data protection, industrial product standards, product liabilities, exchange
control, and labor. For details, please refer to ‘‘Regulatory Overview — Laws and

adversely affected if we do not respond to the changes in a timely manner or fail to maintain
compliance status.

RISK FACTORS
The trading price of our H Shares may be volatile, which could result in substantial losses to

The trading price of our H Shares may experience significant volatility and fluctuate
widely due to factors beyond our control, including general market conditions in Hong
Kong, mainland China, the United States, and other global markets. Specifically, the
performance and price volatility of other Hong Kong-listed companies operating primarily

Hong Kong, thereby potentially affecting the trading performance of our H Shares.

Shares shortly after the Global Offering. These factors, independent of our actual business
performance, could contribute to substantial price volatility and potential losses for
investors in our H Shares.
The conversion of a significant number of Unlisted Shares into H Shares could adversely
impact the market price of our H shares.

subsequently sold in the public market, the market price of our H Shares and our future
ability to raise equity capital may be adversely affected. Such sales, particularly if

downward pressure on the prevailing market price of our H Shares or lead to

sale of H Shares by these investors or Shareholders, or even the perception that such sales
may occur, could have a material adverse effect on the market price of our H Shares and
increase volatility in trading volumes.

control of our Company, which could otherwise provide Shareholders an opportunity to sell
their shares at a premium. Such actions could negatively affect the market price of our H
Shares and limit the influence of other Shareholders on the Company’s governance and
future direction.

We have applied to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange for, and the Hong Kong Stock

MANAGEMENT PRESENCE
Rule 8.12 of the Hong Kong Listing Rules provides that a listing applicant applying
for a primary listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange must have sufficient management
presence in Hong Kong, and this normally means that at least two of such listing applicant’s
executive directors must be ordinarily resident in Hong Kong. Rule 19A.15 of the Hong
Kong Listing Rules provides that the requirement under Rule 8.12 of the Hong Kong
Listing Rules may be waived by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange at its discretion. It states
that in exercising such discretion, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange will have regard to,
among other considerations, the listing applicant’s arrangements for maintaining regular
communication with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Currently, the head office of the Company and the business operations of the
Company and its major subsidiaries are based, managed and conducted in the PRC and
jurisdictions other than Hong Kong. Most of our Directors reside in the PRC, with Mr.
Chong Hon Wang, one of our independent non-executive Directors residing in Hong Kong.
The Company does not, and for the foreseeable future, will not, have executive Directors
who are ordinarily resident in Hong Kong as required under Rules 8.12 and 19A.15 of the
Hong Kong Listing Rules.
Accordingly, the Company has applied to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange for, and the
Hong Kong Stock Exchange has granted, a waiver from strict compliance with Rules 8.12
and 19A.15 of the Hong Kong Listing Rules based on the following arrangements to
maintain effective communication between the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and the
Company:
(a) we have appointed Ms. Chen and Mr. Ng Tung Ching Raphael (‘‘Mr. Ng’’) as our
authorized representatives pursuant to Rule 3.05 of the Listing Rules. The
authorized representatives will act as our Company’s principal channel of
communication with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The authorized
representatives will be readily contactable by phone, facsimile and email to
promptly deal with enquiries from the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, and will also
be available to meet with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to discuss any matter
within a reasonable period of time upon request of the Hong Kong Stock
Exchange;

OVERVIEW OF CHINA’S PREFABRICATED BUILDING MARKET
Background of Green Building Development and Its Characteristics
Amid growing global environmental challenges, ESG principles have become a key
framework for promoting sustainability, with green building being a primary focus.
Emerging in the 1970s during the global energy crisis, green buildings aim to reduce energy
consumption and environmental impact through innovative design and technology. These
buildings prioritize the efficient use of resources, such as energy, water, and materials, while
minimizing negative environmental impacts. It also prioritizes creating healthy,
comfortable living and working environments for occupants. In the future, green building
is expected to increasingly integrate advanced technologies and emphasize resource
recycling, driving the construction industry toward a more sustainable, low-carbon
future. By the end of 2023, the cumulative green building area in cities and towns across
the country has reached about 11.85 billion square meters, and the cumulative number of
projects that have received the green building label is more than 27,000. Prefabricated steel
structure buildings are an important part of achieving fully green buildings.
Definition and Classification of Prefabricated Buildings and Traditional Buildings
Based on construction methods, buildings can be broadly categorized into two types:
traditional buildings and prefabricated buildings. Traditional buildings are mainly
constructed through on-site construction, relying heavily on manual labor, which results
in longer construction time. In contrast, prefabricated buildings are assembled from
pre-made components produced in a controlled off-site environment and transported to the
site for installation. The penetration rate of prefabricated buildings in the overall
construction sector, in terms of the floor space of buildings completed, increased from
20.0% in 2020 to 29.3% in 2024. This innovative construction method is set to be a key
direction in the transformation of the construction industry.
– 92 –

=== PAGE 103 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Within prefabricated buildings, there are further classifications by different type of
material used: prefabricated steel structures (PS), prefabricated concrete structures (PC),
and other (including wood structures, etc.):
. Prefabricated steel structure (PS) buildings refer to a type of prefabricated
building where steel is the primary load-bearing material. The steel components
are prefabricated in a factory and quickly installed on-site. Key features include
high strength and lightweight characteristics (approximately 30% to 50% lighter
than PC structures), enabling large-span space designs. PS buildings also have a
short construction cycle, easy installation, excellent durability and 100%
recyclable, aligning well with green building principles and thus widely used in
industrial, commercial, public and agricultural buildings.
. Prefabricated concrete structure (PC) buildings are a type of prefabricated
building that uses concrete as the primary load-bearing material. It involves
prefabricating concrete components in a factory and then lifting and connecting
them on-site. The characteristics of PC buildings include excellent fire resistance
and earthquake resilience, making them widely used in residential buildings and
public infrastructure.

Specifically, PS buildings offer significant advantages for industrial facilities compared
to other building types. PS buildings meet load-bearing and large-span requirements, offer
flexible layouts that facilitate equipment arrangement and production flow optimization,
enable rapid construction to meet quick production timeline, and are easy to maintain and
expand, thereby reducing long-term costs. As a result, PS buildings have become the most
economical, time efficient, and environmentally friendly choice for industrial buildings.

Market Size of China’s Prefabricated Buildings
From a market size perspective, China’s prefabricated building market grew from
RMB448.5 billion in 2020 to RMB589.3 billion in 2024, with a CAGR of 7.1%. In future,
with the rollout of national policies and regional government plans targeting prefabricated
building adoption, the market is expected to further expand from RMB509.9 billion in 2025
to RMB707.0 billion in 2029, at a CAGR of 4.6%. Despite the stable growth rate of China’s
construction industry, the proportion of prefabricated buildings in new projects has
consistently risen, driven by government policies, technological advancements, and industry
demand for more efficient and sustainable products and services. The growing adoption of
prefabricated buildings is largely attributed to their advantages, including reduced
construction time, lower labor costs, enhanced material efficiency, and superior
structural quality due to factory-controlled production. Additionally, prefabrication
aligns with China’s sustainability goals by minimizing construction waste and improving
energy efficiency. In comparison to developed markets such as the U.S. and Europe, where
prefabricated buildings have already achieved high penetration rates, China remains in an
early stage of adoption, presenting significant growth potential.
Within the prefabricated building market, prefabricated steel structure buildings (PS
buildings) are increasingly used in factories, warehouses, high-rise office buildings, and
public facilities due to their high strength, lightweight structure, efficiency in construction,
and ability to provide large, open spaces. As new energy and advanced manufacturing
industries rapidly develop, the demand for industrial buildings in China is expected to grow.
Coupled with the residential and commercial building sectors nearing saturation, the
market size of PS building market is expected to further rise from RMB441.3 billion in 2024
to RMB551.5 billion in 2029, and its market share is expected to increase from 74.9% in
2024 to 78.0% in 2029.

Introduction of Prefabricated Steel Structure Building System
Prefabricated steel structure buildings are structures installed on-site from
pre-manufactured steel components. These building systems typically include primary
structure (columns and beams), secondary structure (purlins and bracing), enclosure
systems, and accessories (door and window frames, fans, insulation materials and
environmental protection equipment). The ability of PS building companies to
simultaneously complete prefabricated steel structure building systems including primary
structure, secondary structure, enclosure systems and accessories, requiring the necessary
certifications, qualifications, and overall technical competence. Therefore, companies that
can offer a complete package of services are considered highly competitive in this field.

Industrial Chain of Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market
The industrial chain of China’s prefabricated steel structure building market is divided
into three key segments: upstream, midstream, and downstream. Upstream involves steel
suppliers and traders providing raw materials from iron ore to steel products, such as
medium-thickness steel plates. Midstream focuses on prefabricated steel structure building
projects that handle the design, welding, and installation of steel components, transforming
raw steel into usable structures. Downstream includes the applications of these
prefabricated steel structures in sectors like factories and warehouses, agricultural
facilities, public buildings, high-rise buildings, etc.

Comparisons of Penetration Rates of Prefabricated Steel Structure Buildings across Different
Countries and Building Types
China’s adoption of prefabricated steel structure buildings remains at an earlier stage
compared to major developed countries such as the United States and Japan. In 2024, the
penetration rate of prefabricated steel structure buildings in China, in terms of the floor
space of buildings completed, was 14.7%, compared to around 50% in the United States
and 40% in Japan. With continued policy support and the growth of the labor force, the
penetration rate of prefabricated steel structure buildings in China is expected to rise
steadily in the coming years.
By building type, the public buildings have demonstrated the highest adoption of
prefabricated steel structure buildings, rising from 36.1% in 2020 to 45.3% in 2024, driven
by the lightness, aesthetic appeal, and flexibility in achieving various designs. The industrial
building sector has the second highest penetration rate and was growing with the fastest
growth rate, increasing from 30.9% in 2020 to 35.5% in 2024, due to the relatively shorter
construction period and lower cost compared to other sectors. In contrast, the penetration
rate in the residential and commercial building sectors over the past five years remained
relatively low, with limited growth due to the higher costs by using prefabricated steel
structure buildings in these fields. In the future, the penetration rate of prefabricated steel
structure buildings is expected to increase with the improvement of labor cost, continuous
design optimization and policy support. The industrial building sector is expected to
maintain its leading growth trajectory, from 38.1% in 2025 to 48.5% in 2029.

100% material recyclability, and high degree of industrialization, are becoming the ideal
construction solution for different building categories across multiple key industries. They
mainly include factories, warehouses, agricultural storage, shopping malls and
supermarkets, which are key building types in the manufacturing, warehousing and
logistics, agriculture and commercial sectors.

Business Model of China’s Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market in the Industrial
Sector
The business process of the prefabricated steel structure building market typically
includes design, manufacturing, procurement, assembling and installation, and other
related stages.
– 100 –

=== PAGE 111 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Within this market, companies primarily operate under three business models, each
reflecting a different approach to project execution: (i) The integrated PS building
subcontracting service providers serve as specialized subcontractors for PS buildings,
offering comprehensive capabilities across project design and optimization, manufacturing,
procurement, and installation. Project design and optimization refers to the design of the
main components in a PS building system, including the primary and secondary structures,
etc., as well as the in-depth optimization of PS building subcontracting projects to achieve
better performance at lower costs, for example, by project design and optimization, the
amount of steel used per unit can be reduced while still meeting performance standards,
thereby lowering costs. Manufacturing refers to the production of the PS structure, while
procurement involves the external sourcing of materials required for PS buildings.
Installation usually includes both on-site execution by the company and management
oversight, where the company supervises subcontractors performing the work. In addition,
integrated PS building subcontracting service providers generally have the ability to
simultaneously deliver complete prefabricated steel structure building systems; (ii) general
contractors in the industrial sector of the PS building market do not subcontract PS
building sub-projects to specialized subcontractors but instead directly undertake and
complete the sub-projects through coordinating multiple suppliers. For instance, they may
engage design institutes for structural planning, procure materials directly, as well as
commission external manufacturers; and (iii) traditional construction contractors,
primarily small-scale enterprises, also serve as specialized subcontractors for PS
buildings, but only focus on the manufacturing and processing of PS building components.
These three business models align directly with the three major project types in the PS
building market: integrated PS building subcontracting projects, general contracting
projects, and Traditional construction projects.

The integrated PS building subcontracting projects stand out as the fastest-growing

design optimization that enhances structural efficiency while lowering material costs.
However, due to the limited number of companies with such advanced design capabilities,
the overall market size for integrated PS building subcontracting projects remains smaller
than that of general contracting and other subcontracting projects. From 2020 to 2024, the
integrated PS building subcontracting project grew rapidly from RMB15.9 billion to

project and the 13.5% of traditional construction project. In future, as China’s PS building
market matures and performance requirements become more stringent, the integrated PS

2025 to RMB53.4 billion in 2029, with a CAGR of 14.0%, higher than the 6.5% of general
contracting project and the 9.3% of traditional construction project.

Drivers of China’s Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market in the Industrial Sector
. Requirement for sustainability. ESG considerations and the rise of green building
initiatives are key drivers in promoting the use of prefabricated steel structure
buildings. The Chinese government has introduced several policies to support
green building practices, such as the ‘‘Green Building Action Plan’’ (綠色建築行動
方案), the ‘‘14th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the Construction
Industry’’ 《(「十四五」建築業發展規劃》), the ‘‘Guidelines on Promoting the
Coordinated Development of Intelligent Construction and Construction
Industrialization’’ 《( 關於推動智能建造與建築工業化協同發展的指導意見》) and
so on, drives the adoption of prefabricated steel structure buildings for their
energy efficiency and recyclability. This policy environment creates a favorable
market for prefabricated buildings, as businesses seek compliance with green
standards, labor efficiency, and innovative building solutions.
. Regional development and industrial shift. China’s industrial shift to central and
western regions, guided by policies such as the ‘‘Opinions on Implementing the
Employment-First Strategy to Promote High-Quality and Adequate
Employment’’ 《( 關於實施就業優先戰略促進高質量充分就業的意見》) in 2023,
generates significant demand for modern factory buildings. From an industry
perspective, the ongoing industrial shift to China’s central and western regions in
China is expected to generate substantial new demand for industrial buildings.
Prefabricated steel structure buildings address the need for rapid construction,
cost efficiency, and durability in these regions, supporting large scale industrial
migration and infrastructure development, which will significantly expand the
addressable market for PS buildings. From the Company’s perspective, while its
current customer base is primarily concentrated in East China, this regional focus
does not fully reflect the broader industry demand landscape. As national policy
continues to drive industrial migration inland, the resulting increase in
construction demand will provide favorable conditions for the Company to
expand its business into central and western regions.
. Rise of labor costs. Increasing labor costs and workforce shortages push the
construction industry toward labor-saving solutions. Prefabricated steel structure
buildings minimize on-site labor requirements and reduce construction timelines.
– 103 –

=== PAGE 114 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Their modular nature ensures high precision and quality, mitigating the risks of
delays and errors. This efficiency not only lowers costs but also meets the
industry’s growing need for productivity and reliability.
Development Trends of China’s Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market in the
Industrial Sector
. Increased demand for customization in prefabricated steel structure buildings.
Customers are prioritizing customized designs that balance cost, functionality,
and aesthetics. Enhanced structural layouts, personalized exteriors, and
streamlined manufacturing processes enable faster construction and lower costs,
meeting diverse industrial needs.
. Product and technological innovation. Advances in materials, manufacturing, and
automated assembly are enhancing strength, durability, and efficiency. Digital
modeling and design software enable precise customization, reducing construction
timelines and adapting to evolving industrial applications.
. Overseas market demand. Emerging economies, particularly in Southeast Asia, are
driving demand for cost-effective and efficient building solutions. Chinese
manufacturers are meeting this demand through high-quality exports and
increased global market presence, fueling growth and diversification in the
industry.
Entry Barriers
. Capability of providing integrated system services. In the PS building market,
providing integrated PS building subcontracting services is a significant entry
barrier. Established companies offer comprehensive services, from design to
installation, supported by specialized teams to ensure structural integrity and
meet client needs. The system includes primary and secondary structures, and
enclosure systems, forming a complex whole. For new entrants, building such
capabilities requires significant investment in expertise and partnerships.
. Strict regulatory compliance and qualifications. PS buildings must comply with
strict safety, environmental, and structural regulations, requiring costly expertise
and certifications. Companies need specific licenses and qualifications, often
demanding rigorous technical standards and audits. These pose significant
challenges for new entrants.
– 104 –

=== PAGE 115 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
. Established brand trust and customer relationships. Established companies have
built strong reputations over time, fostering trust with clients in sectors such as
commercial, industrial, and agricultural construction. New entrants face the
challenge of establishing credibility and customer relationships in a market where
trust and reliability are highly valued.
Cost Analysis for Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Projects
Due to the complexity of enterprise-level costs and the diversity of prefabricated steel
structure building contractors — where cost categories can vary significantly, such as some
general contractors excluding design and installation costs — this analysis adopts the
prefabricated steel structure building project perspective to provide a more objective and
accurate reflection of cost composition. From the perspective of prefabricated steel
structure building project costs, the cost structure in China is highly concentrated on
material and installation costs, which accounted for 75.1% and 19.0% of total costs,
respectively, in 2024. This makes material and installation costs are two core factors
impacting profitability. The dominance of material and installation costs are primarily due
to the high unit price of steel, the industry’s high degree of prefabrication, and the
standardized nature of production processes, which reduces the need for additional
customization or on-site adjustments. As a result, labor and other costs are proportionally
much lower, each accounting for a small share of the total cost. In terms of labor cost, the
average annual salary in construction industry has risen from RMB64,243 in 2020 to
RMB78,882 in 2024, with a CAGR of 5.3%. Against the background of an aging
population in China, this trend is expected to continue in the future.

Analysis of Arch Warehouses
In the agricultural supply chain, encompassing production, origin storage warehouses,
logistics, and ultimately end consumers, origin warehouses hold a pivotal position. Located
close to production sites, these warehouses vary significantly in construction and
technology, with many built from traditional brick and mortar that lack advanced
preservation capabilities. This outdated infrastructure leads to high spoilage rates and short
storage times, especially for perishable goods, as temperature and humidity control are
often limited or absent. Consequently, the inability to maintain optimal storage conditions
directly impacts product quality and shelf life, posing a significant pain point that adds to
overall supply chain inefficiency. With the escalating demand for high-quality fresh produce
and the support of relevant policies to solve the problem of the ‘‘first kilometer’’ of
agricultural products leaving the village and entering the city, it has become increasingly
imperative to enhance origin storage facilities with cutting-edge technology and improved
infrastructure.
. Classification of Arch Warehouses. According to the different building structures,
arch warehouses can be categorized into two types: traditional structures and
innovative structures. Traditional structures mainly include simple sheds, brick
and concrete warehouses and wooden warehouses, while innovative structures are
dominated by steel structures, especially prefabricated steel arch warehouses.
– 106 –

=== PAGE 117 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
➢ Traditional Structures: Traditional structures include steel-frame sheds with
plastic film, offering low-cost, easy-to-build solutions for temporary storage
of seasonal produce. Brick-and-concrete warehouses provide good
insulation, ideal for temperature- and humidity-sensitive items like seeds.
Wooden warehouses, with simple and low-cost designs, suit small-scale
storage needs for products with minimal requirements.
➢ Innovative Structures: Prefabricated steel arch warehouses are made of steel
with an arch design, strong, durable, and well-sealed, ideal for long-term and
large-scale storage of grains and other agricultural products.
From a market scale perspective, the agricultural storage market, also named as
the ‘‘first kilometer’’ market, encompasses the initial warehousing segment that
safeguards agricultural products right at their origin. At the macro level, the
nationwide capacity of production-based storage facilities for agricultural
products stands at approximately 307,427 thousand cubic meters, underscoring
significant future development opportunities. The market size has expanded from
approximately RMB200.5 billion in 2020 to RMB237.6 billion in 2024, with a
CAGR of 4.4%. In future, driven by increasing demand for premium-quality fresh
products, the market is projected to reach RMB306.1 billion by 2029, with a
CAGR of 5.2%. Currently, the penetration rate of arch warehouses in the
agricultural storage market is less than 1%. However, owing to their advanced
structural design, enhanced energy efficiency, and superior preservation
capabilities, they are expected to gradually gain market acceptance, with a
penetration rate projected to grow to 3% by 2029.
. Key Values of Prefabricated Steel Arch Warehouses for Agricultural Warehousing
➢ Revenue Side. The optimized design of the prefabricated steel arch
warehouses enhance ventilation, enabling unobstructed air circulation to
ensure a higher quality rate of agricultural products. Their energy efficiency
and anti-condensation technology preserve crop freshness, enhancing
off-season economic benefits and reducing losses.
➢ Cost Side. Prefabricated steel arch warehouse components enable efficient,
7-day installation, significantly reducing construction time and labor costs.
Large space layout is realized through beamless design, with no dead space in
the warehouse, which can maximize space saving and improve the effective
inventory volume ratio.
Market Status Analysis of Prefabricated Steel Structure Building in Southeast Asia
Currently, the penetration rate of PS buildings in the industrial sector in SEA is higher
than in China, particularly in countries like Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia and Thailand.
This is mainly due to the lower land prices and low land utilization rates in Southeast Asia,
where most industrial buildings are low-rise factories, making PS buildings a natural fit.
Additionally, Southeast Asia’s industrial base remains relatively underdeveloped, with a
lower degree of industrialization. However, in recent years, the region has experienced rapid
– 107 –

=== PAGE 118 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
economic and industrial growth, driven by regional economic integration, increasing
demands for modernization, and infrastructure development. The fast construction speed
and flexibility of PS buildings make them ideal for meeting the growing needs of industrial
buildings. Moreover, Southeast Asian governments are placing greater emphasis on green
buildings and sustainable development, introducing various policies to support
environmentally friendly construction. This has encouraged companies to favor PS
buildings, which are efficient, low in labor intensity, and recyclable, aligning with green
policy directions. This trend further strengthens the mainstream position of PS buildings in
the Southeast Asian construction market. Driven by these favorable factors, the PS
buildings market in Southeast Asia is expected to grow at a CAGR of 12.2% from 2025 to
2029, reaching US$2.2 billion by 2029, solidifying its role as a significant part of the
region’s construction industry.
In terms of competitive landscape, the PS building market in Southeast Asia is
currently quite fragmented, with the overall market concentration (concentration rate of
top five players) being less than 2%, even in relatively mature and fast-growing segments
such as Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Thailand. Moreover, local companies lag
significantly behind Chinese firms in design and production capabilities. Amid the wave of
Chinese construction companies ‘‘going global,’’ leading Chinese PS building enterprises are
expected to consolidate their market presence and dominate the region.

Drivers of Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market in Southeast Asia
. Infrastructure and industrial development policies. Governments in Southeast Asia
are promoting infrastructure upgrades and industrialization to drive economic
growth. Enhanced transportation, logistics, and power supply reduce enterprise
costs and boost productivity, encouraging the construction of new facilities.
Prefabricated steel structure buildings, known for fast construction,
cost-effectiveness, and flexibility, align with these modernization goals and
industrial development efforts.
– 108 –

=== PAGE 119 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
. Foreign direct investment and supply chain diversification. Rising FDI and global
supply chain shifts are strengthening Southeast Asia’s manufacturing role, with
USD206 billion in FDI recorded in 2023 across key countries. Prefabricated steel
structure buildings cater to high-growth sectors like electronics, automotive, and
new energy by offering quick, scalable, and resilient solutions, enabling
companies to establish and expand operations efficiently while enhancing
regional industrial growth.
. Resilience to climate conditions. Frequent natural disasters in Southeast Asia drive
demand for durable, disaster-resistant buildings. Prefabricated steel structures
provide superior resistance to seismic forces, wind, and corrosion, reducing risks
and maintenance costs. Their durability makes them a preferred choice for
developers and investors in climate-vulnerable areas, sustaining demand across
the region.
Advantages of Chinese Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Companies Expanding Globally
. Cost advantage. Chinese companies excel in prefabricated steel production due to
their advanced digital and smart manufacturing capabilities. Combined with
China’s relatively low labor costs, these factors result in significant cost
efficiencies, enabling them to offer competitive prices.
. Service advantage. Known for their comprehensive customer service, Chinese
companies offer everything from pre-project consultation to customized design
and responsive post-construction support. By adopting a ‘‘customer-first’’
approach, they ensure timely responses to client needs and efficient project
execution.
. Technology and products advantage. Chinese prefabricated steel structure building
companies boast design capabilities and processing technology that are at a
world-leading level. This advanced expertise allows them to deliver high-quality,
durable, and efficient building services that not only meet but often exceed
international standards.
