REGULATORY OVERVIEW
REGULATORY OVERVIEW — LAWS AND REGULATIONS OF THE PRC
Our business operations are primarily supervised and regulated by the government of
the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘PRC’’). This section summarizes the principal laws
and regulations in the PRC that may have a significant impact on our business.
Regulatory Overview of the Steel Structure Industry
Our principal products involve steel structures, which are an element of the metal
products industry, and the segment in which we operate is the metal structure
manufacturing industry. Meanwhile, our products are widely used in the construction
industry and construction projects, and are therefore regulated by the relevant regulations
in the construction industry.
Metal Structure Manufacturing Industry
The regulatory system of the metal structure manufacturing industry in the PRC
mainly consists of government regulation and industry self-regulation, with the Ministry of
Housing and Urban-Rural Development (‘‘MOHURD’’) and the competent local
administrative departments for construction as the main bodies of government
regulation, and China Construction Metal Building Structure Association and China
Steel Construction Society as the main bodies of industry self-regulation respectively.
The PRC Government implements a relatively strict market access and qualification
approval and accreditation system for enterprises entering the steel structure industry. For
enterprises entering the steel structure industry, the government will examine and approve
the grades of qualification and the scope of business according to their operating results,
capital, technology, equipment and other conditions. At present, the qualifications for
professional contracting of steel structure engineering enterprises in the PRC are classified
into Grade 1, Grade 2 and Grade 3, subject to annual review and dynamic assessment.
China Steel Construction Society has also published the Provisions on the Management of
Qualifications for Steel Structure Manufacturing Enterprises in China《( 中國鋼結構製造業
企業資質管理規定》), which classifies steel structure enterprises into Special Grade, Grade 1,
Grade 2 and Grade 3, and serves as the basis for industry access or declaration of
qualification for general contracting of engineering construction.
The administrative authorities of the industry where we operate are the MOHURD
and the competent local administrative departments for construction, and the main
responsibilities of the MOHURD are as follows: establishing a scientific and normative
system of engineering construction standards; supervising and managing the construction
market and regulating the behavior of all parties involved in the market; formulating and
directing on the implementation of policies and plannings for urban construction; providing
guidance on the construction of urban municipal utilities and safety and emergency
management; and overseeing and managing the quality and safety of construction
engineering.
– 112 –

=== PAGE 123 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
The national self-regulatory organizations of the industry where we operate are China
Construction Metal Building Structure Association and China Steel Construction Society.
Founded in August 1981, China Construction Metal Building Structure Association is a
national, industrial and non-profit social organization formed voluntarily by enterprises in
the industry, as well as relevant universities and colleges, research institutes and individuals.
It is primarily responsible for assisting the government and relevant departments in
formulating and implementing industry development planning; assisting relevant
government departments in organizing and undertaking the compilation of standards;
establishing a system of industry association standards, compiling association standards,
and conducting enterprise credit rating; organizing and implementing industry analysis, and
carrying out industry research.
China Steel Construction Society is a national and industrial social organization
formed voluntarily by enterprises, institutions and individuals related to the steel structure
industry in June 1984. It is primarily responsible for establishing industry self-regulation
mechanism and regulating the industry behavior; investigating market changes and
identifying the problems of the industry existed in the course of development; setting up
the technical standard system of China Steel Construction Society and organizing technical
exchanges and trainings.
Please refer to the paragraph headed ‘‘Laws and Regulations relating to the
Construction Industry’’ herein for information on how we are regulated by regulations
relating to the construction industry.

Construction Law
The Construction Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Construction Law’’) was
adopted on November 1, 1997 by the 28th session of the Standing Committee of the Eighth
National People’s Congress, and was amended for the first time in accordance with the
Decision on the Amendment of the Construction Law of the PRC《( 關於修改〈中華人民共和
國建築法〉的決定》) of the 20th session of the Standing Committee of the Eleventh National
People’s Congress dated April 22, 2011 and amended for the second time in accordance with
the Decision on the Amendment of Eight Laws (including the Construction Law of the
PRC) 《( 關於修改〈中華人民共和國建築法〉等八部法律的決定》) of the 10th session of the
Standing Committee of the Thirteenth National People’s Congress dated April 23, 2019.
Enterprise engaged in construction activities and implementing supervision and
management of construction activities within the territory of the PRC shall comply with
the Construction Law. Our products relating to steel structure building system are applied
in construction activities and construction projects and therefore, we shall comply with the
provisions of the Construction Law.
Regulations on the Administration of Construction Engineering Quality
Pursuant to the Construction Law, stipulations pertinent to construction permit,
examination of the qualifications for construction enterprises, awarding, contracting and
ban on subcontracting of construction projects as well as supervision, safety and quality
management of the construction projects shall be applicable to the construction of other
special construction projects, with details formulated by the State Council. Accordingly, the
State Council has formulated the Regulations on the Administration of Construction
Engineering Quality, which were promulgated by the Decree No. 279 of the State Council of
the People’s Republic of China on January 30, 2000, and amended for the first time in
accordance with the Decision of the State Council on the Amendment of Certain
Administrative Regulations 《( 國務院關於修改部分行政法規的決定》) dated October 7,
2017, and amended for the second time in accordance with the Decision of the State
Council on the Amendment of Certain Administrative Regulations dated April 23, 2019. All
those engaged in the new construction, expansion, reconstruction and other related
activities of construction works and the implementation of supervision and management of
construction engineering quality within the territory of the PRC shall comply with the
Regulations on the Administration of Construction Engineering Quality.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
According to the Regulations on the Administration of Construction Engineering
Quality, the owner, survey entity, design entity, construction entity and engineering
supervisory entity of a construction project shall be responsible for the quality of such
construction project in accordance with the law. If the general contractor subcontracts the
construction project to other entities in accordance with the law, the subcontractors shall be
accountable to the general contractor for the quality of the subcontracted works under the
subcontractor agreement, and the general contractor and the subcontractors shall be jointly
and severally liable for the quality of the subcontracted works. The competent
administrative department for construction under the State Council implements unified
supervision and management of the quality of all construction projects in the country, and
the competent administrative departments for construction under the local people’s
governments at or above the county level implements supervision and management of the
quality of construction projects in the corresponding administrative areas.
Provisions on the Management of Qualifications for Construction Enterprises
According to the provisions under the Construction Law and the Regulations on the
Administration of Construction Engineering Quality, the qualifications for construction
engineering enterprises, survey entities, design entities and engineering supervisory entities
engaged in construction activities are classified into different grades according to their
registered capital, professionals and technicians, technical equipment, performance record
of completed construction projects, etc., and only if they pass qualification examinations
and obtain appropriate qualification certificates can they engage in construction activities
within the scope permitted for the corresponding grades of qualification; a construction
project owner shall award the project contract to entities with corresponding grades of
qualification. In order to regulate the grades of qualification of construction enterprises,
the MOHURD has formulated the Provisions on the Management of Qualifications for
Construction Enterprises, which are applicable to the application for the qualifications for
construction enterprises and the implementation of supervision and management of the
qualifications for construction enterprises within the territory of the PRC.

Enterprises, the competent department for housing and urban-rural development under the
State Council is responsible for the unified supervision and administration of the
qualifications for construction enterprises nationwide. The transport, water resources and
industry and information technology departments under the State Council support the

fine.
Measures for the Administration of Completion, Final Inspection and Acceptance, and

Contracting and Subcontracting
Our operations primarily involve contracting and subcontracting processes as
stipulated in the Construction Law, and the operations of MEGA Construction, a
subsidiary held by us, involve GC (general contracting) process.
Laws and regulations relating to contracting and subcontracting mainly include,
among others, the Construction Law and the Measures for the Administration of
Construction Subcontracting of Building and Municipal Infrastructure Construction
Projects 《( 房屋建築和市政基礎設施工程施工分包管理辦法》). The principal regulatory
requirements for contracting and subcontracting under the Construction Law include
qualification requirements, prohibiting subcontracting entire projects or dividing a project
into parts and subcontracting, etc. and it also clearly stipulates the responsibility methods
for the quality of projects involved in contracting and subcontracting as follows: an entity
contracting to undertake a construction project must hold a legally-obtained certificate of
qualification and undertake the project within the business scope permitted for the
corresponding grade of qualification; a contractor is prohibited from subcontracting the
entire construction project undertaken to others or dividing the entire construction project
into parts and subcontracting those parts to others; a general contractor of a construction
project may subcontract part of the contracted project to a subcontractor with appropriate
qualification, provided, however, it must be approved by the construction project owner,
except for the subcontracting agreed in the general contracting agreement. In case of
general contracting, the construction of the primary structure of a project shall be
completed by the general contractor itself. The general contractor of a construction project
shall be accountable to the construction project owner as agreed in the general contractor
agreement; and the subcontractor(s) shall be accountable to the general contractor as
agreed in the subcontractor agreement.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Article 2.0.23 of the Code for Calculation of Construction Area of Buildings (建築工程
建築面積計算規範) (GB/T50353–2013) issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural
Development (MOHURD) on December 19, 2013, defines ‘‘primary structure’’ as ‘‘the
organic construction that receives, bears, and transfers all upper loads of a construction
project, maintaining the integrity, stability, and safety of the upper structure.’’ In practice,
primary structures primarily include brick-concrete structures, reinforced concrete
structures, and steel structures.
Article 12 of the Measures for the Identification and Handling of Illegal
Subcontracting in Construction Project Contracting 《( 建築工程施工發包與承包違法行為
認定查處管理辦法》) states: ‘‘The following circumstances constitute illegal subcontracting:
(3) When a general contractor subcontracts the construction of the primary structure of a
project within the scope of the general contract to other entities, except for steel structure
projects.’’ Therefore, although steel structures are part of the primary structure, the
regulation explicitly excludes ‘‘steel structure subcontracting’’ from illegal subcontracting.
According to the Qualification Standards for Construction Enterprises《( 建築業企業資
質標準》) issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Rural Development on November 6,
2014, enterprises that have obtained the qualification of general contracting for
construction can subcontract professional projects in accordance with the law. The steel
structure engineering in the primary structure belongs to professional contracting
engineering which is allowed to be subcontracted; Professional contracting projects also
include foundation engineering, earthwork, lifting equipment installation engineering,
environmental protection engineering, special engineering, etc.
The Measures for the Administration of Construction Subcontracting of Building and
Municipal Infrastructure Construction Projects was issued by the MOHURD on February
3, 2004 in accordance with Decree No. 124 of the Ministry of Construction of the People’s
Republic of China, and was amended for the first time in accordance with the Decision of
the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on the Amendment of the
Measures for the Administration of Construction Subcontracting of Building and
Municipal Infrastructure Construction Projects 《( 住房和城鄉建設部關於修改〈房屋建築和
市政基礎設施工程施工分包管理辦法〉的決定》) dated August 27, 2014 (Decree No. 19 of the
Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development) and amended for the second time in
accordance with the Decision of the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on
the Amendment of Certain Departmental Regulations《( 住房和城鄉建設部關於修改部分部
門規章的決定》) dated March 13, 2019 (Decree No. 47 of the Ministry of Housing and
Urban-Rural Development). The Measures for the Administration of Construction
Subcontracting of Building and Municipal Infrastructure Construction Projects sets out
specific norms regulating subcontracting activities and classifies the subcontracting of
building and municipal infrastructure construction projects into specialty subcontracting
and labor subcontracting. Specialty subcontracting refers to the awarding of specialty
works out of projects undertaken by general contractors to other construction enterprises
with corresponding qualifications. Labor subcontracting refers to the awarding of labor
works out of projects undertaken by the general contractor or out of works undertaken by
the specialized contractors to labor subcontractors. A subcontractor shall be accountable to

According to Article 5 of the Provisions on the Management of Qualifications for

Building and Municipal Infrastructure Construction Projects specifies that either of general
contractors or specialty contractors may award their labor works.
The Circular of the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on the
Issuance of the Reform Plan for Construction Engineering Enterprise Qualification
Management System (the ‘‘Reform Circular’’), considered and approved by the State
Council at its executive meeting on November 11, 2020, simplifies the qualification
requirements related to the construction industry, including labor subcontractor
qualification. The Reform Circular was issued by the MOHURD on November 30, 2020,
expressly specifying to merge certain enterprise qualification categories with extremely
narrow divisions, similar scopes of business or less market demand, and consolidate grades
of qualification with too many levels. Construction enterprises applying for labor
subcontractor qualifications are required to make registration only, without going
through the previous examination and approval procedures, with the competent
departments for housing and urban-rural development at the district and municipal level
in the place where the enterprises are registered responsible for the registration procedures.
We have established an appropriate management system for labor subcontractors, and
at present, all major labor subcontractors on the supplier list are qualified in accordance
with the law.
Bidding and Tendering
According to Article 19 of the Construction Law, construction projects shall be
contracted through bidding process in accordance with the law and those not suitable for
bidding can be contracted directly. Accordingly, our engagement in construction-related
business may involve situations where we are required to comply with laws and regulations
relating to bidding and tendering.
According to Article 3 of the Law of the PRC on Bidding and Tendering《( 中華人民共
和國招標投標法》), the following construction projects to be undertaken within the territory
of the PRC, including the surveying, design, construction and supervision of such projects
as well as the procurement of major equipment and materials for such projects, shall be
subject to bid invitation:
(i) projects such as large-scale infrastructure facilities and public utilities involving
the social and public interests and public safety;
(ii) projects that are, wholly or partially, invested with state-owned funds or financed
by the state;
(iii) projects using loans or assistance funds from international organizations or
foreign governments.

According to Article 2 of the Government Procurement Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共

According to Article 26 of the Government Procurement Law of the PRC, government

(i) public bidding;
(ii) invitation to tender;
(iii) competitive negotiation;
(iv) single-source procurement;
(v) request for quotations;
(vi) other procurement methods as determined by the government procurement

(ii) projects using funds from state-owned enterprises and institutions, which hold the
controlling or dominant position.
According to Article 3 of the Provisions on Engineering Projects Subject to Mandatory

foreign governments include:
(i) projects using loans or assistance funds from international organizations such as
the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank;
(ii) projects using loans or assistance funds from foreign governments and their

Laws and Regulations on Production Safety
Our principal business involves manufacturing and construction-related production
activities, and is governed by laws and regulations relating to production safety. The laws,
administrative regulations and departmental rules relating to production safety applicable
to us mainly include the Production Safety Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國安全生產法》),
the Regulations on the Administration of Production Safety of Construction Projects《( 建
設工程安全生產管理條例》), the Regulations on Production Safety Licenses《( 安全生產許可
證條例》) and the Regulations on the Reporting and Investigation of Production Safety
Accidents《( 生產安全事故報告和調查處理條例》).
Production Safety Law
According to the Production Safety Law of the PRC, production enterprises shall
strengthen production safety management, improve production safety conditions, promote
production safety standardization and improve production safety levels. Production and
operation entities which do not meet the production safety conditions prescribed by this law
and other relevant laws, administrative regulations and national or industrial standards
shall not engage in production and operation activities. In order to ensure the rules and
regulations on production safety being observed in the production process, the production
and operation entities shall establish and improve the production safety responsibility
systems and production safety policies specifying, among other things, the responsible
person for each position, the scope of responsibilities, and the evaluation criteria.
Production and operation entities shall provide labor protection equipment and
production safety training for employees. If the primary person in charge of a production
and operation entity fails to perform his or her duties for production safety as required in
the Production Safety Law, he or she would be subject to legal liabilities regarding the
seriousness of production safety accident.

=== PAGE 133 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Regulations on the Administration of Production Safety of Construction Projects
According to the Regulations on the Administration of Production Safety of
Construction Projects, construction project owners, survey entities, design entities,
construction entities, engineering supervision entities and other entities related to the
production safety of construction projects must comply with the provisions under the laws
and regulations on production safety, ensure the safe production of construction projects,
and assume the responsibility for the production safety of construction projects in
accordance with the law. Subcontractors shall obey the general contractors in respect of
production safety management, failing of which the subcontractors shall bear the primary
responsibility for any production safety accident resulted therefrom.
Regulations on Production Safety Licenses
According to the Regulations on Production Safety Licenses, the State applies a
production safety licensing system to enterprises engaged in mining, construction, and the
production of hazardous chemicals, fireworks and crackers, and blasting equipment for
civil use (hereinafter collectively referred to as enterprises). Enterprises may not engage in
production activities without obtaining a production safety license. The production safety
supervision and administration department under the State Council is responsible for the
issuance and management of safety production licenses for centrally-managed non-coal
mining enterprises and enterprises producing hazardous chemicals and fireworks and
crackers. The competent construction departments under the people’s governments of
provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the central government
are responsible for the issuance and management of safety production licenses for
enterprises engaging in construction, and are subject to the guidance and supervision of the
competent construction department under the State Council. Any enterprises in violation of
the provisions of these regulations and carrying out production without obtaining a
production safety license shall be ordered to stop production; the illegal proceeds of such
enterprises will be confiscated and a fine of RMB100,000 to RMB500,000 will be imposed;
and in case that a significant accident or other serious consequence is caused by them, which
constitutes a criminal offense, they shall be prosecuted for criminal responsibility according
to the law.
Regulations on the Reporting and Investigation of Production Safety Accidents
According to the Regulations on the Reporting and Investigation of Production Safety
Accidents, production enterprises shall regulate the reporting and investigation of
production safety accidents, implement a system of accountability for production safety
accidents, and prevent and reduce production safety accidents. Accidents shall be reported
in a timely, accurate and complete manner, and no entity or individual shall delay or omit
the reporting of, or falsely report or hide, any accidents. The people’s governments at or
above the county level shall strictly fulfill their responsibilities by investigating and
managing accidents in a timely and accurate manner in accordance with the provisions of
these regulations.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Regulations relating to Company Establishment and Foreign Investment
Company Establishment
The establishment, operation and management of entities in the PRC are governed by
the Company Law of the People’s Republic of China (the ‘‘Company Law’’), which was
promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (the ‘‘SCNPC’’)
on December 29, 1993 and came into effect on July 1, 1994, and was subsequently amended
on December 25, 1999, August 28, 2004, October 27, 2005, December 28, 2013, October 26,
2018 and December 29, 2023 respectively. Under the Company Law, companies are
classified into limited liability companies and joint stock companies. The Company Law
also applies to foreign-invested limited companies and joint stock companies. According to
the Company Law, where the law on foreign investment provides otherwise, the relevant
provisions shall prevail.
The Company Law is the primary law governing the distribution of dividends by PRC
companies. A PRC company may only pay dividends on its accumulated profits, if any, as
determined in accordance with the PRC accounting principles. In addition, a PRC company
is required to set aside at least 10% of its after-tax profits as determined in accordance with
the PRC accounting principles to a general statutory reserve each year until the
accumulated amount of such reserve reaches 50% of its registered capital. Such reserve
or fund cannot be distributed as dividends. A PRC company is not allowed to distribute any
profits until any losses of previous financial years have been set off. Retained profits from
previous financial years may be distributed together with the distributable profits of the
current financial year. Foreign investors may invest or reinvest in enterprises established in
China with dividends in RMB with the approval of the competent government departments.
Foreign Investment
Since our shareholders include entities registered in Hong Kong, we apply to the
regulations involving Foreign Investment of the PRC, which encourages, regulates and
protects the legitimate rights and interests of foreign investment. At the same time, we shall
fulfill obligations such as information reporting in accordance with relevant regulations.
We strictly adhere to relevant laws and regulations pertaining to foreign investment, and
currently there are no circumstances involving foreign investment that will have a
significant impact on our business.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Although we are a foreign-invested enterprise, currently, none of our business involve
restricted areas of foreign investment. As provided under the Foreign Investment Law of
the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國外商投資法》) (‘‘Foreign Investment Law’’), which was
promulgated by the National People’s Congress on March 15, 2019 and came into effect
on January 1, 2020, foreign investment refers to investment activities directly or indirectly
conducted by one or more natural persons, business entities, or other organizations of a
foreign country within the territory of the PRC, including the following: (1) foreign
Investors establishing foreign-invested enterprises in the PRC alone or collectively with
other investors; (2) foreign Investors acquiring shares, equities, properties or other similar
rights of domestic enterprises within the territory of the PRC; (3) foreign Investors
investing in new projects within the territory of the PRC alone or collectively with other
investors; and (4) foreign Investors investing through other ways prescribed by laws and
regulations or the State Council. The State adopts the management system of
pre-establishment national treatment and negative list for foreign investment. The
pre-establishment national treatment refers to granting to foreign investors and their
investments, in the stage of investment access, the treatment no less favorable than that
granted to domestic investors and their investments; and the negative list refers to special
administrative measures for access of foreign investment in specific fields as stipulated by
the State. The State will grant national treatment to foreign investments outside of the
negative list. The negative list is released by or upon approval of the State Council.
Currently, none of our business involve areas prohibited or restricted for foreign
investment, and complies with the provisions of foreign investment laws and regulations.
According to the Catalogue of Encouraged Industries for Foreign Investment (2022
Version) 《( 鼓勵外商投資產業目錄（2022年版）》) (the ‘‘2022 Catalogue’’), which was
promulgated by the Ministry of Commerce and the NDRC on October 26, 2022 and
came into effect on January 1, 2023, the Special Administrative Measures (Negative List)
for Foreign Investment Access in Pilot Free Trade Zones (2021 Version)《( 自由貿易試驗區
外商投資准入特別管理措施（負面清單（）2021年版）》), which came into effect on January 1,
2022, and the Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment
Access (2024 Version) 《( 外商投資准入特別管理措施（負面清單（）2024年版）》) (the ‘‘2024
Negative List’’), which came into effect on November 1, 2024, industries are classified into
two categories: encouraged industries and industries on the negative list. Industries on the
2024 Negative List were further classified into two sub-categories: restricted industries and
prohibited industries. Foreign investors are not allowed to invest in the prohibited
industries. On December 26, 2019, the State Council promulgated the Regulations on the
Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國外商投資法實
施條例》) (‘‘Regulations on the Implementation of Foreign Investment Law’’), which came into
effect on January 1, 2020. The Regulations on the Implementation of Foreign Investment
Law further explains that the PRC encourages and promotes foreign investment, protects
the legal rights and interests of foreign investors, regulates the management of foreign
investment, continues to improve the foreign investment environment and further expands
opening up. Furthermore, Foreign Investment Law and Regulations on the Implementation
of Foreign Investment Law shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to the investment made in the
PRC by investors from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Macao
Special Administrative Region.

Other Regulations relating to Our Business
Laws and Regulations relating to Special Equipment
Pursuant to the Special Equipment Safety Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國特種設備
安全法》), special equipment refers to boilers, pressure vessels (including gas cylinders),
pressure pipelines, elevators, cranes, passenger cable-ways, large entertainment facilities
and in-plant (in-factory) special motor vehicles that involve great danger to the personal
and property safety, as well as other special equipment applicable to this law according to
relevant laws and administrative regulations. Special equipment producers shall be licensed
by the departments in charge of the supervision and administration of special equipment
safety before engaging in relevant production activities. Special equipment users shall use
special equipment produced with a permit and passing inspection, and such users shall,
before or within 30 days after putting special equipment to use, register the use with the
departments in charge of the supervision and administration of special equipment safety
and obtain a use registration certificate. Special equipment users shall have special
equipment safety management personnel, testing personnel and operating personnel with
corresponding qualifications in accordance with the relevant state provisions. Special
equipment users shall conduct routine maintenance and regular self-check on the special
equipment used by them and also conduct regular checks on and repair the safety
accessories and safety protection devices of the special equipment used by them, and keep
corresponding records.
In addition to the regulations above, according to the Regulations on Safety
Supervision of Special Equipment 《( 特種設備安全監察條例》) issued by the State Council,
special equipment users shall make requests for periodic inspection to the special equipment
inspection and testing institutions as required by the safety technical codes on periodic
inspection.

Laws and Regulations in relation to Environmental Protection
Environmental Protection
Pursuant to the PRC Environmental Protection Law 《( 中華人民共和國環境保護法》),
any entity causing environmental pollution and other public hazards are required to adopt
environmental protection measures in their operations and to establish responsibility
systems for environmental protection. These entities are also required to adopt effective
measures to prevent and control the environmental pollution and hazards caused by the
discharge of exhaust gases, waste water, waste residue, dust, malodorous gases, radioactive
substances, noise, vibration, electromagnetic radiation, and other hazards generated in the
course of production, construction or other activities.
Pursuant to the PRC Environmental Protection Law, which was promulgated by the
SCNPC on December 26, 1989 and amended on April 24, 2014, all enterprises and
institutions which discharge pollutants shall adopt measures to prevent and control
pollution and damage to the environment from exhaust gas, waste water, waste residues,
medical waste, dust, malodorous gases, radioactive substances, noise, vibration, ray
radiation, electromagnetic radiation and other hazards generated in the course of
production, construction or other activities. The relevant authorities are authorized to
impose various types of penalties on the persons or entities in violation of the
environmental regulations, including fines, restriction or suspension of operation,
shut-down, detention of office-in-charge, etc.
According to the PRC Environmental Impact Assessment Law《( 中華人民共和國環境
影響評價法》), promulgated by the SCNPC on October 28, 2002 and amended on July 2,
2016 and December 29, 2018 respectively, the Administrative Regulations on the
Environmental Protection of Construction Project 《( 建設項目環境保護管理條例》),
promulgated by the State Council on November 29, 1998 and amended on July 16, 2017,
and other relevant environmental laws and regulations, enterprises which plan to construct
projects shall provide the assessment reports, assessment form, or registration form on the
environmental impact of such projects to relevant environmental protection administrative
authority for approval or filing. Enterprises planning to construct projects may entrust a
technical entity to conduct environmental impact assessment and compose environmental
impact assessment reports or forms of the construction project. If the enterprise has the
technical capability of environmental impact assessment, it may conduct environmental
impact assessment of its construction project and prepare environmental impact assessment
reports or form by itself. Enterprises shall, after the completion of the construction project
for which the environmental impact assessment reports and assessment form are prepared,
according to standards and procedures prescribed by the environmental protection
administrative department of the State Council, conduct acceptance check of the
constructed supporting environmental protection facilities and prepare the acceptance
check report.

Laws and Regulations in relation to Labor, Social Insurance and Housing Provident Fund

議案件適用法律問題的解釋（二）》) enacted by the Supreme People’s Court on July 31, 2025

Laws and Regulations in relation to Intellectual Property Protection
Patent
According to the PRC Patent Law《( 中華人民共和國專利法》), which was last amended
on October 17, 2020 and came into effect on June 1, 2021, patents in China fall into three
categories: invention, utility model and appearance design. Under the PRC Patent Law
currently in force, the term of patent rights starts from the date of application. Patents
relating to invention are effective for twenty years, and utility model patents and
appearance design patents are effective for ten and fifteen years respectively. The PRC
Patent Law adopts the principle of ‘‘first-to-file’’ system, which provides that where more
than one person files a patent application for the same invention, a patent will be granted to
the person who first files the application.
Trade Secrets
According to the PRC Anti-Unfair Competition Law《( 中華人民共和國反不正當競爭
法》), which was promulgated on September 2, 1993 and last amended on April 23, 2019, the
term ‘‘trade secrets’’ refers to technical and business information that is unknown to the
public, has commercial value and may create business interests or profits, and is maintained
as a secret with relevant security measures taken by its right holders. Trade secret
requirements under the current framework in China is still under development and not
robust.
Under the PRC Anti-Unfair Competition Law, business persons are prohibited from
infringing others’ trade secrets by: (1) acquiring a trade secret from the right holder by
theft, bribery, fraud, coercion, electronic intrusion, or any other illicit means; (2) disclosing,
using, or allowing another person to use a trade secret acquired from the right holder by
any means as specified in the item (1) above; (3) disclosing, using, or allowing another
person to use a trade secret in its possession, in violation of its confidentiality obligation or
the requirements of the right holder for keeping the trade secret confidential; (4) abetting a
person, or tempting, or aiding a person into or in acquiring, disclosing, using, or allowing
another person to use the trade secret of the right holder in violation of its confidentiality
obligation or the requirements of the right holder for keeping the trade secret confidential.
If a third party knows or should have known that an employee or former employee of the
right holder of trade secrets or any other entity or individual conducts any of the illegal acts
listed above, but still accepts, publishes, uses or allows any other to use such secrets, this
practice will be deemed as an infringement of trade secrets.
– 129 –

=== PAGE 140 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
A party whose trade secrets are being infringed may petition for administrative
corrections, and regulatory authorities may stop any illegal activities and fine infringing
parties in the amount of RMB100,000 to RMB1,000,000, and where the circumstance is
serious, the fine will be RMB500,000 to RMB5,000,000. Alternatively, persons whose trade
secrets are being infringed may file lawsuits in a Chinese court for loss and damages
incurred due to the infringement.
According to the Reply of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce of the
PRC on the Issues concerning the Constituent Elements of Trade Secrets《( 國家工商行政管
理局關於商業秘密構成要件問題的答覆》), the measures to protect trade secrets include oral
or written non-disclosure agreements, requiring the employees of, or persons in business
contact with, the right holders of trade secrets to keep trade secrets confidential or other
reasonable measures. Once the right holders have asked others to keep trade secrets
confidential and have adopted reasonable confidentiality measures, the requested persons
bear the responsibility for keeping the trade secrets confidential.
Trademarks
Pursuant to the PRC Trademark Law《( 中華人民共和國商標法》) promulgated by the
SCNPC on August 23, 1982 and last amended on April 23, 2019 and became effective on
November 1, 2019, the period of validity for a registered trademark is ten years,
commencing from the date of approval for registration. If the registrant intends to use
the trademark after the expiration of its registration, a registration renewal application
shall be filed subject to the requirements within twelve months prior to its expiration.
Where the registrant fails to do so, a grace period of six months may be granted. The
validity period for each renewal of registration is ten years commencing from the date
immediately after the expiry of the preceding period of validity for the trademark. In the
absence of a renewal upon expiry, the registered trademark shall be canceled. Industrial and
commercial administrative authorities have the authority to investigate any behavior
infringing the exclusive right under a registered trademark in accordance with the law. In
case of a suspected criminal offense, the case shall be timely referred to a judicial authority
and handled according to the law.
Copyrights
Pursuant to the PRC Copyright Law 《( 中華人民共和國著作權法》), which became
effective on June 1, 1991 and was last amended on November 11, 2020, copyrights include
personal rights such as the right of publication and right of authorship as well as property
rights such as the right of reproduction and right of distribution. Reproducing, distributing,
performing, projecting, broadcasting or compiling a work or disseminating the same to the
public via an information network without permission from the owner of the copyright
therein, unless otherwise provided in the PRC Copyright Law, shall constitute
infringements of copyrights. The infringer shall, according to the circumstances of the
case, assume the responsibility to cease the infringement, take remedial action, and offer an
apology, pay damages, etc.

Domain Names
According to the Administrative Measures for the Internet Domain Names《( 互聯網域

Laws and Regulations in relation to Foreign Exchange
The principal regulations governing foreign exchange transactions in China include the
PRC Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations 《( 中華人民共和國外匯管理條例》)
promulgated by the State Council on January 29, 1996 and came into effect on April 1,
1996, which was then amended on January 14, 1997 and August 5, 2008, and the
Regulations on Foreign Exchange Settlement, Sales, and Payment《( 結匯、售匯及付匯管理
規定》) which were promulgated by the People’s Bank of China on June 20, 1996, and came
into effect on July 1, 1996. Pursuant to these regulations and other PRC rules and
regulations on currency conversion, Renminbi is freely convertible for payments of current
account items such as trade and service-related foreign exchange transactions and dividend
payments, but not freely convertible for capital expenditure items such as direct investment,
loans or investments in securities outside the PRC unless prior approval of the SAFE or its
local counterparts is obtained.
Foreign-invested enterprises are permitted to convert their after-tax dividends into
foreign exchange and to remit such foreign exchange out of their foreign exchange bank
accounts in the PRC. However, foreign exchange transactions involving overseas direct
investment or investment and exchange in securities, derivative products abroad are subject
to registration with the SAFE and approval from or filing with the relevant PRC
government authorities (if necessary).
On March 30, 2015, the SAFE promulgated the Circular Concerning Reform of the
Administrative Approaches to Settlement of Foreign Exchange Capital of Foreign-invested
Enterprises《( 關於改革外商投資企業外匯資本金結匯管理方式的通知》) (which was partially
abolished on December 30, 2019 and partially amended on March 23, 2023, the ‘‘SAFE
Circular 19’’), further expanding the extent of convertibility under direct investment. The
SAFE Circular 19 stipulates that the use of capital funds and exchange settlement funds by
foreign-invested enterprises shall be subject to foreign exchange management regulations,
and implement negative list management.

=== PAGE 142 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
On June 9, 2016, the SAFE promulgated the Circular of the SAFE on the Policies for
Reforming and Standardizing Management of Foreign Exchange Settlement under the
Capital Account 《( 國家外匯管理局關於改革和規範資本項目結匯管理政策的通知》) (which
was partially amended on December 4, 2023, the ‘‘SAFE Circular 16’’). The SAFE Circular
16 unifies the policies of discretional foreign exchange settlement for all the domestic
institutions. The discretional foreign exchange settlement means that the foreign exchange
capital in the capital account which has been confirmed by the relevant policies subject to
the discretional foreign exchange settlement (including foreign exchange capital, foreign
loans and funds remitted from the proceeds from the overseas listing) can be settled at the
banks based on the actual operational needs of the domestic institutions. The proportion of
discretional foreign exchange settlement of the foreign exchange capital is temporarily
determined as 100%. Violations of the SAFE Circular 19 or SAFE Circular 16 could result
in administrative penalties in accordance with the PRC Foreign Exchange Administration
Regulations and relevant provisions.
Furthermore, the SAFE Circular 16 stipulates that the use of foreign exchange incomes
of capital accounts by foreign-invested enterprises shall follow the principles of authenticity
and self-use within the business scope of enterprises. The foreign exchange incomes of
capital accounts and capital in Renminbi obtained by the foreign-invested enterprises from
foreign exchange settlement shall not be used for the following purposes: (i) directly or
indirectly used for the payment beyond the business scope of the enterprises or the payment
prohibited by relevant laws and regulations; (ii) directly or indirectly used for investment in
securities or financial schemes other than bank’s principal guaranteed products unless
otherwise provided by relevant laws and regulations; (iii) used for granting loans to
non-connected enterprises, unless otherwise permitted by its business scope; and (iv) used
for the construction or purchase of real estate that is not for self-use (except for the real
estate enterprises).
In October 2019, the SAFE issued the Circular of SAFE on Further Promoting the
Facilitation of Cross-border Trade and Investment 《( 國家外匯管理局關於進一步促進跨境
貿易投資便利化的通知》) (which was partially amended on December 4, 2023, the ‘‘SAFE
Circular 28’’), pursuant to which foreign-invested enterprises whose approved business
scope does not include equity investments are allowed to use their capital funds obtained
from foreign exchange settlement to make domestic equity investments in China, provided
that such investments do not violate the negative list and the target investment projects are
genuine and in compliance with laws.
According to the Circular of SAFE on Optimizing Foreign Exchange Administration
to Support Foreign-related Business Growth 《( 國家外匯管理局關於優化外匯管理支持涉外
業務發展的通知》) promulgated and effective on April 10, 2020 by the SAFE, the reform of
facilitating the payments of incomes under the capital accounts shall be promoted
nationwide. Enterprises which satisfy the criteria are allowed to use income under the
capital account, such as capital funds, foreign debt and overseas listing, etc., for domestic
payment, without the need to provide proof materials for veracity to the bank beforehand
for each transaction, provided that the use of funds is genuine and in compliance with laws
are and complying with the prevailing administrative provisions on use of income from
capital accounts.

Dividend Distribution
According to the PRC Company Law, Foreign Investment Law and Regulations on the
Implementation of Foreign Investment Law, foreign-invested enterprises in the PRC may
pay dividends only out of their accumulated profits as determined in accordance with PRC
accounting standards and regulations. A company is required to set aside 10% of its
respective profits to its statutory common reserve where it distributes its after-tax profits of
the current year, until the accumulative amount of such reserve reaches more than 50% of
its registered capital. If the company’s statutory common reserve is not enough to make up
for the losses of the previous year, the current year’s profits shall first be used for making
up the losses before the statutory common reserve is drawn as provided in the foregoing
requirement. After the company has drawn statutory common reserve from the after-tax
profits, it may, upon a resolution made by the shareholders’ meeting or general meeting,
draw a discretionary common reserve from the after-tax profits. After the losses have been
made up and common reserves have been drawn by the company, the remaining after-tax
profits shall be distributed to shareholders.
According to the Notice of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on Further
Promoting Trade and Investment Facilitation and Improving Authenticity Review《( 國家外
匯管理局關於進一步推進外匯管理改革完善真實合規性審核的通知》) promulgated by the
SAFE on January 26, 2017, (1) under the principle of genuine transaction, the banks
shall review the board resolutions regarding profit distribution, the original copy of tax
filing records and audited financial statements; and (2) domestic institutions shall hold
income to account for previous years’ losses according to the law before remitting the
profits. Moreover, domestic institutions shall make detailed explanations of sources of
capital for investment and its utilization arrangements, and provide board resolutions,
contracts and other proof of authenticity when proceeding with the registration procedures
in connection with an outbound direct investment.
Regulations in relation to Employee Share Incentive Plan
On February 15, 2012, the SAFE promulgated the Circular of the SAFE on Relevant

incentive plan of an overseas listed company, subject to a few exceptions, are required to
register with the SAFE through a domestic qualified agent, which could be a PRC
subsidiary of such overseas listed company, and complete certain procedures.

Outbound Investment
Pursuant to the Administrative Measures on Outbound Investments《( 境外投資管理辦

Enterprise Income Tax and Value-added Tax
According to the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國企業所得稅
法》) promulgated by the National People’s Congress on March 16, 2007, came into effect on
January 1, 2008 and amended on February 24, 2017 and December 29, 2018, and the
Implementation Regulation of the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和
國企業所得稅法實施條例》) promulgated by the State Council on December 6, 2007, came
into effect on January 1, 2008 and amended on April 23, 2019, other than a few exceptions,
the income tax rate for both domestic enterprises and foreign-invested enterprises is 25%.
Enterprises are classified as either ‘‘resident enterprises’’ or ‘‘non-resident enterprises’’.
Besides enterprises established within the PRC, enterprises established outside China whose
‘‘de facto management bodies’’ are located in the PRC are considered ‘‘resident enterprises’’
and subject to the uniform 25% enterprise income tax rate for their global income. A
non-resident enterprise refers to an enterprise established under foreign law whose ‘‘de facto
management bodies’’ are not within the PRC but which has an establishment or premise in
the PRC, or which does not have an establishment or premise in the PRC but have income
sourced within the PRC. An income tax rate of 10% will normally be applicable to
dividends declared to investors of non-PRC resident enterprises that do not have an
– 134 –

=== PAGE 145 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
establishment or premise in the PRC, or that have such establishment or premise but the
relevant income is not effectively connected with the establishment or premise, to the extent
such dividends are derived from sources within the PRC.
According to the Provisional Regulations on Value-Added Tax of the PRC《( 中華人民
共和國增值稅暫行條例》) (the ‘‘VAT Regulations’’) promulgated by the State Council on
December 13, 1993, came into effect on January 1, 1994 and amended on November 10,
2008, February 6, 2016 and November 19, 2017, respectively, and the Implementation Rules
for the Provisional Regulations on Value-added Tax of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國增值稅暫
行條例實施細則》) promulgated by the Ministry of Finance and came into effect on
December 25, 1993, and amended on December 15, 2008 and October 28, 2011, all
taxpayers in the PRC engaging in the sale of goods, the provision of processing, repair and
replacement services, or import of goods are required to pay value-added tax. Other than
those as specified in the VAT Regulations, the tax rate of 17% shall be levied on general
taxpayers selling or importing various goods; the tax rate of 17% shall be levied on the
taxpayers providing processing, repairing and replacement services; the applicable tax rate
for the export of goods by taxpayers shall be nil, unless otherwise stipulated. According to
the Notice of the Ministry of Finance and the State Administration of Taxation on
Adjusting Value-added Tax Rates 《( 財政部、國家稅務總局關於調整增值稅稅率的通知》)
promulgated on April 4, 2018 and came into effect on May 1, 2018, the reduced rates of
17% and 11% applicable to the taxpayers who have VAT taxable sales activities or
imported goods are adjusted to 16% and 10%, respectively. According to the Notice on
Relevant Policies for Deepening Value Added Tax Reform《( 關於深化增值稅改革有關政策
的公告》) issued on March 20, 2019 and came into effect on April 1, 2019, the value added
tax rate was reduced to 13% and 9%, respectively.
Pursuant to the Arrangement Between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong

Regulations in relation to Real Estates
Pursuant to the Land Administration Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國土地管理法》)
promulgated by the SCNPC on June 25, 1986 and last amended on August 26, 2019, the
PRC applies a system of control over the purposes of use of land, including land for
agriculture, land for construction and unused land. All entities and individuals shall use
land in strict compliance with the purposes of use defined in the overall plans for land
utilization. Registration of the ownership and the right to the use of land shall be governed
by the laws and administrative regulations relating to real estate registration and the legally
registered ownership and right to the use of land shall be protected by law and may not be
infringed upon by any entities and individuals.
Pursuant to Law on the Administration of the Urban Real Estate of the PRC《( 中華人
民共和國城市房地產管理法》) promulgated by the SCNPC on July 5, 1994 and last amended
on August 26, 2019, the PRC practices a system of registration and certification for land use
right and housing ownership. Where a house has been built on the land for real estate
development obtained pursuant to the law, the certificate of land use right shall be
presented for submitting the application for registration to the department of housing
administration under the local people’s government at or above the county level. The
department of housing administration under the local people’s government at or above the
country level shall issue a certificate of housing ownership after verification.
Approval and Filing of Fire Protection Design
The Fire Protection Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國消防法》) (the ‘‘Fire Protection
Law’’) was promulgated on April 29, 1998 and last amended on April 29, 2021. The Fire
Protection Law stipulates that the fire protection design and construction of construction
projects shall comply with the national technical standards for fire protection. The owner,
designer, builder, project supervisor and other entities shall be responsible for the fire
protection design and construction quality of construction projects in accordance with law.
The review and acceptance system for the fire protection design of construction projects is
applicable to construction projects that require the fire protection design in accordance
with the national technical standards for fire protection.
According to the Fire Protection Law and the Interim Provisions on the
Administration of Fire Protection Design Review and Final Inspection of Construction
Projects 《( 建設工程消防設計審查驗收管理暫行規定》) (the ‘‘Interim Provisions on Fire
Protection’’) promulgated by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development of
the PRC on April 1, 2020 and last amended on August 21, 2023, special construction
projects stipulated in the Interim Provisions on Fire Protection shall pass the review of fire
protection design before commencement and pass the fire protection acceptance before use.
Construction projects other than special ones shall file the fire protection acceptance, and

the competent housing and urban-rural development authority shall perform selective
inspection on the fire protection acceptance. A project that fails to pass the selective

Regulations in relation to Leased Properties
Pursuant to the Measures for Administration of Lease of Commodity Properties《( 商
品房屋租賃管理辦法》) (also referred to as the New Lease Measures), which was
promulgated by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on December 1,
2010 and came into effect on February 1, 2011, the parties concerned to a housing leasing
shall go through the housing leasing registration formalities with the competent
construction (real estate) departments within thirty (30) days after the lease contract is
signed. In the event that the parties fail to comply with such registration and filing
requirements, the competent construction (real estate) departments shall order rectification
within a time limit. If the rectification is not made within the time limit, a fine of less than
RMB1,000 shall be imposed for an individual or a fine ranging from RMB1,000 to
RMB10,000 shall be imposed for an entity.
Pursuant to the Civil Code of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國民法典》), which was
promulgated by the National People’s Congress on May 28, 2020 and came into effect in
January 2021, the term of a leasing contract shall not exceed 20 years, and the parties’
failure to proceed with the registration and filing procedures for the lease contract as
required under the laws and administrative regulations does not affect the validity of the
contract.
Overseas Listing
On February 17, 2023, the CSRC promulgated the Trial Administrative Measures for
the Overseas Securities Offering and Listing by Domestic Enterprises《( 境內企業境外發行
證券和上市管理試行辦法》) (the ‘‘Overseas Listing Trial Measures’’) and the 5 relevant
guidelines, which came into effect on March 31, 2023. The Overseas Listing Trial Measures
will comprehensively improve and reform the existing regulatory regime for overseas
offering and listing of PRC domestic enterprises’ securities and regulate both direct and
indirect overseas offering and listing of PRC domestic enterprises’ securities by adopting a
filing-based regulatory regime.
According to the Overseas Listing Trial Measures, a domestic enterprise directly
offering and listing overseas shall file with the CSRC, submit the filing report, legal
opinions and other relevant materials as required under the Overseas Listing Trial
Measures, and state the shareholders’ information and other matters in a truthful, accurate
and complete manner. An issuer seeking initial public offering and listing shall file with the
CSRC within 3 business days after submitting the issuance and listing application
documents overseas. The Overseas Listing Trial Measures also require the issuer to
submit a detailed report to the CSRC on material events, such as change of control, or
voluntary or mandatory delisting of the issuer who has completed the overseas securities
offering. If the issuer fails to complete the filing procedure or conceals any material fact or
falsifies any major content in its filing documents, it may be subject to administrative
– 137 –

=== PAGE 148 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
penalties, such as order to rectify, warnings, fines, and its controlling shareholders, actual
controllers, the person directly in charge and other directly liable persons may also be
subject to administrative penalties, such as warnings and fines.
On the same day, the CSRC also held a press conference for the release of the Overseas
Listing Trial Measures and issued the Notice on Administrative Arrangements for the
Filing of Overseas Offering and Listing by Domestic Enterprises《( 關於境內企業境外發行上

approval from the CSRC in relation to the overseas public offering and listing (including
additional issuance) of shares of joint stock companies, shall continue to conduct overseas
offering and listing within the validity period of the approval. If domestic enterprises do not
complete overseas offering and listing within the validity period of the approval, they shall
fulfill the filing procedure as required.
Full Circulation
According to the Overseas Listing Trial Measures, for a domestic enterprise directly
offering and listing overseas, shareholders of its domestic unlisted shares applying to
convert such shares into overseas listed shares and have them listed and circulated on
overseas stock exchanges shall conform to relevant regulations promulgated by the CSRC,
and authorize the domestic enterprise to file with the CSRC on their behalf. The domestic
unlisted shares shall be collectively registered and deposited with the domestic securities
registration and clearing institution, and the provisions of the overseas place where the
shares are listed shall be applicable to the registration and settlement arrangements for
overseas listed shares.
Pursuant to the Guidelines on Application for ‘‘Full Circulation’’ of Domestic Unlisted
Shares of H-share Companies《( H股公司境內未上市股份申請「全流通」業務指引》) (the ‘‘Full
Circulation Guidelines’’) issued and implemented by the CSRC on November 14, 2019 and
amended on August 10, 2023 and the Overseas Listing Trial Measures, ‘‘full circulation’’
means listing and circulating on the Stock Exchange of the domestic unlisted shares of an
H-share company, including unlisted domestic shares held by domestic shareholders prior
to overseas listing, unlisted domestic shares additionally issued after overseas listing, and
unlisted shares held by foreign shareholders. Domestic joint stock companies that have not
been listed may file with the CSRC for the ‘‘full circulation’’ at the time of their initial
public offering and listing overseas.

The operations of MBS Buildings Co., Ltd., Hopeway (Thai) Co., Ltd., and Union

is an overview of the key legal and regulatory framework applicable to our business
activities in Thailand.

Foreign Business Act
The Foreign Business Act B.E. 2542 (1999) (‘‘FBA’’) is the primary regulation
governing the operation of businesses by foreigners (including foreign entities) in Thailand.
According to the FBA, companies registered in Thailand with 50% or more of their share
capital owned by individuals without Thai nationality or foreign-registered entities are
classified as ‘‘foreigners’’ and are subject to the FBA’s provisions.
Pursuant to Section 4 of the FBA, a ‘‘Foreigner’’ means:
(1) a natural person who is not of Thai nationality;
(2) a juristic person not registered in Thailand;
(3) a juristic person registered in Thailand, being of the following descriptions:
a) being a juristic person at least one half of capital shares of which are held by
persons under (1) or (2) or a juristic person in which investment has been
placed by the persons under (1) or (2) in the amount at least equivalent to one
half of the total capital thereof;
b) being a limited partnership or a registered ordinary partnership the managing
partner or the manager of which is the person under (1);
(4) a juristic person registered in Thailand at least one half of the capital shares of
which are held by persons under (1), (2) or (3) or a juristic person in which
investment has been placed by the persons under (1), (2) or (3) in the amount at
least equivalent to one half of the total capital thereof;
The FBA restricts foreigners from engaging in specific businesses listed under three
categories (Lists) attached to the Act. List 1 includes businesses entirely prohibited for
foreigners. List 2 includes businesses that foreigners may engage in only upon obtaining
permission from Minister of Commerce with the approval of the Council of Ministers. List
3 comprises businesses that foreigners can conduct only after receiving permission from the
Director-General of the Department of Business Development (‘‘DBD’’) and approval from
the Foreign Business Committee, either through a foreign business license or certificate.
One of the restricted activities under List 3 is the service business. Foreigners must
obtain approval from the Director-General of the DBD and the Foreign Business
Committee before conducting such businesses in Thailand.
– 139 –

=== PAGE 150 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Additionally, wholesale and retail businesses are also classified as restricted under List
3. However, there are exceptions:
1. Foreign companies conducting wholesale businesses with a minimum paid-up
registered capital of THB 100 million per store.
2. Foreign companies operating retail businesses with a minimum paid-up registered
capital of THB 100 million for up to five stores.
Foreigners or foreign companies as defined in Section 4 of the FBA that do not meet
these capital requirements must secure approval from the Director-General of the DBD and
the Foreign Business Committee to legally prior to conducting these activities in Thailand.
Law and Regulation Relating to Distribution of Dividend
Distribution of dividend by a limited company registered in Thailand, regardless of
whether to shareholders domiciled in or outside Thailand, is subject to the provisions under
the Civil and Commercial Code of Thailand (‘‘CCC’’). Pursuant to the CCC, if the company
has incurred losses, no dividend may be paid unless such losses have been made good. To
distribute dividends, a resolution passed by the shareholders of the company is required for
their declaration and distribution. However, in situations where the board of directors
anticipates that the company’s financial status would be profitable, the board of directors,
by a majority vote, may declare and distribute an interim dividend to the shareholders
subject to the article of association of the company. In this regard, dividend to be
distributed to shareholders of a limited company must be distributed within one (1) month
from the date of the shareholders’ or Board’s resolution and such dividend must come from
net profits made by such company only. In addition, at each distribution of dividend, the
company must appropriate to a reserve fund of at least 5% of the profits, until the reserved
fund reaches the amount of 10% of the registered capital of the company.
The legal reserve is a mandatory fund that a company must set aside under CCC. The
legal reserve cannot be distributed as dividends to shareholders, as it serves as financial
protection for the company and its creditors. It can only be distributed after the completion
of liquidation.
Dividend payments to shareholders are subject to Thai withholding tax. In Thailand,
dividend payments made to foreign shareholders are generally subject to a withholding tax
at a rate of 10%.
– 140 –

=== PAGE 151 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Personal Data Protection Act
Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019) (‘‘PDPA’’) serves as Thailand’s primary
legislation on personal data protection. It fully came into effect on June 1, 2022.
The PDPA regulates the collection, use, and disclosure (collectively, the ‘‘process’’ or
its derivative) of personal data by data controllers and data processors. A data controller
refers to a person or a juristic person with the authority to make decisions regarding the
processing of personal data. A data processor, on the other hand, is a person or a juristic
person acts on behalf of or under the instructions of a data controller to process personal
data. The PDPA applies to the processing of personal data of all individuals (the ‘‘data
subjects’’) residing in Thailand, regardless of whether the data processing occurs within the
country or abroad. Under the PDPA, data controllers are generally restricted from
collecting, using, or disclosing personal data without obtaining explicit consent from the
data subjects prior to or at the time of personal data collection unless otherwise permitted
by law or any other lawful basis as provided under the PDPA applies (e.g., contract basis).
The PDPA also imposes several obligations on data controllers and data processors,
including notifying the purpose of personal data processing, the applicable lawful basis, and
other matters required by the PDPA, implementing adequate data security measures,
maintaining records of data processing activities, appointing a Data Protection Officer
(where applicable), entering into data process agreement between data controller and data
processor, and notifying authorities and data subject of data breaches. Cross-border data
transfers are permitted only when the recipient country or international organization meets
the PDPA’s data protection standards or if a legal exemption applies.
Transfer Pricing Regulations
Transfer pricing regulations in Thailand, governed by Sections 71 bis and 71 ter of the
Revenue Code, came into effect on January 1, 2019, with supporting guidelines from the
Thai Revenue Department (TRD). These regulations require related-party transactions to
comply with the arm’s length principle, ensuring that the terms reflect those agreed upon by
independent parties under similar conditions. Related parties are defined as entities where
one holds not less than 50% direct or indirect shares in the other or has relation with the
other regarding management, decisions making or controlling that the other cannot operate
its business independently. Companies with annual revenue exceeding THB 200 million
must file a Disclosure Form documenting the relationship and total amount of related party
transactions together with the annual corporate income tax return within 150 days after
from the closing date of accounting period. If requested by the Thai Revenue Department,
taxpayers must also submit additional documentation or evidence to provide the necessary
information (‘‘Transfer Pricing Documentation’’) for the tax authority’s analysis of the
related party transactions within 60 days, with a possible extension up to 120 days or to 180
days for the first-time request. Non-compliance, such as failing to file the disclosure form,
may result in penalties up to THB 200,000, with additional tax liabilities, penalties, or
surcharges if transactions deviate from the arm’s length principle.

=== PAGE 152 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Regulation on Industrial Product Standard
In Thailand, the regulation of industrial product standards is governed by the
Industrial Product Standards Act B.E. 2511 (1968) (‘‘IPS’’) and its subsequent amendments,
administered by the Thai Industrial Standards Institute (‘‘TISI’’) under the Ministry of
Industry. The IPS Act authorizes the TISI to establish and enforce Thailand Industrial
Standards (‘‘TIS’’), which apply to both mandatory and voluntary product standards to
ensure the safety, quality, and performance of industrial products within the country.
Under the IPS Act, there are two types of standards:
1. Mandatory Thailand Industrial Standards: These standards apply to industrial
products that are subject to a Royal Decree issued under the authority of the IPS
Act. Such products must comply with the relevant TIS and obtain a mandatory
TIS mark before they are manufactured, imported, or sold in Thailand.
Manufacturers and importers of these products are required to obtain a license
from TISI prior to the production or importation of these goods. Failure to
comply with the mandatory standards can result in penalties, including fines of up
to THB 2 million, imprisonment for up to two years, or both, depending on the
severity of the violation.
2. Voluntary Thailand Industrial Standards: These standards apply to industrial
products that are not explicitly subject to a Royal Decree. Manufacturers may
voluntarily choose to comply with TIS and apply for a voluntary TIS mark if they
believe their products meet the applicable standards. While compliance with
voluntary standards is not legally required, obtaining a voluntary TIS mark can
enhance a product’s credibility and market competitiveness.
Regulation on Product Liability
The Product Liability Act B.E. 2551 (2008) (‘‘Product Liability Act’’) is designed to
protect consumers’ rights in cases where damages are caused by unsafe products. Under this
Act, various business operators, including manufacturers, hirers, importers, and sellers of
goods (especially when the manufacturer, hirer, or importer cannot be identified), are
considered potentially liable parties (‘‘PLPs’’) for damages resulting from unsafe products.
An ‘‘unsafe product’’ is defined as any product that can cause harm or injury due to a
manufacturing defect, design flaw, or insufficient warnings, instructions, or information
regarding its usage, maintenance, or care.
According to the Act, all PLPs involved with an unsafe product are jointly liable for
any damages caused by that product, regardless of whether the harm was due to their
intentional acts or negligence. To hold the PLPs liable, the injured consumer only needs to
show that they suffered harm from the unsafe product and that they used and maintained
the product as intended. The consumer does not need to identify which specific PLP caused
the damage.
– 142 –

=== PAGE 153 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
However, the Product Liability Act outlines certain exceptions where PLPs are not
liable for damages if they can prove any of the following:
. The product was not unsafe;
. The consumer knew the product was unsafe;
. The consumer misused the product despite clear warnings or instructions.
If the court finds that a consumer was harmed by an unsafe product, it will award
compensation to the consumer.
Regulation of Factory Operation
The Factory Act B.E. 2535 (1992) (‘‘FA’’) governs factory operations in Thailand.
Under this law, a ‘‘factory’’ is defined as a building, location, or vehicle that either: (i) uses
machinery with a combined capacity of 50 horsepower or more (or its equivalent), or (ii)
employs 50 or more workers, regardless of machinery use.
The Act classifies factories into three categories based on operational requirements:
1. Type 1 Factories: No prior notification or permission is required for operation.
2. Type 2 Factories: Operators must notify the relevant authorities before
commencing operations.
3. Type 3 Factories: Operators must secure a license from the relevant authorities
prior to operation.
Non-compliance with these requirements may result in penalties, including fines and/or
imprisonment, depending on the type of factory and the nature of the violation.
In addition to the notification requirements for Type 2 factories and the licensing
requirements for Type 3 factories under FA, factory operators are also obligated to comply
with regulations issued by the Ministry of Industry or the Department of Industrial Works.
These regulations, established under the authority of the Factory Act, are designed to
regulate and oversee various aspects of factory operations.
The specific requirements vary based on the industry type and factory size. They may
include provisions related to the location and surrounding environment of the factory, the
types or specifications of machinery used, the qualifications of personnel or workers
employed, and standards and methods for waste management, among other factors.
Failure to comply with these requirements or regulations can result in penalties, such
as fines, being imposed on the factory operator.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Law and Regulation Relating to the Foreign Exchange
Thai foreign exchange controls are managed by the Bank of Thailand (‘‘BOT’’) on
behalf of the Ministry of Finance under the Exchange Control Act B.E. 2485 (1942) (the
‘‘ECA’’), as amended and relevant rules (‘‘Exchange Control Regulations’’). The BOT has
authorized commercial banks and certain entities to act as agents for foreign exchange
transactions. Since 1998, the Bank has implemented measures to limit specific foreign
exchange transactions involving the Baht currency by domestic financial institutions and
non-residents, aiming to prevent instability and speculation in the currency market.
Exceptions may be granted based on specific financial circumstances.
When person receives foreign currency from abroad, such as payments for goods or
services, or loans exceeding USD1 million or its equivalent, they must bring the foreign
currency into the country immediately, within 360 days from the date of export or the
transaction date. Additionally, the foreign currency must be sold or deposited with a
commercial bank in Thailand within 360 days from the date of receipt or import. If the
foreign currency received from abroad is intended to settle or offset expenses overseas, it
can be used directly for those purposes without being brought into Thailand.
For outward remittances from Thailand, such as (i) dividends after applicable tax
payments, (ii) interest on loans from overseas, and (iii) principal payments on such loans,
authorized agents must be informed and supporting documents such as a resolution of the
board of directors’ meeting and/or the shareholders’ approving the dividend payment, list
of shareholders, etc. for outward remittances of dividends, may be required by the
authorized agents for verification before remittance to overseas. The remitted amount must
be adhere to the specific amounts outlined in the relevant documents.
Law and Regulation Relating to Employment and Labour Law:
The primary laws governing employment and labor in Thailand include Sections 575 to
586 of the Civil and Commercial Code (CCC), the Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998)
(LPA), the Labour Relations Act B.E. 2518 (1975) (LRA), the Social Security Act B.E. 2533
(1990) (SSA), and the Workmen’s Compensation Act B.E. 2537 (1994) (WCA), along with
their amendments.
The CCC and LPA serve as the main legal frameworks aimed at protecting employees’
working conditions and regulating employment terms and employment agencies. Notably,
under these laws, an employment contract is not required to be in written form.
The LPA further establishes that employees are entitled to certain rights, including a
notice period before termination, leave entitlements, severance payments, and holidays.
The SSA and WCA are designed to provide compensation for employees injured during
the course of their work. Employers are mandated to contribute to both the Social Security
Fund and the Workmen’s Compensation Fund to mitigate the financial risks associated
with workplace injuries. Failure to comply with these obligations constitutes a criminal
offense, subjecting the employer to potential fines, imprisonment, or both.
