HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT
OVERVIEW
We are an integrated prefabricated steel structure building (‘‘PS building’’)
subcontracting service provider in the industrial sector of PS building market. We offer
integrated services for construction projects across industries, covering project design and
optimization, procurement, manufacturing and installation. We are primarily engaged in
the construction of PS buildings in the PRC, and to a lesser extent, overseas. By leveraging
our technology and expertise, we have built a reputation in China’s industrial sector of the
PS building market. According to the F&S Report, we ranked third in China’s industrial
sector of the PS building market in terms of revenue in 2024, representing a 3.5% market
share; and the top two players capturing a market share of 35.8% and 6.5%, respectively.
Our history can be traced back to April of 1999, the time when our Company was
established under the name of ‘‘United Steel Buildings (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.’’, being a
limited liability company under the corporate category of sole proprietorship in China by
our founders, Mr. Chen and Ms. Chen, through C&M Global, Inc. (‘‘C&M Global’’). On
July 7, 2000, our Company changed its name to ‘‘United Metal Building System (Shanghai)
Co., Ltd.’’. It was converted into a joint stock limited liability company on April 12, 2012
and was renamed as ‘‘USAS Building System (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.’’.

DETAILS OF PRE-IPO INVESTMENTS
Overview
(a) Transfer of Equity Interests to Sunny International (the ‘‘2007 Transfer’’)
Asia Investments ARM (AIA) S.A. (‘‘Asia Investments’’) first acquired 20% indirect
interest in our Company on November 29, 2007 from Mr. Chen for a consideration of
RMB30 million which was determined with reference to based on the arm’s length
commercial negotiation between Mr. Chen and Asia Investments with reference to the
valuation of our Company and fully settled on November 29, 2007. Asia Investments then
subsequently sold 2% indirect interest in our Company back to Mr. Chen on September 20,
2010 for a consideration of RMB4.1 million, which was determined based on the arm’s
length commercial negotiation between Mr. Chen and Asia Investments and fully settled on
September 20, 2010, which resulted in Asia Investments’ indirect interest in our Company to
18%.
On March 2, 2011, Asia Investments agreed to transfer its 18% indirect interest in our
Company at a consideration of US$2.45 million in exchange for its wholly-owned
subsidiary, Sunny International, acquiring a direct 18% equity interest in our Company
at the same consideration. The consideration was determined after arm’s length
negotiations between the parties and was fully settled on May 4, 2011. Immediately after
the above transactions, 18% equity interests in our Company were held by Asia Investments
through Sunny International.

PRINCIPAL TERMS OF THE PRE-IPO INVESTMENTS
Use of proceeds from We intend to use all of the proceeds from the Pre-IPO Investors
the Pre-IPO involved in the 2007 Transfer, the 2011 Capital Contributions,
Investments the 2020 First Capital Injection, the 2020 Second Capital
Injection for business development and operation as well as
general working capital. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we
have fully utilized all of the proceeds from the Pre-IPO
Investments.
As the funds from the Pre-IPO Investors involved in the 2017
Equity Transfers, the 2022 First Equity Transfers and the 2022
Second Equity Transfer, the 2023 Equity Transfer and the 2024
Equity Transfer are only the consideration for the equity
transfers between the relevant investors, they are not intended
to be used as the proceeds from the Pre-IPO Investments of our
Company.
Strategic benefits Our Company believes that it can benefit from the Pre-IPO
brought to our Investors’ industry insight, knowledge and experience as well as
Company by the the additional funding provided by them. We have secured the
Pre-IPO Investors capital required for business development and expansion. In
addition, their investments demonstrate their confidence in the
business of our Group and their recognition of our performance
and prospects.
Basis of determining the The consideration for each round of Pre-IPO Investments was
consideration determined by the parties at arm’s length through commercial
negotiations.
Lock-up period Pursuant to the applicable PRC laws, all the Shares issued by our
Company prior to the Global Offering (including the Shares held
by Pre-IPO Investors) are subject to transfer restrictions for a
period of one year from the Listing Date.

Shanghai Stock Exchange Listing Application
We submitted a public application to the CSRC for the listing on the Main Board of
the Shanghai Stock Exchange on April 28, 2014 (the ‘‘Shanghai Stock Exchange Listing
Application’’). We had updated our prospectus on February 25, 2016 and responded to all
enquiries from the CSRC. In May 2017, upon CSRC’s review, our application for listing on
Shanghai Stock Exchange Listing was not approved by the CSRC on the ground that we did
not disclose sufficient material information for investors to make assessment and
investment decisions, and therefore failed to meet the requirement under Article 41 of the
Administrative Measures for Initial Public Offering and Listing of Stocks that was in effect
at that time.
We received the ‘‘Decision on Not Approving the Initial Public Offering Application of
USAS Building System (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. 《( 關於不予核准美聯鋼結構系統（上海）股份有
限公司首次公開發行股票申請決定》) in May 2017 (the ‘‘Decision’’). We did not file any
appeal with or submit further response to the CSRC regarding the Decision. Therefore, our
application process relating to the Shanghai Stock Exchange Listing Application was
considered concluded, and it was neither ‘‘terminated’’ nor considered ‘‘lapsed’’.
Based on the Decision issued by the CSRC, the major comments were (i) significant
fluctuations in our operating revenue during the reporting period, which were inconsistent
with industry trends; (ii) volatility in gross profit margins, with significant variations among
projects and periods where gross profit margins were substantially higher than the industry
average; (iii) a continuous decline in employee numbers and a rising proportion from
outsourced processing, with outsourcing production volume accounting for over 50% of
total production volume in 2016; and (iv) a 33.4% year-on-year increase in revenue in 2016,
while administrative expenses and distribution and selling expenses decreased on
year-on-year basis by 7.9% and 0.4%, respectively, indicating a lack of synchronization
between operating expenses and revenue growth.

HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT
In relation to the Decision, our Directors are of the view that the Decision is no longer
applicable or relevant to the Listing, or render our Company not suitable for the Listing.
Over the past decade, our Group has undergone substantial development. This includes (i) a
significant expansion in business scale in terms of revenue and size of operation, (ii) a more
diversified business structure, evolving from solely PS building subcontracting services
during the three years ended December 31, 2014, 2015 and 2016 (the ‘‘Reporting Period’’) to
a broader portfolio encompassing PS building subcontracting services, general contracting
services, and industrial environmental equipment during the Track Record Period, and (iii)
an enhancement of our geographical footprint and customer base. For further details,
please refer to ‘‘Business’’ in this Prospectus. In light of these developments, our Directors
believe that the historical financial information of our Group presented during the
Reporting Period was less indicative of, and not directly comparable to, our current
financial performance. In addition, our Directors have taken into consideration the
following:
(i) Our revenue fluctuations
For the Reporting Period, we recorded fluctuations in revenue performance,
which were not completely consistent with the peers’ trend.
In 2014, we recorded operating revenue of RMB903.5 million, representing a
year-on-year growth of 40.6%, which was higher than the peers average of –8.0%
(based on their revenue from light steel structure business). In 2014, we capitalized on
the business opportunities arising from the growth of e-commerce, which boosted the
market demand for steel structure buildings in warehouse and logistics facilities. In
addition, in 2014, we adopted a business strategy of taking up more projects with low
profit margin in order to secure a higher volume of projects and expand our revenue.
In 2015, we recorded operating revenue of RMB567.2 million, representing a
year-on-year growth of –37.2%, which was lower than the peers average of –15.6%
(based on their revenue from light steel structure business). In 2015, in response to the
slowdown in macroeconomic growth, and with a view to mitigating operational risks,
we proactively adopted a business strategy to tighten the client selection criteria and to
refrain from taking on projects with lower margin or longer payment cycles.
In 2016, we recorded operating revenue of RMB768.0 million, representing a
year-on-year growth of 35.4%. This included a revenue of RMB316.1 million for the
first half of 2016, a growth of 20.0% from the same period in 2015 and outperformed
the average of its peers, which stood at –10.8% (based on their revenue from light steel
structure business). The aforesaid peer comparison was based on the data for the first
half of 2016, as it was the latest available data at that time). Such performance was
primarily driven by the gradual stabilization in macroeconomic condition, increased
steel structure investments form our clients and the rising price of raw materials.
– 167 –

=== PAGE 178 ===
HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT
In addition to the aforesaid factors that caused our revenue fluctuations to differ
from those of our peers, we specialized in PS building subcontracting services, with
light steel structures constituting the sole core business during the Shanghai Stock
Exchange Listing Application. By contrast, at the time of the Shanghai Stock
Exchange Listing Application, the peer companies for comparison were those entities
based in the PRC and listed on either Shanghai or Shenzhen Stock Exchange. These
companies were engaged in a diverse range of steel structure and related construction
and civil engineering businesses, including manufacturing and sale of a wide variety of
heavy and light steel structures, high-rise steel structures (高層鋼結構), large-span
spatial steel structures (空間大跨度鋼結構), construction heavy steel structures (建築重
鋼結構), bridge steel structures (橋樑鋼結構), residential steel structures (住宅鋼結構)
as well as other kinds of construction or related materials. They also held
qualifications to undertake subcontracting services for steel structure work and
general contracting or subcontracting services for construction and civil engineering
related work. Their light steel structure business represented only one part of their
operations, and did not account for a relatively high proportion of their overall
business.
Therefore, while the revenue fluctuations of the peers may provide some reference
value, we are not absolutely comparable to the peers. Our strategic focus on light steel
structure business and the specific strategic adjustments may also lead to differences in
revenue growth rate under this segment compared with the peers during the Reporting
Period.
According to F&S, the PS building market is characterised by significant
variations among enterprises in terms of project types, customer structures, and
business cycles. While companies operate within the same market, their performance
can be influenced by a wide range of factors such as segment composition, overall
competitiveness, project acquisition, project structures, execution schedules, client
demand, and construction progress. Further, each entity may pursue its distinct
development strategies and adopt different responses to the changing macroeconomic
conditions. As a result, overall market growth does not necessarily imply that all
participants benefited equally or experienced growth at a similar pace, or at all.
Considering these dynamics, together with the long project cycles and phased revenue
recognition that are typical in the construction industry, fluctuations in the annual
performance among the industry participants are common. The fact that our Company
delivered better performance in the first half of 2016 underscores the differences among
enterprises in this industry with respect to the factors set forth above. According to
F&S, such variations are consistent with the characteristics and cyclical patterns of the
PS building industry and are considered reasonable.

and 10.8% of total revenue for the first half of 2025, respectively, whereas in

Further, our revenue recognition primarily follows the input method and is
recognized over time, if one project starts in the first quarter, we are expected to
recognize most of the revenue within the same year. Conversely, the project initiated in
the fourth quarter often result in revenue recognition split between the current and
following year. Therefore, the annual fluctuation in revenue normally reflects our
project-based nature, and our revenue, and hence our financial performance, may vary
significantly across different periods based on the different contract sum and progress
of our projects.

Although we recorded revenue fluctuation in the recent years, the market size of
prefabricated steel structure buildings in the industrial sector grew from RMB191.5

(ii) Our gross profit margin fluctuations
During the Reporting Period, we recorded gross profit margin of 15.0%, 21.2%
and 15.1% in 2014, 2015 and 2016, respectively. The fluctuation was mainly
attributable to the combined effect of (i) the business strategy adjustment made by
us. Contrasted to 2014 during which we adopted the business strategy of taking up a
greater number of projects of lower profit margin to increase project volume and drive
revenue growth, in order to achieve business expansion, in 2015, we became more
conservative in project selection and refrained from taking on projects with lower
margins in response to the slowdown in macroeconomic growth, and with a view to
mitigating operational risks. Therefore, the gross profit margin in 2015 increased
accordingly; and (ii) the price fluctuation of raw materials, which was the main
component of our cost of sales. Throughout the Reporting Period, our gross profit
margin generally reflected the prevailing price trends of steel plates. During the
Reporting Period, the price of medium and thick steel plates in China was
approximately RMB3,221/ton, RMB2,368/ton and RMB2,722/ton respectively.
Regarding fluctuation in gross margins across projects, according to F&S, a
certain degree of variance in gross margins between projects is a normal industry
characteristic. PS building subcontracting service projects are custom-designed based
on building functionalities and client’s requirements. Differences in process
requirements, load-bearing capacity, project scale, design complexity, and whether
installation or additional services are included can lead to variations in project costs,
thereby resulting in differences in gross margins across projects.
Compared with the Reporting Period, our overall gross profit margin for the
Track Record Period, which amounted to 12.7%, 14.8%, 12.5% and 10.2%,
respectively, was relatively stable. For detailed discussions on the movements of our
gross profit margin for the Track Record Period, please refer to ‘‘Financial
Information — Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin’’ and ‘‘Financial Information
— Period to Period Comparison of Results of Operations’’ in this prospectus.

(iii) Our employee and outsourcing
Employees
During the Reporting Period, we experienced a persistent decline in our
number of employees, which was 418, 355 and 333 as of December 31, 2014, 2015
and 2016, respectively, primarily attributable to the reduced demand for
workforce due to the enhanced and improved production and management
efficiency resulting from our investments of several million of new fixed assets
such as numerical control cutting machine and ongoing upgrades to our
information technology software systems, including integrate Bill of Materials
System with logistics management, helpful to reduce the number of production
and warehouse logistics employees. In addition, the number of employees
decreased significantly from 2014 to 2015, which was generally in line with the
decrease in our revenue in 2015. In 2016, we further enhanced the internal
management structure to improve efficiency by reducing the number of
management employees. Therefore, the changes in the number of employees
during the Reporting Period were generally aligned with our development and
enhancement of our operational efficiency.
During the Track Record Period, the number of our employees increased
steadily, with 536, 559, 639 and 692 employees as of December 31, 2022, 2023 and
2024, and June 30, 2025, respectively. The increase in employee numbers
compared to the Reporting Period was primarily driven by our continuous
expansion of business, particularly in the general contracting and industrial
environment equipment. Additionally, in 2024, we established a new sales
– 171 –

=== PAGE 182 ===
HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT
department to facilitate overseas market expansion. Therefore, the changes in the
number of employees during the Track Record Period were aligned with our
business expansion.
Outsourced production
During the Reporting Period, the outsourcing ratio (outsourced production
volume over total production volume) was approximately 38.0%, 43.1% and
50.7% in 2014, 2015 and 2016, respectively. The increase was primarily driven by
the geographical constraints of our several large-scale projects in 2015 and 2016
that were located remotely from our production facilities.
During the Track Record Period, the outsourcing ratio was approximately
54.5%, 60.5%, 56.9% and 67.5%, respectively. The relatively higher ratio in 2023
was primarily attributable to the fact that several major projects were located far
from our production facilities (for example, in Guangxi and Heilongjiang
Provinces). Given our relatively high in-house production capacity, we
strategically prioritized manufacturing higher-value-added components or those
for projects in suitable locations. As a result, we opted to engage local
subcontractors near the respective project sites to complete the production.
Thus, as it can be seen above, whether our Group chooses to outsource is
primarily based on the transportation costs of the primary structure components,
project location, production schedule, etc. The number of employees has no
significant direct relationship with our outsourcing decision.
According to F&S, it is a common industry practice for PS building service
providers to outsource certain materials processing. Relatively high percentage of
our production during the Track Record Period was outsourced mainly due to: (i)
limited in-house production capacity, with the utilization rate for PS building
components of 128.3%, 88.1%, 101.7% and 158.7%, respectively, during the same
periods; (ii) the greater importance of design and on-site construction supervision
for these primary structure components over the standardized production of such
components because precise and detailed design drawings and on-site supervision
and management can ensure high-quality and efficient completion; and (iii)
typical high transportation costs of the bulky and heavy primary structure
components. Therefore, leveraging on outsourcing, we, based on location,
customers’ specifications, and overall internal production scheduling, are able
to focus our resources on higher value-added stages, such as project design
refinement. For details, please refer to ‘‘Business — Suppliers — Outsourced
Product Providers’’ in this prospectus.
According to F&S, outsourcing ratio in PS building subcontracting services
industry varies significantly driven by substantial differences in production
capacity allocation across companies’ in-house production lines, typically ranging
between 30% to 70%. Our outsourcing ratio falls within the industry range.

concerted action party before the change, resulting in our Company’s

handling handover matters, during which he failed to identify the
information disclosure obligation and handed over this matter to the
senior management in a timely manner, resulting in the omission of such
matter being brought to the attention of the then Board for its review
and approval at the material time.
This incident was discovered by our Company during the auditing
process and during the review of our internal control in 2023 by our
Company and our professional parties. On the advice of the PRC Legal
Advisers, the then Board subsequently held a board meeting on April 28,
2024 ratifying the provision of such guarantee and issued an
announcement on the NEEQ concerning this matter on April 30,
2024. As of the date of its announcement on April 30, 2024, the loan
facility had been fully repaid and the guarantee had been fully
discharged. Despite the delay, the matter was sufficiently disclosed in
the announcement on the NEEQ pursuant to its disclosure
requirements, and the NEEQ did not impose any regulatory measures
or disciplinary action concerning this incident.

HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT
Our Company has, since the occurrence of the above-mentioned
incidents, adopted the following measures to prevent similar incidents
of non-compliance from occurring from the PRC legal compliance
perspective:
(1) our Company engaged Grandway Law Offices as its PRC Legal
Advisers and upon its advice arranged for an announcement to be
made and published on NEEQ as soon as practicable in order to
comply with its disclosure obligations under the requirements of
the NEEQ.
(2) our Company has actively revised its relevant internal systems such
as the ‘‘Information Disclosure Management System’’ based on the
opinions of its PRC Legal Advisors, in order to ensure that (i) a
sufficient mechanism is in place to ensure that transactions
requiring board approval would be sought prior to their
execution and (ii) matters or information required to be disclosed
to the investors are identified and disclosed in time pursuant to the
relevant laws and regulations;
(3) our Company has established a team led by its Board office,
including the secretary to the Board and the assistant secretary to
the Board as assisted by our Company’s finance and administrative
personnel to identify such disclosure obligations and matters
requiring for Board approval, instead of relying on any single
person to identify such matters; and
(4) our Company has since the above incidents provided regular
training to the responsible staff handling corporate governance and
internal control matters, with a view to increasing their awareness
of the relevant laws and regulations under the instructions of its
PRC Legal Advisers. Our Company communicates with its PRC
Legal Advisers on a timely basis and the training is organized on a
monthly to bimonthly basis as required.
In relation to the internal control measures that our Company has

disclosure obligations after the Listing;

FREE FLOAT
Rule 19A.13C of the Listing Rules provides that, where a new applicant is a PRC issuer
with no other listed shares at the time of listing, this will normally mean that the portion of
H shares for which listing is sought that are held by the public and not subject to any
disposal restrictions (whether under contract, the Listing Rules, applicable laws or
otherwise), at the time of listing, must: (a) represent at least 10% of the total number of
issued shares in the class to which H shares belong at the time of listing (excluding treasury
shares), with an expected market value at the time of listing of not less than HK$50 million;
or (b) have an expected market value at the time of listing of not less than HK$600 million.
The Cornerstone Investors (as defined in the section headed ‘‘Cornerstone Investors’’
in this prospectus) have agreed to a lock-up period of six months following the Listing
Date. As such, the 7,252,800 H Shares held by the Cornerstone Investors (assuming an
Offer Price of HK$7.10 per Offer Share, being the low-end of the indicative Offer Price
range set out in this prospectus) upon the Listing shall not be counted towards the free float
of the H Shares of the Company at the time of Listing. Upon completion of the Global
Offering, and excluding (i) the 7,252,800 H Shares held by the Cornerstone Investors which
will be subject to a lock-up period; and (ii) the H Shares held by the existing Shareholders
subject to lock-up requirement under the PRC laws and regulations, it is expected that at
least 17,347,200 H Shares representing a market capitalization of HK$123.2 million
(assuming an Offer Price of HK$7.10 per Offer Share, being the low-end of the indicative
Offer Price range set out in this Prospectus, and the Over-allotment Option is not exercised)
will not be subject to any disposal restrictions (whether under contract, the Listing Rules,
applicable laws or otherwise) at the time of the Listing, and representing approximately
14.4% of the total issued share capital of our Company on the Listing Date, which is higher
than the 10% threshold and expected market value at the time of Listing of not less than
HK$50 million under Rule 19A.13C(1)(a) of the Listing Rules. Our Company will therefore
satisfy the free float requirement.

BUSINESS
OVERVIEW
Who We Are
We are an integrated prefabricated steel structure building (‘‘PS building’’)
subcontracting service provider in the industrial sector of PS building market. We offer
integrated services for construction projects across industries, covering project design and
optimization, procurement, manufacturing and installation. We are primarily engaged in
the construction of PS buildings in the PRC, and to a lesser extent, overseas. By leveraging
our technology and expertise, we have built a reputation in China’s industrial sector of the
PS building market. According to the F&S Report, we ranked third in China’s industrial
sector of the PS building market in terms of revenue in 2024, representing a 3.5% market
share; and the top two players capturing a market share of 35.8% and 6.5%, respectively.
We are committed to driving continuous innovation within the industrial sector of the
PS building market. From research and development, design, production, and engineering
application to comprehensive project management, we deliver safe and efficient integrated
PS building services. This holistic approach has enabled us to develop distinctive
competencies in the industry.
Our Industry Position and Achievements
According to the F&S Report, buildings can be broadly classified into traditional
buildings and prefabricated buildings, with the latter offering higher efficiency, reduced
waste, and greater adaptability. Within the category of prefabricated buildings, there are
further classifications based on the primary materials used: PS buildings, PC buildings, and
others, such as wood buildings. Prefabricated steel structures are particularly notable for
their lightweight, strength, and adaptability, making them an ideal choice for sustainable
and efficient construction.

BUSINESS
According to the F&S Report, the industrial sector of the PS building market involves
the design, production, and installation of steel-based construction components, offering
superior efficiency, strength, and adaptability across industrial, commercial, and residential
applications. In the industrial sector, PS building are especially valued for their ability to
accommodate large spans, enable rapid assembly and provide scalability, making them an
optimal choice for modern industrial construction. We are recognized for delivering
integrated PS building subcontracting services tailored to diverse project requirements and
our brand of ‘‘USAS’’ has gained recognition within the industry and market.
As an active player in China’s industrial sector within the PS building market, we have
consistently dedicated ourselves to the advancement and development of the industry. Since
the early 1990s, our founder and core team have introduced advanced PS building services
and products to the PRC market, actively promoting the concept of integrated PS building
services in construction and operations. In 2001, we contributed to the official release of the
DGTJ08–010–2001 specification procedures for the production and installation of light
steel structures (輕型鋼結構製作及安裝驗收規程), which is an industry standard guideline
issued by the Shanghai Metal Construction Association (上海市金屬結構行業協會). Since
then, we have continued to contribute to the drafting of numerous key national and
industry standards as well as industry regulations and codes. In addition, we are an
executive council member of the Shanghai Metal Construction Association, a founding
member of the Sub-association for Building Envelop System of the China Steel
Construction Society (中國鋼結構協會圍護系統分會) and the Metal Roofing Technical
Sub-committee of the China National Building Waterproof Association (中國建築防水協會
金屬屋面技術分會), as well as a council member of the Sub-association for Building
Envelop System of the China Steel Construction Society (中國鋼結構協會圍護系統分會)
and the Metal Roofing Technical Sub-committee of the China National Building
Waterproof Association (中國建築防水協會金屬屋面技術分會). In collaboration with
industry associations, prestigious academic institutions and well-known companies such
as Baosteel, we have completed several significant research and development projects that
contribute to the advancement of PS building services.
We were among the first companies in our industry to be recognized as a ‘‘High and
New Technology Enterprise’’. We have been named one of the ‘‘Top 10 National Metal
Enclosure System Enterprises’’ (全國金屬圍護系統行業10強企業) by the China Steel
Construction Society and have been recognized seven times consecutively by the
Shanghai Contract Credit Promotion Association as a ‘‘Contract-Abiding and
Creditworthy Enterprise’’ (守合同重信用企業). Many of our projects have received
prestigious industry awards, such as the ‘‘Jin Gang Award’’ (金鋼獎), ‘‘Jin Yu Award’’
(金禹獎), and the ‘‘China Construction Engineering Steel Structure Gold Award’’ (中國建築
工程鋼結構金獎). Additionally, we have been honored with titles such as ‘‘Shanghai
Renowned Brand’’ and ‘‘China Steel Structure Brand’’ (中國鋼結構品牌).
Our customers are mainly in the automotive and auto parts industry, with revenue
from customers in this industry contributing approximately 67.0%, 49.2%, 56.6% and
62.8% of our total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six
– 188 –

=== PAGE 199 ===
BUSINESS
months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. Our customer base also includes the machinery,
food and beverage and other sectors. We are proud to serve many leading enterprises within
these sectors, highlighting the extensive applicability and value of our PS building
subcontracting services across diverse industrial landscapes. Through our project quality
and technical expertise, we have earned recognition from both domestic and international
customers. Over the years, we have developed enduring partnerships with many customers
and certain of them have maintained business relationships with us for over 20 years.
Our Green Building Vision
As global attention on climate change and environmental protection intensifies, the
development of green buildings has become both a global trend and a key component of
China’s national strategy for the construction industry. In recent years, China has
implemented robust green building policies and standards, such as the ‘‘Green Building
Action Plan’’ and the ‘‘Evaluation Standard for Green Building,’’ further accelerating the
adoption of sustainable practices in the industry. This shift presents significant growth
opportunities, particularly in the industrial sector of the PS building market.
We aim to provide our customers with green PS building subcontracting services while
striving to achieve a harmonious balance among three core objectives of green buildings:
people-centric design (People), economic benefits (Profitability), and environmental
protection (Planet-friendly) — collectively known as the ‘‘3P Principle.’’

Building on our strengths in the industrial sector of PS building market, we have
structured our efforts in the field of green buildings into three core components:
. Sustainability: Steel, the primary material in our PS buildings, aligns with the
principles of the global circular economy. Unlike traditional concrete, steel is fully
recyclable, significantly reducing material waste and operational costs. Compared
to prefabricated concrete structures, prefabricated steel structures are
approximately 30% to 50% lighter, with a recyclability rate of 100%, offering a
more sustainable solution for the long term, according to the F&S Report.
– 189 –

=== PAGE 200 ===
BUSINESS
. Energy Efficiency: Our PS buildings are designed with lightweight, high-strength
materials that reduce the need for heavy foundations and lower overall
construction energy consumption. According to the F&S Report, the modular,
prefabricated nature of these buildings enables faster construction timelines —
about 50% shorter than conventional methods — thereby minimizing on-site
labor and resource usage.
. Prefabrication: Through factory-based production system, PS buildings achieve
high efficiency and quality in construction while reducing energy consumption
and environmental impact. This production process ensures standardized
component designs and factory prefabrication.
We are members of the U.S. Green Building Council, with multiple projects certified
under the LEED Green Building Rating System. These projects not only align with national
energy-saving and emission reduction policies but also significantly reduce environmental
impact through innovative design and construction practices.
Our Business Categories
Our business is organized into three business categories, defined by revenue
recognition models and operational characteristics: (i) PS building subcontracting
services, (ii) general contracting services, and (iii) industrial environmental equipment.
These interconnected business categories create synergies that fuel the sustained growth of
our Group.
PS building subcontracting services
Since its inception, PS building subcontracting services have been the cornerstone of
our business and continue to be the largest contributor to our revenue. Our focus remains
on delivering comprehensive PS building subcontracting services, which encompass project
design and optimization, procurement, production, on-site installation, and quality
assurance. Over the years, we have continuously honed our expertise and expanded the
range of services we offer within this domain.
For the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30,
2025, we had 149, 173, 119 and 113 PS building subcontracting projects, respectively. For
the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2025,
revenue from our PS buildings was RMB1,770.7 million, RMB1,293.9 million, RMB1,240.5
million and RMB1,247.3 million, respectively, accounting for 93.1%, 89.0%, 81.5% and
87.6% of our total revenue for the same periods, respectively.
In addition, we have developed a comprehensive portfolio of proprietary PS building
subcontracting services, recognized for the high quality, reliable performance, and seamless
integration within construction systems for various downstream industries. A standout
innovation in this business category is our Curvet Dual-Wave Arch Warehouse Series
(Curvet雙波拱形倉系列產品), specifically designed to meet the needs of agricultural
storage. According to the F&S Report, we are the only player in China’s PS building
market that provide PS building applications in the agricultural storage field, addressing a

BUSINESS
critical gap in China’s agricultural infrastructure in the industrial sector of the PS building
market. As advised by F&S, agricultural storage is an emerging market with significant
growth potential, having considered: (i) the nationwide capacity of production-based

agricultural storage infrastructures. These include faster assembly and installation, superior
durability, and improved energy efficiency, extending the shelf life of perishable goods, such
as root crops. Although agricultural storage is a novel addition to our PS buildings
portfolio, it currently accounts for a relatively small portion of our overall revenue
compared to traditional projects. In 2024, we completed two agricultural storage PS
building subcontracting projects.
General Contracting Services
In addition to our core PS building subcontracting services, we have expanded into
general contracting services, having obtained the Grade I General Contracting
Qualification for Construction Projects (建築工程施工總承包一級資質). This qualification
enables us to serve as both a general contractor and a specialized subcontractor, allowing us
to offer comprehensive subcontracting services across all stages of a project. We provide
general contracting services for both PS building subcontracting projects and PC building
projects. As a general contractor, we oversee the entire project lifecycle, including project
implementation, construction of primary structures, quality control, scheduling, safety, and
budget management. We then subcontract the on-site construction labor services to labor
subcontractors and the remaining construction process to specialized subcontractors, such
as pile foundation construction, heating, ventilation and air conditioning construction,
architectural decoration, temporary construction and security. We collaborate with various
subcontractors to ensure smooth execution of each project.
While we provide general contracting services, our revenue remains predominantly
driven by PS buildings, with general contracting serving as a complementary function that
supports our core subcontracting business. This dual capacity enhances our ability to
deliver integrated services that combine robust project oversight with our expertise in PS
buildings, adding significant value to projects where PS buildings are a core component.
Typically, for a large-scale construction project, we assume the role of general contractor,
managing the overall project, and undertake the PS building work by our PS buildings
business category. By integrating both roles within a single project, we eliminate
inefficiencies commonly associated with external subcontractors, ensuring high-quality
outcomes and streamlined project management.

Industrial Environmental Equipment
Our industrial environmental equipment business category was established to address
the rising demand for specialized products in industrial manufacturing environments. This
business category primarily focuses on the Machinery Filtering and Acoustic Systems
(‘‘MFAS’’) line, which currently generates the vast majority of our revenue. The MFAS line
provides customized intake, exhaust, and dust filtration systems, as well as noise reduction
equipment specifically designed for gas turbines. Our customers in this business category
mainly include certain of the world’s leading gas turbine manufacturers. In addition to
MFAS, we are developing and commercializing the Air Pollution Control (‘‘APC’’) product
line. The APC line offers advanced flexible dust control products and services that are
versatile and adaptable to a wide range of industrial facilities. The growing adoption of
environmental equipment in industrial buildings not only aligns with our green building
vision but also enhances the functionality of our PS buildings, fostering mutual
reinforcement and integration.
This business category has shown rapid growth and complements our PS buildings,
becoming an increasingly significant contributor to our revenue generation. For the years
ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2025, revenue from
this business category was RMB31.8 million, RMB69.4 million, RMB100.0 million, and
RMB35.3 million, respectively. The growth in this business category is driven by
increasingly stringent global environmental standards in industrial manufacturing.

STRENGTHS
Distinctive business model and service advantages
According to the F&S Report, the industrial sector of the PS building market
encompasses three primary business models: (i) integrated PS building subcontracting
service providers, (ii) general contractors, and (iii) traditional construction contractors. For
details, please refer to ‘‘Industry Overview — Analysis of China’s Prefabricated Steel
Structure Building Market — Business Model of China’s Prefabricated Steel Structure
Building Market in Industrial Sector’’ in this prospectus. We offer integrated services that
include project design and optimization, procurement, manufacturing and installation of PS
buildings. This comprehensive approach enables seamless project execution, providing
customers with tailored, end-to-end system services that maximize efficiency and deliver
exceptional value.
As a PS building subcontracting service provider, we stand out through our
technologies, product systems, and full-process project management model. By
conducting thorough analysis and optimization across all project phases, we deliver
integrated subcontracting services that not only meet the specific needs of our clients but
also enhance investment efficiency. The integrated nature of our business model serves as a
key competitive advantage, ensuring reliable delivery and superior outcomes across diverse
regions and industries.
According to the F&S Report, the industrial sector within the PS building market can
be categorized into three primary project types: general contracting projects, prefabricated
steel structure subcontracting projects, and PS building subcontracting projects. Among
these, PS building subcontracting projects stand out for their ability to facilitate in-depth
design and optimization of prefabricated steel structure products. The F&S Report projects
that the integrated PS building subcontracting projects will grow from RMB31.6 billion in
2025 to RMB53.4 billion in 2029, representing a CAGR of 14.0%, notably higher than the
6.5% CAGR of general contracting projects and the 9.3% CAGR of prefabricated steel
structure subcontracting projects. This strong growth reflects the rising demand for PS
buildings and underscores the effectiveness and future potential of our business model
within this expanding industry.
Comprehensive professional certifications and qualification profile
The industrial sector of the PS building market operates with high entry barriers,
stringent regulatory controls, and rigorous quality standards. Our extensive portfolio of
top-tier domestic and international certifications strengthens our competitive stance in the
market.

and product plans. As projects advance, our team applies advanced product systems to
maintain safety and precision in design, while strictly adhering to local standards.
Moreover, we offer comprehensive consulting services during product manufacturing and
construction to ensure smooth execution and successful project delivery.

BUSINESS
PS Building Operation
As the cornerstone of our business, PS building subcontracting service operations
combine advanced design, production, and streamlined construction processes to deliver
comprehensive, high-performance building systems for PS buildings. Below sets forth our
sample PS building subcontracting projects.
Key components of PS buildings
We provide a suite of interrelated components that work in harmony to create
high-quality, sustainable, and cost-effective building systems for PS buildings:
. Primary structure: Forms the building’s framework, providing essential
load-bearing support.
. Secondary structure: Connects the framework to roofing and walls, ensuring
structural stability and integrity.
. Enclosure systems: (i) roof enclosure system, which offers weather resistance,
insulation, and esthetic appeal, with flexible material options to suit varying
project requirements; (ii) wall enclosure system, which provides insulation,
weatherproofing, and design versatility for the building exterior; and (iii) steel
deck system, which enhances structural stability for multi-story applications,
supporting additional loads efficiently.
. Accessories: Include doors, windows, fans, skylights, and other features that
improve functionality, ventilation, and energy efficiency.
– 204 –

=== PAGE 215 ===
BUSINESS
By integrating these four components, we deliver a comprehensive, high-performance
building system tailored to the unique needs of each PS building subcontracting project.
This holistic approach ensures that every aspect of the building — from structural integrity
to environmental performance — is optimized for efficiency and sustainability.
Process overview
To transform concepts into completed structures, our PS building subcontracting
service business category follow a structured workflow designed to maximize efficiency and
ensure superior outcomes:
Identification of business opportunities
The identification of potential projects is driven by a proactive and strategic approach
led by our sales personnel of the Marketing Center. They play a key role in developing
market opportunities by conducting market research, engaging directly with potential
clients, conducting site visits, and attending seminars to build strong relationships with key
decision-makers. By working in tandem with the Contract and Quotation Department, sales
personnel ensure that each project is thoroughly assessed for technical feasibility, client
needs, and market conditions. This collaboration ensures that all potential projects are
carefully evaluated, and initial estimates are prepared to highlight the advantages of our PS
buildings and integrated services.
Throughout this process, the Technical Center also provides critical support by
conducting feasibility analysis and offering technical consultations. This consultative
approach allows us to present tailored, high-value service to customers, positioning us as a
preferred partner from the outset.
Pre-tendering and tendering process
Once a project is identified and an opportunity to tender is recognized, we initiate a
proactive and strategic approach to the tendering process. As our projects focus exclusively
on the private sector, we emphasize providing multiple quotes and tailored services that
meet the specific needs of each client. Our Business Management Center leads the process,
coordinating with our Technical Center to ensure the feasibility of the proposed services
and align them with the client’s requirements.
Our tendering process is highly collaborative, emphasizing customized, system-based
service tailored to meet client-specific requirements, rather than competing solely on cost.
Sales personnel lead the process by initiating a request for quotation, gathering and
confirming all key project details, including design drawings, specifications, and required
documentation, to ensure clarity and alignment with client expectations. Simultaneously,
our Supply Chain Management engages in inquiries with suppliers to obtain accurate
pricing and technical details, which are critical for preparing competitive and reliable
quotes.

Throughout the Track Record Period, our tender success rate demonstrated
adaptability and effectiveness in securing new contracts, reflecting our ability to respond
to shifting market dynamics. According to F&S, in the PS building industry, the tender
success rate for Chinese PS building companies with annual revenue exceeding RMB10.0
million generally ranges from 15% to 30%, which varies depending on various factors,
including market competition, economic conditions, pricing, technical and functional
capabilities and negotiation with customers on contract terms. Our Directors consider,
concurred by F&S, that our tender success rate for PS building subcontracting projects
during the Track Record Period was comparable to the industry average.
The primary reason for our relatively lower success rate for PS building subcontracting
projects in 2024 was our increased efforts in overseas expansion to attract new clients. The
number of tenders we submitted witnessed a significant growth, with the growth rate
outpacing that of the projects we successfully won. Our tender success rate for PS building
subcontracting projects for the six months ended June 30, 2025 increased to 32.1%
primarily because several of our major customers undertook significant business expansion
initiatives in 2025. Our established long-term relationships with these clients contributed to
a higher tender success rate for their projects. Additionally, the limited number of
competitors in our overseas markets further enhanced our bidding success, thereby
elevating the overall average tender success rate. In recent years, the real estate sector has
experienced a downturn; however, such downturn has primarily impacted the commercial
building and residential segments, whereas our PS building subcontracting services are
mainly focused on the industrial sector. The demand for our services were primarily driven

BUSINESS
by the industrial needs of clients across various industries such as automotive
manufacturing, machinery and other commercial industries. For instance, our revenue
from end customers in automotive and auto parts industry increased by 237.0% to
RMB894.1 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025 from RMB265.3 million for the
six months ended June 30, 2024. Therefore, the overall slowdown in the real estate industry
in China has not had a significant impact on our business operations nor tender success rate
of this segment during the first half of 2025.
Award of contract and project team organization
Upon receiving the tender award notification, the project is formally transferred from
the sales personnel to the project team. The project team is composed of key personnel from
our various departments, such as the Business Management Center, Technical Center,
Supply Chain Management, and Project Center, with each department taking responsibility
for their respective roles in executing the project. Once the project team is formed, the first
step is the kick-off meeting, where all stakeholders align on key objectives, timelines, and
project goals. The meeting is led by the project manager, with input from design personnel,
the Technical Center, and the Supply Chain Management team to ensure that every aspect
of the project is thoroughly planned and well-coordinated. The project team will also begin
working on detailed execution plans, including procurement schedules, resource allocations,
and construction timelines.
Simultaneously, the Business Management Center works with the Legal Center and the
Finance Center to finalize the contract details. This step is critical to ensure that the project
has the appropriate legal and financial framework to proceed smoothly. Once all details are
confirmed and the contract is signed, the project officially moves into the execution phase.
Project execution
The execution phase begins with the Technical Center completing project designs,
encompassing both structural and detailed drawings. This step ensures that the project’s
technical requirements are clearly defined and tailored to the client’s specific needs.
Following the completion of designs, the Production Center develops a comprehensive
production and shipping schedule, organizes the production process, and ensures that all
components are produced according to plan. Once the design and production plans are
finalized, we enter the formal execution phase. During this phase, the Technical Center
continues to play a critical role by refining the technical aspects of the project and providing
advanced system services.
Our Supply Chain Management is responsible for sourcing high-quality materials,
particularly large-volume raw materials, that meet the specific requirements. This phase
marks the start of full-scale procurement and early-stage construction. To ensure the timely
availability of essential materials, such as steel plate, we procure from a vetted list of
approved suppliers, with quotes and negotiations conducted during the tendering phase.
Once procurement is underway, our Production Center engages in preparing the
necessary components for assembly and installation. With careful coordination between all
departments, we ensure that the project progresses on schedule. The Project Center oversees
– 207 –

=== PAGE 218 ===
BUSINESS
the entire construction process, managing timelines and ensuring that all work aligns with
the agreed-upon plans. This department also maintains close collaboration with design
personnel to ensure that any necessary design adjustments are seamlessly incorporated
during construction, and leads on-site coordination and quality control, ensuring that the
PS building services are integrated smoothly and effectively.
During the project execution phase, we typically set certain project milestones. Once
these milestones are reached, we are generally entitled to collect progress payments from the
clients. These milestones are generally as follows: (i) the arrival of major PS building
components at the project site; (ii) completion of installation of primary structures for
individual project unit; and (iii) completion of installation of enclosure systems for
individual project unit. Upon achievement of such milestones, we usually submit a progress
payment application to our customer stating the amount of work completed. Our customer
will certify our work by issuing a payment certificate to us. We will then issue the invoice to
our customer for progress payment.
For installation, we generally engage specialized labor subcontracting companies,
selected for their expertise in installing PS buildings. We oversee the installation process to
ensure all work meets our stringent quality standards. For further details on our labor
subcontracting, please refer to ‘‘— Suppliers — Labor Subcontracting’’ below.
This well-coordinated, systematic approach to project construction ensures that each
phase integrates seamlessly, enabling us to deliver high-quality, efficient, and reliable
services that meet or exceed customer expectations.
Final inspection and project handover
Once construction work is completed, the project enters the final inspection phase.
This is a critical stage in the project lifecycle, where we ensure that all aspects of the
building meet the agreed-upon specifications and quality standards before the formal
acceptance by our clients. The final inspection is a legally mandated step, where compliance
with building codes and contractual obligations is verified. Once the inspection is
successfully completed and the project is approved, we proceed with the physical
handover. This marks the moment when the project is formally transferred to the client,
signifying the completion of construction work.
Following the physical handover, we proceed to obtaining the certification of the
completed construction work from our customers for the final project financial settlement.
During this stage, we settle the volume of the construction work we have carried out with
the client. Our Finance Center manages the collection process of settlement payment, to
ensure that outstanding transactions are completed accurately and timely.
Post-construction support and maintenance
After the project handover, we continue to provide ongoing support and maintenance
services to ensure that the building systems function as expected. Our after-sales service
team is dedicated to maintaining open communication with the client, addressing any
post-construction issues, and ensuring long-term satisfaction.

General Contracting Service Operation
Our workflow for general contracting services follows a structure similar to that of our
PS buildings, with comprehensive processes designed to ensure efficiency, quality, and
seamless project execution. However, there are key distinctions that highlight the unique
aspects of general contracting services. We primarily act as a general contractor for
construction projects, providing professional and comprehensive project management
services. The scope of general contracting services involves broader project oversight and
coordination responsibilities compared to PS building subcontracting service business
category.
As the general contractor, we assume a central role in managing the integration of
multiple project components, ensuring smooth execution from start to finish. During the
design phase, we work closely with architects and engineers to align project specifications
with the customer’s vision and requirements. Throughout construction, we oversee
scheduling, progress tracking, and quality control, ensuring all subcontractors adhere to
the required safety, efficiency, and performance standards.
Process overview
Our general contracting service follows a structured workflow to ensure seamless
project execution:
Identification of business opportunities
In addition to regular pursuit of business opportunities for our general contracting
services, leveraging our expertise and established reputation in PS buildings, our general
contracting team also collaborates closely with PS buildings sales personnel to identify
business opportunities. When engaging with potential customers to discuss services for PS
buildings, the sales team evaluates whether the project has the demand for general
contracting services. If such opportunities are identified, our general contracting sales
personnel are brought in to participate. This collaborative effort ensures that we effectively
identify and secure projects with general contracting needs, offering customers
comprehensive service that integrate our specialized PS building expertise with broader
project management services.
Pre-tendering and tendering process
Once a project is identified and an opportunity to tender is recognized, we initiate a
proactive and strategic approach to the tendering process. We prepare detailed proposals in
collaboration with our Technical Center, Business Management Center and Supply Chain
Management to ensure our tendering process and quotes are tailored to meet client-specific
requirements and our pricing policy. Our tendering strategy considers project complexity,
material costs, labor availability, and regulatory compliance.

According to F&S, the tender success rate of general contracting services in the PRC
generally rages from 5% to 40%. The wide range of tender success rate for general
contracting projects in the PRC is primarily due to the significantly different tender
strategies employed by various companies. Some companies secure projects by broadly
participating in numerous tenders, while others conduct thorough preliminary analysis of
their own capabilities and potential competitors with a high probability of success,
subsequently winning those projects through meticulous tender preparation. Given the
complementary role of our general contracting business category, we do not adopt a
high-volume tendering strategy. Instead, we only participate in project tender after carefully
analyzing the project circumstances, as well as our capabilities and advantages. This
approach has consequently led to a relatively high tender success rate for us. Our Directors
consider, concurred by F&S, that our tender success rate for general contracting projects
during the Track Record Period was comparable to the industry average.
Our success rate for general contracting projects increased to 35.3% in 2024, compared
to 25.0% in 2022 and 20.0% in 2023, primarily attributable to the accelerated development
of our general contracting business segment since the end of 2023, which has fueled growth
in both the volume of tenders submitted and the successful tenders secured in 2024. For the
six months ended June 30, 2025, our success rate for general contracting projects decreased
to 18.8%, primarily because the contraction in China’s real estate development industry has
led to intensified competition in the market, with more contractors competing for fewer
available projects, our overall tender success rate was reduced.

Once awarded with the contract, the project is formally transferred to the project team.

with each department taking responsibility for their respective roles in executing the
project. Once the project team is formed, the first step is the kick-off meeting, where all
stakeholders align on key objectives, subcontracting scope, timelines, and project goals.
Signing subcontracting agreements
Our general contracting services operate under a two-tier framework. First, we enter
into a contract with the project owner, serving as the general contractor. Subsequently,
specialized aspects of the project are subcontracted to either external vendors or internal
business departments within our Group. For general contracting projects involving PS
building components, we will undertake this part internally and carry out construction
work in accordance with the process of PS building operations. For general contracting
projects for PC buildings, we assume the responsibility for the construction of the primary
structure. This mainly encompasses procurement activities carried out in accordance with
the design specifications provided by the project owner, arranging for the transportation of
relevant materials and components to the construction site, and conducting thorough
on-site inspections. Generally, we subcontract the on-site labor work of this portion to
qualified labor subcontractors. The construction process implemented by these
subcontractors are supervised by us to ensure compliance the project requirements and
quality standards. In addition, we will subcontract specific construction tasks to specialized
subcontractors. Examples of such tasks include pile foundation construction, the
installation and construction of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems,
architectural decoration work, the establishment of temporary structures, and
security-related construction activities.
Given our core focus on PS building subcontracting projects, our general contracting
projects generally include the undertaking of PS building components by our PS building
subcontracting service business department. This approach allows us to leverage our
internal expertise, ensuring strict quality control, cost efficiency, and timely delivery for
these critical components. We then subcontract other specialized works to qualified external
subcontractors.
Project execution and on-site coordination
During the construction phase, our project managers oversee daily operations on-site,
coordinating subcontractors and monitoring work progress. We conduct regular site
inspections, supervising subcontractors’ compliance with safety standards, technical
specifications, and contractual obligations. Any necessary design modifications are
reviewed and implemented in coordination with the client and engineering team.
During the project execution phase, we typically set certain project milestones. Once
these milestones are reached, we are generally entitled to collect progress payments from the
clients. These milestones are generally as follows: (i) monthly progress payment per value of
work performed; and (ii) completion of construction of individual project unit. Upon
achievement of such milestones, we usually submit a progress payment application to our
customer stating the amount of work completed. Our customer will certify our work by
issuing a payment certificate to us. We will then issue the invoice to our customer for
progress payment.

Final inspection and project handover
When the construction of the project is completed, we conduct final inspection and
acceptance alongside the client and regulatory authorities to ensure compliance with project

Industrial Environmental Equipment Operation
The industrial environmental equipment business category represents a strategic
extension of our expertise in the PS buildings, responding to the growing demand for
advanced environmental products in industrial manufacturing. This extension is
underpinned by shared core capabilities, converging technical requirements and
overlapping customer bases across both business categories. Our core technical strengths
lie in the design, fabrication and installation of non-standard, large-scale prefabricated steel
components, which require complex engineering, modularized manufacturing, and precision
assembly. These capabilities can be transplanted to the design and production of industrial
environmental equipment. Meanwhile, our existing equipment for manufacturing PS
building components (such as cutting and forming machines, welding machines and shot
blasting machines) can be adapted with minor adjustments for the production of industrial
environmental protection equipment. In addition, our customers for PS buildings span
across the industrial sector and are facing growing regulatory obligations for environmental
compliance. We may leverage our established customer relationships and sales network to
develop the industrial environmental equipment business category, capitalizing on
synergistic advantages.

BUSINESS
This category is currently anchored by our MFAS, which contributed the vast majority

Gas Turbine
Our MFAS are custom-designed auxiliary equipment for gas turbines, which are
essential energy conversion devices. These turbines require precise airflow management to
maintain high efficiency and optimal performance. MFAS, as supporting systems,
integrates modules such as the venting house, air intake system (including filtration,
cooling, and noise reduction), acoustic chamber, and silencer/exhaust to ensure smooth and
efficient operation of gas turbines. These systems are large, heavy, and highly specialized,
designed to fit seamlessly with gas turbines from leading global manufacturers. The
customization of MFAS is tailored specifically to each client’s turbine specifications,
ensuring a perfect match.
In addition to MFAS, we are developing and commercializing our advanced APC
products for industrial dust control. Unlike MFAS, which is specialized for gas turbines,
our APC products are highly versatile and can be adapted to nearly all types of industrial
facilities. These products are focused on efficiently removing dust from the air in industrial
environments, providing a compact and space-saving products compared to traditional
filtration systems. Many of our PS buildings customers are potential clients for our APC
products. We are actively working on highlighting the synergy between our PS building
subcontracting services and APC products offerings, which allow us to deliver integrated
systems that address both structural and environmental needs. During the Track Record
Period, we also sold agricultural machinery and accessories from time to time to certain
customers.

Process overview
Our industrial environmental equipment business focuses on providing tailored
products and services for customers across various industries. The sales process follows a
structured workflow to ensure seamless product delivery and after-sales support:
Identification of business opportunities
Our sales team actively identifies potential customers through market research,
industry exhibitions, and business referrals. We primarily target international industrial
manufacturers, construction firms, and energy companies requiring environmental
compliance products.
Preliminary negotiations, product design and award of contract
Upon initial engagement with a client, we conduct technical discussions to identify
specific project requirements. The client provides detailed turbine parameters, including
equipment specifications, performance expectations, and applicable compliance standards.
Based on this information, we carry out advanced fluid dynamics, acoustic, and structural
analyses to develop a preliminary model for the client’s review.
We then proceed with multiple rounds of technical validation and clarification to
further refine the model, including optimizing airflow, reducing noise, and ensuring
durability. Once both parties reach a consensus on the technical aspects, we enter into a
technical agreement with the client.
Following the conclusion of the technical agreement, our Technical Center works
jointly with the Quotation Department to prepare a project quotation. Once the pricing and
commercial terms are reviewed and approved by the Contract Department, a formal
contract is executed with the client.
Product manufacturing
The manufacturing process involves material preparation, assembly, coating, and
rigorous quality control inspections. Each unit undergoes performance testing to meet
industry and client specifications before being approved for delivery. For details, please
refer to ‘‘— Our Production — Production Process’’ below.
Product delivery
The final product undergoes rigorous quality control to meet strict operational
standards. Final products are packaged and delivered either at our production facilities or
locations designated by our customers, with logistics carefully managed to ensure timely
delivery.

(2) New projects awarded indicates projects contracted during each respective year/period, where

adding newly awarded projects and deducting those completed within the period, resulting

=== PAGE 230 ===
BUSINESS
Notes:
(1) The opening backlog value represents the total contract value of projects awarded but not yet
completed at the start of each year/period.
(2) Adjustments or variation orders refer to modifications in design or changes requested by the
customer after the signing of the contract. These include changes in the design conditions or
requirements proposed by the customer before the delivery of completed design documents.
(3) The ending backlog value reflects the portion of estimated revenue for projects that remain
uncompleted at the end of each year/period.
The backlog value calculation starts with the total contract value of projects awarded
but not yet completed at the beginning of the period. We add the estimated contract values
of new projects awarded and adjust per any approved variation orders. From this adjusted
total, recognized revenue for the period is subtracted, yielding the backlog value to be
carried forward.
During the Track Record Period, the number of projects and their corresponding
backlog values exhibited significant fluctuations, primarily influenced by the nature, scale,
and timing of project completions and new awards. These trends reflect typical patterns in
project-based industries, where customers’ payment and backlog values align closely with
project progression.
For the year ended December 31, 2022, the number of projects began at 191 and
declined to 164 by year-end. This reduction was largely driven by the completion of 68
projects, while only 41 new projects were awarded during the same period. The
corresponding backlog value decreased by 64.2%, from RMB1,238.4 million to
RMB443.2 million. This sharp decline was primarily attributed to the substantial
recognition of revenue from completed projects, highlighting the cyclical nature of our
project pipeline. In particular, in 2022, the opening backlog value and the new contract
awards from Customer A, our largest customer for the same year, totaled RMB1,331.1
million. Of this amount, 92.6% of the relevant construction work was completed during the
year, resulting in the recognition of approximately RMB1,233.0 million in revenue for 2022
and thereby affecting a substantial reduction in our ending backlog value in the same year.
For the year ended December 31, 2023, the number of projects continued to decline,
ending at 92 from an opening count of 164, with 156 projects completed and 84 new projects
awarded. The backlog value for the year ended December 31, 2023 decreased to RMB363.3
million, reflecting relatively stable movement. The sustained decrease in both project count
and backlog value during this period was primarily attributed to the completion of a large
number of projects in 2023.
– 220 –

=== PAGE 231 ===
BUSINESS
For the year ended December 31, 2024, the number of projects decreased to 67 from an
opening count of 92. This reduction resulted from the completion of 101 projects against 76
new awards. As of December 31, 2024, we recorded a relatively higher ending backlog value
of approximately RMB1,001.1 million, as compared to RMB443.2 million, RMB363.3
million as of December 31, 2022 and 2023, respectively, primarily because we were awarded
with one general contracting project (Project #16) with contract sum amounting to
approximately RMB229.4 million as well as 13 large-scale PS building subcontracting
projects with each contract sum over RMB50.0 million. In line with the commencement
dates and timelines, only 5.6% of the construction work of these projects was completed
and recognized in revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024.
For the six months ended June 30, 2025, the number of projects increased to 117 from
an opening count of 67, primarily because we were awarded with 86 new projects during the
period. As of June 30, 2025, our ending backlog value decreased to approximately
RMB883.9 million from RMB1,001.1 million as of December 31, 2024, reflecting a
substantial progress recorded for newly awarded projects during the period.
From July 1, 2025 to the Latest Practicable Date, the number of projects remained
relatively stable at 119 from an opening count of 117 and the backlog value decreased to
RMB789.2 million compared to an opening of RMB883.9 million. The decrease primarily
resulted from the completion of a substantial number of projects during the period. While
we continued to expand into key markets such as Thailand, the new projects added were
generally smaller in both scale and contract value.
From an industry perspective, these levels of backlog — in both project count and
value — remain consistent with sector norms, reflecting a healthy flow of projects that
supports long-term revenue generation. This balance ensures that we continue to capitalize
on market opportunities while maintaining a stable and scalable operational model.
