Project Delays
Project #11, a PS building subcontracting project located in Thailand, with a contract
sum of RMB89.3 million, was suspended from June to October 2024. The delay was
primarily because: (i) our client’s customs clearance delays impeded the timely entry of the
PS building components manufactured by us; and (ii) the rainy season in Thailand rendered
the site unsuitable for construction activities from June to late October in 2024. We resumed
on-site construction since November 2024. However, due to the necessity of clearing the
construction site after rain, the progress was relatively slow. We adopted Ex-works (EXW)
delivery term for this project, so that the client was responsible for transportation and
custom clearance, and all associated costs shall be borne by itself. During the period of
delay, additional expenses incurred by us were mainly for on-site machinery and installation
workers. When formulating the budget for the installation fees, we had already taken into
consideration the uncontrollable factors associated with overseas projects, such as the rainy
season in Southeast Asia, and incorporated these costs into the pricing. As such, no
significant additional costs were incurred from the suspension of this project. As we had
taken into account potential weather conditions at the project site during the initial
budgeting process and incorporated such factors into our cost projects, we did not incur any
cost overrun and therefore did not seek compensation from our customer. As of the Latest
Practicable Date, we had completed the construction work for this project.
Project #17, a PS building subcontracting project located in Jiangsu Province, the
PRC, with a contract sum of approximately RMB130.5 million, the commencement date of
which was postponed from May 2024 to September 2024, and further to December 2024,
primarily due to change of design by the project owner. After signing contract with the
client, we maintained proactive communication with them, who promptly informed us of
the design plan changes and the potential delay in the project schedule. Therefore, we only
completed the design phase of the project and did not commence the procurement nor
arrange for outsourced production before being informed the final project schedule. We
estimated that the additional costs incurred in connection with this project amount to be
immaterial, primarily consisting of labor costs related to our design personnel. Such
amount did not result in a cost overrun for the project. Given the immateriality of the
amount and our long-standing cooperative relationship with the client, we did not seek
compensation from the client. As of the Latest Practicable Date, the construction of this
project was proceeding normally.
Project #28, a PS building subcontracting project located in Thailand, with a contract
sum of RMB39.7 million. From June to late October 2024, the on-site construction progress
of the project was significantly slow due to the rainy season in Thailand, resulting in the
expected completion date being postponed from August 2024 to April 2025. During the
extended construction period, additional expenses incurred by us were mainly for on-site
machinery and installation workers. In August 2024, the project owner entered into a
supplementary agreement with us, providing additional compensation to us to cover the
corresponding costs. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had completed approximately
99.0% of the construction work for this project.
– 226 –

=== PAGE 237 ===
BUSINESS
Project #29, a PS building subcontracting project located in Jiangsu Province, the
PRC, with a contract sum of approximately RMB22.1 million, its commencement was
postponed from July 2022 to April 2023, primarily due to construction delays by the general
contractor. In addition, owing to complications with the project owner’s land-related
procedures, the overall construction progressed in an intermittent manner from April 2023
to October 2024. In August 2024, we entered into a supplementary agreement with the
project owner in respect of the extended construction period. Under this agreement,
additional fees were provided to compensate for the losses incurred by us as a result of the
project delays. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had completed significant construction
work for this project, which was expected to complete the inspection in 2025.
Project #30, a PS building subcontracting project located in Hebei Province, the PRC,
with a contract sum of approximately RMB31.0 million, its commencement date was
postponed from May 2023 to April 2024. The delay was primarily caused by the overall
delay in the construction work of the general contractor. Specifically, the pre-embedding
process took longer than schedule and the concrete columns had not been completed in a
timely manner, rendering the site unsuitable for the installation of PS buildings. As our
construction team observed the potential delay on-site, we withdrew the on-site teams
during the affected period. As a result, no significant additional costs were incurred. As of
the Latest Practicable Date, we had completed the construction and inspection of this
project.
Project #31, a PS building subcontracting project located in Jiangsu Province, the
PRC, with a contract sum of approximately RMB19.8 million, its completion date was
delayed from October 2023 to September 2024. The delay was primarily caused by: (i)
postponed commencement date from June to September 2023 due to the design change by
the project owner; and (ii) extended construction process caused by further design
modifications made by the project owner during the construction process. In December
2023 and March 2024, we entered into two supplementary agreements with the general
contractor and the project owner. These agreements included the additional costs incurred
by us arising from project delays caused by design changes. As of the Latest Practicable
Date, we had completed the construction and inspection of this project.
The contracts between us and our customers generally stipulate that in the event of
project cancellation or material delays due to customer’s reasons, we are entitled to claim
the costs and losses incurred by us from our customers. In practice, if the project schedule is
delayed upon the customers’ request, we will typically engage in friendly negotiations with
the customer regarding costs and losses resulting from the delay. During the Track Record
Period, for projects where delays resulted in significant additional costs, we received
sufficient compensation from our customers. For other projects where the additional costs
were not material and were covered by our original budgeting, we did not pursue claims
against our customers, having taken into account commercial considerations and industry
practice.

BUSINESS
OUR PRODUCTION
Production Process
The production process at our facilities is designed to ensure the efficient and
high-quality production of PS building components and industrial environmental
equipment. By combining advanced equipment, streamlined workflows, and rigorous
quality control measures, we deliver products that meet both industry standards and
customer expectations.
Below is a description of the key stages in our production process, which can be
illustrated with a simple flowchart.
Product
Materials Cutting and Surface
Assembling Welding inspection and
inspection forming treatment
packaging
Profiling Hole making
Materials inspection
The process begins with materials inspection, where incoming raw materials, primarily
steel plate, are carefully examined to ensure compliance with project-specific standards and
quality requirements. Inspections are conducted jointly by our production staff and, when
applicable, representatives designated by our clients. Materials are then organized and
stored in designated areas to prevent mix-ups and facilitate smooth handling throughout
the production cycle.
– 231 –

=== PAGE 242 ===
BUSINESS
Cutting and forming
Next, the steel materials undergo cutting and forming. In this stage, the raw steel is
processed into parts of predetermined shapes, sizes, and lengths using precision cutting and
forming machinery. This step includes trimming, leveling, milling, and bending the
materials to achieve the desired dimensions and configurations. Maintaining strict safety
protocols, we ensure that workers operate machinery at a safe distance from one another to
minimize risks.
Assembling
Following cutting and forming, the components proceed to assembling. At this stage,
our technicians verify the accuracy of dimensions, angles, weld joints, and other critical
parameters to confirm conformity with the project’s technical drawings. Once inspected, the
parts are assembled into larger substructures or modules, laying the groundwork for the
final product.
– 232 –

=== PAGE 243 ===
BUSINESS
Welding
The assembled components are then subjected to welding, where individual steel parts
are joined together using high-precision welding techniques. We employ both internal
inspections and third-party testing services to validate the strength and quality of the welds.
Depending on the project’s requirements, customer representatives may also inspect the
welds to ensure that the products meet all necessary specifications.
Surface treatment
After welding, the components undergo surface treatment, which includes polishing to
eliminate imperfections such as rust stains or welding slag. Depending on the project
requirements, additional steps such as galvanizing or painting may be performed to enhance
corrosion resistance and durability of the material. The galvanizing process involves
immersing components in molten zinc, creating a protective zinc layer, while painting adds
further protection and visual appeal.
– 233 –

=== PAGE 244 ===
BUSINESS
Profiling
For production of our secondary structure and enclosure systems components, steel
coils are shaped through profiling processes to create specific forms. These profiled steel
coils are commonly used to enhance the rigidity and strength of steel components while
reducing the overall weight of the structure.
Hole making
For production of our secondary structure and roof enclosure systems components, we
drill holes on the profiled coils in accordance with various design requirements for the
specific projects. Following design, marking locations, and selecting appropriate
hole-making methods depending on the size, number and thickness of the steel
components, holes are drilled and created. Edge treatment then need to be conducted
followed by dimension inspection to ensure consistency with the design.
– 234 –

=== PAGE 245 ===
BUSINESS
Production inspection and packaging
The final stage is product inspection and packaging. Completed products are
rigorously inspected by our quality control team and, where applicable, by client
representatives. Once approved, the products are carefully packaged and wrapped in
protective materials to prevent damage during transportation. They are then prepared for
delivery to project sites, ensuring that they reach their destination in optimal condition.
Throughout the production process, specialized equipment such as gantry cranes is
used to transport bulky and heavy materials within the production facility safely and
efficiently. This approach ensures seamless movement between production stages and
supports the timely completion of all tasks. We conduct stringent quality control measures
to ensure the quality of our products. For details, please refer to ‘‘— Quality Control’’
below.
Production Facilities
Our production capabilities are currently supported by our advanced production
facilities located in (i) Shanghai, (ii) Suzhou, Jiangsu Province and (iii) Jiangmen,
Guangdong Province. Our production facilities are equipped to support multiple product
lines, ensuring flexibility and scalability across all operations. This approach allows us to
optimize both in-house production for core components and outsourced production
capacity for outsourced parts, achieving a balanced and efficient production workflow.

BUSINESS
Our production facilities are equipped with the advanced machinery and equipment,
which we believe is essential to increase automation, ensure reliability of our production
processes as well as quality of our products. Major machinery and equipment applied in our
production processes include cutting and forming machines, automatic assembling
machines, wielding machines, surface treatment equipment such as angle grinders and
shot blasting machines, forming and bending machines, as well as punching and press
machines. In addition, cranes and forklifts are extensively used for the transportation of
raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished goods, ensuring efficient and safe
handling throughout the production process.
We carry out inspections and maintenance of our production facilities, which include
regular inspection and repair of our machinery and equipment. Our employees are trained
before they are allowed to use the relevant equipment. Equipment users shall follow the
internal protocol to carry out daily maintenance, including wiping and adding lubricating
oil to the machinery. In case of unexpected machinery failure, equipment user shall report
immediately to the supervisor and inform the relevant maintenance staff for repair. During
the Track Record Period, we did not experience any material or prolonged suspensions of
operations due to machinery, equipment or other facility failures.

business focus on PS buildings. As PS building subcontracting services constitute our
primary business category, the production of PS building components represents a critical
capacity, underpinning the delivery of our projects. This strategic importance has driven
our efforts to maintain a high utilization rate, and we plan to expand this core production
capacity to support our ongoing domestic and international business growth.
For the year ended December 31, 2022, the utilization rate reached a high level of
128.3%. This was primarily due to intensive production scheduling, particularly in January,
as we allocated additional operating hours around the Chinese New Year Festival to meet

this period, demonstrating our commitment to operational excellence and client
satisfaction.

the utilization rate amounted to 88.1% for the year ended December 31, 2023. This
reduction coincides with the growth of our other business categories, particularly industrial
environmental equipment, which has diversified our production activities and contributed
to a more balanced utilization of our production resources. The utilization rate for PS
building components increased to 101.7% for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily
due to intense production scheduling aimed at meeting critical project milestones. The
utilization rate for PS building components reached 158.7% for the six months ended June
30, 2025, primarily driven by our intensive production scheduling during the period, which
ensured timely fulfillment of our delivery commitments to our customers.

Expansion plans
Expansion and upgrade of our current production facilities
To strengthen our market position, we are expanding and upgrading our production
facilities to enhance high-quality production capacity. The expansion and upgrade are
target to be completed by end of 2026, increasing our annual production capacity by 50,000
tons of PS building components and 2,000 tons of industrial environmental equipment. The
total capital expenditure for the expansion and upgrade of our production facility is
estimated to be approximately RMB50.2 million, and approximately RMB22.4 million
(HK$24.6 million) to be funded by the net proceeds from the Global Offering. The
remaining portion will be financed through cash generated from operating activities, bank
borrowings, or equity and debt fund raising. For details, please refer to the section headed
‘‘Future Plans and Use of Proceeds’’ in this prospectus.
Expansion plans in Southeast Asia
Southeast Asia is a key focus of our international strategy, underpinned by its strong
economic growth and increasing demand for PS buildings. To capitalize on this growth, we
plan to pursue opportunities for establishing local production facilities in the region. For
instance, we plan to establish a production facility in Thailand and we plan to use
approximately RMB10.0 million (HK$11.0 million) of the estimated net proceeds of the
Global Offering for land leasing, facility construction and purchase of major machinery and
equipment. For details, please refer to the section headed ‘‘Future Plans and Use of
Proceeds’’ in this prospectus.
CUSTOMERS
Our customers are mainly in the automotive and auto parts industry, with revenue
from customers in this industry contributing approximately 67.0%, 49.2%, 56.6% and
62.8% of our total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six
months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. Our customer base also includes the machinery,
food and beverage and other sectors. These companies comprise private enterprises, listed
companies, and foreign-invested companies, enabling us to cater to a broad spectrum of
recurring customers who rely on our tailored and high standards of service. For the years
ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2025, we served 91,
98, 95 and 59 customers, respectively.

Building long-term relationships with our customers is a cornerstone of our business
strategy. Over the years, we have developed enduring partnerships with many customers
and certain of them have maintained business relationships with us for over 20 years. These
long-standing relationships highlight the consistent trust our customers place in us to meet
their evolving needs.
Our ability to sustain and deepen customer relationships is driven by our reliable
delivery, high-quality and tailored services. Many of our customers operate in industries
with specialized requirements, and we excel in adapting our services to meet their unique
operational demands. This deep understanding of customer needs fosters customer
stickiness by embedding our services into their operations.
Furthermore, our flexible maintenance and after-sales support services ensure that we
continue to add value long after project completion, further strengthening our role as a
trusted partner. By combining technical expertise, proactive engagement, and a
customer-centric approach, we have built a business model that emphasizes long-term
collaboration and mutual growth.

For the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2023, Customer B was both one of our top

Customer Concentration
During the Track Record Period, the revenue concentration from our top five
customers has fluctuated, with aggregate contributions of approximately 77.7%, 64.6%,
59.0% and 84.0% for the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2023, 2024 and the six months
ended June 30, 2025, respectively. The decline from 2022 to 2024 reflects our strategic
efforts to diversify our customer base, onboard new clients, and reduce reliance on a small
group of major customers. These results align with our deliberate approach to broadening
market exposure and expanding our project portfolio across industries and geographies.
However, top five customers’ contribution to our revenue rebounded to 84.0% for the six
months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was mainly because several of our major
customers in the automotive and auto parts, machinery, and food and beverage industries
experienced significant business expansion in 2025, leading to substantially increased
demand and a higher volume of orders placed with us.
Our revenue concentration during the Track Record Period was significantly
influenced by our largest customer, Customer A, which contributed approximately 64.8%
of our revenue in 2022. This was primarily driven by the rapid expansion of the new energy
industry, during which Customer A undertook large-scale facility construction projects to
meet growing production demands. Leveraging our expertise in delivering high-quality,
efficient PS building subcontracting services, we supported Customer A in executing its
ambitious expansion plans.

BUSINESS
For the year ended December 31, 2023, Customer A’s contribution to our revenue
declined to 43.1% in line with the pace of its domestic expansion. This shift was further
supported by the successful onboarding of new clients and the execution of contracts for
returning customers, including additional project awards from long-term clients. These
developments demonstrate our ability to not only retain long-term customers but also
expand our relationships by offering a wider range of services.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, Customer A’s contribution to our revenue
amounted to 42.1%. The diversification of our customer base is further evidenced by the
increasing contribution from new customers, particularly as we expanded into new
industries and geographies. For instance, our industrial environmental equipment
business category contributed additional revenue during the Track Record Period,
reflecting our ability to generate income from supplementary business categories beyond
our core PS building subcontracting services. Moreover, the onboarding of overseas
projects and orders in 2024 has accelerated this trend, with contributions expected from
these international markets. This diversification highlights our ability of reducing any single
client or region.
For the six months ended June 30, 2025, Customer A’s contribution to our revenue
increased to 61.1%. The increase was primarily attributable to Customer A’s business
expansion initiatives in Central China, which involved the establishment of multiple new
facilities in the region to meet its growing operational demand, resulting in a substantial
increase in orders placed with us.
We are of the view that the likelihood of our relationship with Customer A to be
subject to material adverse change or termination is relatively low, based on the following
key considerations:
. We have established long-term business relationship with Customer A since 2008.
This long-term relationship has enabled deep familiarity with Customer A’s
operational and technical requirements, which allow us to better provide tailored
PS building subcontracting services to Customer A. Hence, Customer A will be
more inclined to collaborate with us for their construction projects under the same
circumstances;
. According to F&S, leading new energy vehicle manufacturers, including Customer
A, implement stringent supply chain management practices. Their supplier
onboarding process is protracted, typically including multiple phases of trial
collaborations and extended evaluation periods before a supplier is selected as a
long-term partner. Consequently, partnerships with established long-term
collaborators are generally not replaced or terminated unless a major risk event
occurs. According to the best knowledge of our Directors, there has been no
anticipation of such an incident with Customer A. As of the Latest Practicable
Date, our project backlog attributed to Customer A amounted to RMB148.0
million; and
– 246 –

. Customer A’s ongoing expansion, fueled by global adoption of new energy
vehicles and its positions as a leading industry player, generates sustained demand
for industrial infrastructure. According to the F&S Report, new energy vehicle
sales experienced a significant growth with a CAGR of 71.9% from 2020 to 2024
and will continue to rise to RMB36.6 million units by 2029 with a CAGR of
25.8%. The rapid growth of new energy industry will drive investments in new
manufacturing facilities and upgrades, creating a scalable need for PS building
subcontracting services from Customer A.
Customer concentration is a common characteristic of the industrial sector of the PS
building market, where large-scale industrial construction projects often involve high-value,
multi-phase, or recurring contracts, leading to significant revenue contributions from major
customers. According to the F&S Report, it’s common for companies in the PS building
industry to have a few major customers contributing a significant portion of their total
revenue.
Overall, while our major customers have contributed significantly to our revenue
during the Track Record Period, their presence among our top five customers is reflective of
our ability to secure and execute large-scale projects successfully. At the same time, our
expanding portfolio of new customers and projects in both domestic and overseas markets
underscore the robustness of our customer base and highlights our resilience in navigating
customer concentration risks.
Salient Terms of Typical Agreement with our Customers
PS building subcontracting services
We generally enter into prefabricated steel structure building subcontracting
agreement with the general contractor of our customers on project basis, which our
Directors believe is in line with the general market practice in the PS building industry.
Salient terms of typical subcontracting agreement for our PS building service are
summarized below:
Contract term : Contract term is usually determined based on the scale
and complexity of the construction projects as well as
clients’ requirements.
Scope of work : The agreements normally set out the scope of services to
be carried out by us and other project specifications or
requirements.

Pricing and price : Usually on a fixed total price subject to re-measurement
adjustment basis. The agreements usually specify an estimated
contract sum based on the agreed unit rates and the
estimated measurement of quantities of work completed.
The actual amount of works to be carried out by us is
subject to our customer’s instructions, which may be
different from the original estimated contract sum stated
in the agreements. Our customers will measure the actual
quantities of works executed on site and we will be paid

become payable to us upon expiration of the defect
liability period.

stipulated in the ‘‘bill of quantities’’ for the specific
project. Should any deviation from the bill of quantities,
the contract sum is adjusted to the extent approved by

Maintenance and After-Sales Service
We prioritize high-quality construction standards and maintain a dedicated after-sales
maintenance team to ensure customer satisfaction and long-term structural integrity. In line
with our contractual commitments, we provide maintenance and repair services during a
specified warranty period, addressing defects arising from construction quality or materials
at no additional cost to the client.
Our agreements with customers also outline clear procedures for issue reporting,
response times, and resolution, ensuring efficient and transparent handling of maintenance
requests. This approach provides customers with a reliable and convenient way to report
issues and request repairs, supported by accessible digital platforms.

BUSINESS
SALES AND MARKETING
Our sales and marketing strategy focuses on identifying business opportunities,
building long-term client relationships, and maintaining a strong market presence. Key
responsibilities are handled by the Marketing Center and the Contract and Quotation
Department, which work together to align market outreach, tendering, and client
engagement with our broader strategic goals.
A core aspect of our strategy is leveraging sales personnel with technical expertise,
enabling them to collaborate closely with clients during the sales process to propose tailored
services that address specific project needs. This consultative approach strengthens our
ability to secure contracts and build trust with clients, fostering long-term partnerships.
Our CRM system supports this customer-centric approach by consolidating data from
client interactions, project updates, and feedback into a centralized database. This enables
us to respond swiftly to new opportunities, track ongoing projects, and maintain consistent
engagement with both existing and potential clients. The system also allows us to analyze
past projects and refine proposals based on clients’ evolving needs, ensuring targeted and
reliable support throughout the project lifecycle.
We employ a multifaceted marketing strategy to adapt to changing client and market
demands. Direct client engagement, including seminars with design institutes, enables us to
connect with industry players and identify upcoming project opportunities. International
exhibitions, conventions, and forums enhance our visibility in global markets, where
demand for advanced industrial products and services continues to grow.
PRICING POLICY
Our pricing strategy and process are closely linked to the cost-plus model, ensuring
that fluctuations in raw material costs, particularly steel plate, are reflected directly in our
quotations. To manage price stability and ensure transparency with customers, we include
explicit validity periods in our quotations. Our tendering approach typically involves
preparing a comprehensive bill of quantities that outlines the specific items and tasks
required for project completion. The tender price or quotation for each project is
determined on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the following factors:
. Scope and complexity of the project
. Delivery schedule and urgency
. Estimated costs of raw materials, particularly steel plate, and equipment leasing
. Subcontracting and labor costs associated with the project
. Historical price trends and fluctuations in key cost items
. Pricing trends for comparable projects
. Competitive strategies of other bidders
– 252 –

=== PAGE 263 ===
BUSINESS
. Payment terms and financial flexibility offered by the customer
The final pricing proposal is prepared by our Contract and Quotation Department and
Business Management Center and reviewed by senior management to ensure alignment with
our financial objectives and strategic priorities.
This structured pricing approach allows us to maintain our competitive edge while
delivering value to our customers. By integrating effective cost management practices, such
as price-locking and price adjustment clauses, we ensure that our projects remain
sustainable even amid fluctuating steel market conditions.
Price Adjustment
To ensure fairness and stability in the execution of long-duration contracts, we may
implement a structured price adjustment mechanism designed to address fluctuations in the
cost of raw materials, particularly steel plate. Upon signing a contract, we promptly secure
upstream pricing for key materials to lock in costs and safeguard profit margins. This
proactive approach minimizes our exposure to immediate market volatility, providing
predictability and stability for both parties.
For contracts spanning extended durations, the settlement price may be adjusted to
reflect significant changes in material costs. Specifically, if the market price of steel plate or
other essential materials increases by more than a certain percentage number (generally 2%)
compared to the baseline price agreed upon at contract execution, an adjustment may be
applied. Adjustments are usually calculated based on verifiable market indices or mutually
agreed benchmarks, ensuring transparency and mutual understanding. Regular reviews of
material cost trends are conducted, and adjustment requests should be supported by
credible evidence to facilitate fair and objective implementation. By aligning financial
outcomes with market dynamics, we foster sustainable contract execution and mutual trust.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had not
exercised the price adjustment mechanism, primarily because the price of raw materials was
on a downward trend. According to the F&S report, the price of the raw material declined
by 13.2%, 10.4%, 13.1% and 0.15%, in 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30,
2025, respectively.

To ensure quality and reliability across all aspects of our supply chain, we have
established a structured supplier selection and management program governed by rigorous
assessment standards.

BUSINESS
Raw Material Suppliers
Raw materials constitute the largest portion of our cost structure, primarily including
steel plate materials, coating materials, fasteners, insulation, and equipment essential for
our projects. These materials are sourced from approved suppliers to maintain high
standards of quality and supply consistency. During the Track Record Period, our raw
materials were predominately sourced from suppliers in the PRC.
To mitigate the impact of market volatility in raw material costs, particularly for steel
plate, we conduct regular market analysis meetings, closely tracking price trends and
adjusting our procurement strategies as needed. When necessary, we secure favorable rates
through prepayment agreements, allowing us to lock in costs without renegotiating prices
directly with suppliers. This approach enables us to maintain cost stability without
engaging in direct price adjustments with our suppliers.
Our raw material purchase agreements are primarily structured on a project-by-project
basis, while we also enter into annual purchase agreements with certain raw material
supplier(s) having long-term business relationship with us.
Salient terms of typical purchase agreements for principal raw materials during the
Track Record Period are summarized below:
Pricing : Agreed pricing includes all associated costs, such as
production, packaging, and delivery.
Minimum purchase : Annual purchase agreements usually stipulate a specific
amount annual minimum purchase amount of us.
Delivery, inspection : Suppliers arrange transportation to designated delivery
and acceptance points, either our production facilities or directly to
project sites. Delivery timelines and logistics are
confirmed through purchase orders and additional
written notifications from us. Upon delivery, materials
undergo inspection for specification compliance, with
suppliers responsible for rectifying any issues or costs of
replacement.
Technical requirements : All raw materials must meet national standards and our
and quality assurance specific technical requirements (e.g., GB/T standards for
steel structures). Suppliers provide quality certification,
including third-party testing reports if requested.
Materials must be securely packaged and clearly
labeled with origin, batch number, and specifications.

Payment terms : Payments generally follow a prepayment structure with
an advance paid upon contract signing and invoice
issuance, and the remaining payable post-delivery upon
preliminary acceptance of goods and receipt of a full
VAT invoice.
Breach of contract and : Provisions include penalties for non-compliance:
penalties suppliers must replace goods or provide compensation
if materials fail to meet quality or specification
standards.
Inventory management and storage solutions
Our inventory management is designed to balance project demands with storage
efficiency, ensuring materials are available as needed while avoiding unnecessary stock
accumulation. We operate warehouses in our production facilities in the PRC, which serve
as central storage for our raw materials and finished goods. In addition to our own
facilities, we strategically collaborate with suppliers to utilize their warehouse capacities.
This arrangement enables us to store materials at supplier sites, reducing our direct
warehousing responsibilities and optimizing logistics. For instance, under specific
agreements, certain suppliers provide us complimentary storage for a limited time, after
which storage fees apply only if the materials remain on-site. This flexible approach allows
us to minimize warehousing costs and streamline inventory access without taking on
additional management or operational burdens.
Our inventory management protocols emphasize precise intake, storage, issuance, and
tracking, all managed through our ERP system for real-time visibility and control.
Materials are meticulously inspected upon arrival, with details recorded in the system to
ensure alignment between physical stock and digital records. To uphold accuracy, we
conduct monthly inventory counts covering select inventory and perform an annual
comprehensive inventory audit. Any discrepancies identified during these reviews are
promptly addressed to maintain consistent inventory data.
Given the project-driven nature of our operations, we do not maintain high inventory
levels. Inventory turnover is closely aligned with project progress, and stock levels fluctuate
according to specific project timelines. Our inventory turnover days for the years ended
December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2025, were approximately
24 days, 25 days, 23 days and 17 days, respectively. This approach to inventory
management ensures that we maintain operational efficiency while meeting the unique
demands of each project.

Labor Subcontracting
Our labor subcontractors are mainly responsible for executing specific installation
tasks according to work orders issued by us. During the Track Record Period, all of the
on-site installation work of our projects in the PRC and overseas were performed by labor
subcontractors. For the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months
ended June 30, 2024 and 2025, our total subcontracting costs, mainly formed of labor
subcontracting costs, amounted to approximately RMB307.8 million, RMB250.7 million,
RMB273.7 million, RMB68.0 million and RMB271.6 million, respectively. These figures
represented approximately 18.5%, 20.2%, 20.5%, 15.1% and 21.2% of our total cost of
sales for the respective periods.
The following are the key terms typically included in our subcontracting agreements
with labor subcontractors, ensuring clarity in the responsibilities and expectations for both
parties:
Responsibilities : Our Group are primarily responsible for PS building
components supply, quality control and project
management, including providing installation drawings
and instructions. We also have site manager in charge of
task supervision, monitoring the quality of incoming
materials and supervising on-site material installation
progress and personnel safety on a daily basis.
Our subcontractors are responsible for completing
specified installation tasks based on instructions
stipulated in the signed contract. These tasks must
adhere to our technical requirements and project
timelines.
Quality and safety : Subcontractors must comply with our stringent quality
and safety standards. We provide pre-job training, safety
manuals, and on-site engineering support to ensure that
all work is performed according to our technical
specifications. Safety audits are performed periodically
to ensure compliance.
Work supervision : Our on-site supervisors monitor the subcontractors’
work, conducting daily checks and progress reports to
ensure that project timelines and quality standards are
met. We take prompt action to address and correct any
deviation by subcontractors from the agreed-upon
schedule or standards.

BUSINESS
Outsourced Product Providers
During the Track Record Period, we primarily outsourced a portion of our production
of primary structure components to third-party providers according to our design and
specifications. These components primarily include beams, columns, custom architectural
elements and other primary structure components. These elements form the critical
load-bearing framework of our projects and provide support for specific functions required
by our customers per each project. Our strategic approach for the outsourcing production
of primary structure components for a PS building subcontracting project is well-defined
based on the following considerations:
Production capacity constraints. Our current production capabilities are insufficient to
meet client demands for PS building subcontracting projects. During the Track Record
Period, we delivered a total of approximately 530,000 tons of PS building components
across all projects, with approximately 206,000 tons manufactured in-house and the
remaining outsourced to outsourced product providers. Our utilization rate for our PS
building components reached 158.7% for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Engaging
external outsourced product providers allows us to scale our project capacity while
maintaining operational efficiency.
In-house design capacities. The design of the primary structure components is critical to
the integrity of a PS building subcontracting project. They need to be meticulously
engineered, using specialized design software, material performance data, and
industry-specific knowledge of scenarios and best practices to ensure they can effectively
support the entire PS building structure. By retaining in-house design capabilities, we
ensure that this critical task is executed by our team, whose expertise aligns with the
high-standard design requirement. According to F&S, in the industrial sector of PS building
market, typical construction subcontractors usually lack such design capabilities. A project
owner usually needs to engage professional third-party design firms to furnish the design
services. Leveraging our expertise, we have demonstrated to the industry our ability to
undertake the design phase of a PS building subcontracting project.
Standardized manufacturing process. Compared to the design complexity, the
manufacturing of primary structure components is rather standardized. These processes,
which involve cutting the steel plates into appropriate sizes, assembling them into the
desired shapes, wielding, and conducting surface treatment, are relatively straightforward.
In fact, this part of the processing only requires the subcontractor to use precision
machinery and strictly follow the design drawings provided by us. As long as the
subcontractor adheres to the established standards and procedures, high-quality products
can be achieved. This simplicity makes it feasible to outsource the production to external
partners.
Rigorous quality assurance. To ensure the production quality, we deploy a dedicated
on-site supervision team. They closely monitor the subcontractor’s production process at
every stage on a daily basis, from the initial steel plate cutting to the final surface treatment.
This real-time supervision allows us to promptly identify and address any potential issues.
– 261 –

=== PAGE 272 ===
BUSINESS
Once the components are produced, we conduct comprehensive product inspections in
accordance with our strict quality control procedures. Only components that pass our
rigorous inspection are approved for delivery to the project site.
Logistics consideration. As the primary structure components are large and heavy, they
generally result in high transportation costs. For instance, a single steel beam used in a
medium-sized industrial building can be several meters and weigh several tons.
Transporting these components demands the use of specialized heavy-haul trucks, which
have higher operating costs compared to normal containers or bulk cargos.
Strategic outsourcing benefits. Outsourcing enables holistic decision-making based on
project location, client specifications, and internal production scheduling priorities. This
operational flexibility allows us to concentrate resources on higher value-added phase, such
as project design optimization. For the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the
six months ended June 30, 2025, the outsourcing ratio was approximately 54.5%, 60.5%,
56.9% and 67.5%, respectively.
We generally select reliable outsourced product providers in close proximity to the
project construction site. By doing so, we can ensure that the primary structure components
are produced in strict accordance with our designs and drawings. These components can
then be directly transported to the project site, thereby significantly reducing transportation
expenses and minimizing our upfront capital investment in establishing a production
facility. We outsourced approximately 82,000 tons, 75,000 tons, 75,000 tons and 92,000 tons
of PS building components from 46, 45, 36 and 35 outsourced product providers for the
years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2025,
respectively. All outsourced product providers during the Track Record Period were
Independent Third Parties. Since the costs paid to outsourced product providers are
significantly attributed to the costs of steel plates, such costs were accounted for as the
material costs under the cost of sales in our financial statements. For the years ended
December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2025, our outsourcing
costs accounted for as the material cost under the cost of sales amounted to RMB517.5
million, RMB350.2 million, RMB372.9 million and RMB535.3 million, respectively. By
combining our in-house expertise with carefully managed outsourcing, we scale production
to align with project demands, ensuring high-quality and cost-effective component delivery.
Our production facility in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province is capable of producing the
primary structure components. When the project site is relatively close to our production
facility, we will produce the primary structure components in-house and use third party
logistic services to transport them to the project site. This approach allows us to better
balance production costs, quality control, and transportation efficiency based on the
specific circumstances of each project.

BUSINESS
Delivery : Outsourced product providers are usually responsible for
arranging timely delivery of products to our project sites.
In case of late delivery, we are entitled with right to
charge them with a penalty and any continuous late
delivery may entitle us with right to terminate the
contract.
Inspection : Inspection is conducted upon delivery of outsourced
products to project sites to verify conformity with
project specifications. Any identified defects are rectified
by the outsourced providers at their expense, ensuring our
high-quality standards are consistently upheld.
Outsourcing is not a simple delegation of tasks; it is a collaborative process and
constitutes a critical component within our PS building operations. To ensure that the
primary structure components in outsourced production fully satisfy the requirements of
our PS building subcontracting project, we assume substantial responsibilities throughout
the entire outsourcing process, as detailed below:
. Provide detailed designs and drawings: to ensure that outsourced product providers
manufacture strictly in accordance with our designs, we will provide highly
detailed design drawings, including detailed design parameters and technical
specifications.
. Conduct raw material inspection: prior to the commencement of the outsourced
production, we carry strict inspections of all incoming raw materials, primarily
the steel plates. By ensuring the quality of raw materials, we lay a solid foundation
for the production of high-quality primary structure components.
. Provide on-site supervision and technical support: to ensure the production quality,
we deploy a dedicated on-site supervision team. They closely monitor the
subcontractor’s production process at every stage, from the initial steel plate
cutting to the final surface treatment. This real-time supervision allows us to
promptly identify and address any potential issues.
. Conduct inspection at production facility: once the components are produced, we
conduct comprehensive product inspections in accordance with our strict quality
control procedures. Only components that pass our rigorous inspection are
approved for delivery to the project site.
. Conduct final product acceptance at project site: upon the arrival of the outsourced
primary structure components at the project site, we perform a final product
acceptance. This involves a comprehensive review of all components, checking for
any damage during transportation, verifying the proper assembly of components,
and conducting performance tests if necessary. This final inspection step serves as
the last line of quality control, ensuring that the products meet all the
requirements for installation at the project site.

. Control the project schedule: we develop a comprehensive and detailed project
schedule that encompasses both the production timeline and the transportation
schedule. We set clear milestones for our outsourced product providers in respect
of both production and delivery to ensure the outsourced production satisfies the
schedule of the overall PS building subcontracting project.

IMPACT OF U.S. TARIFF MEASURES
The United States has in recent years implemented a series of trade measures, including
the imposition and escalation of tariffs under Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act of 1974 and
Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962. In particular, in March 2025, the U.S.
government announced an additional 25% tariff on various categories of steel products,
followed by further policy actions in April 2025 and a temporary suspension of certain prior
tariff measures. In May 2025, after their trade meeting in Geneva, the Chinese and the U.S.
government released a joint statement announcing, among others, the removal of the 91%
tariff announced in April 2025 and a 90-day pause, leading the effective tariffs on imports
from China to 30%, down from 145%; and China will reduce tariff imposed on imports
from the U.S. since April 2, 2025 to 10%, down from 125%. In August 2025, the United
States announced to extend the suspension of tariffs on China for another 90 days. In
October 2025, the US authorities announced an escalation of tariff measures against
imports from China. Pursuant to such announcement, an additional 100% tariff will be
imposed on all PRC-origin goods exported to the US with effect from November 1, 2025.
However, a new round of economic and trade consultations was held in Malaysia during
October 25 and 26, 2025 between the U.S. and China. The U.S. and China reached a ‘‘very
substantive framework agreement,’’ under which the U.S. will no longer consider imposing
an additional 100% tariff on Chinese goods. As advised by PRC Legal Advisers, the latest
applicable tariff imposed by U.S. on Chinese imports primarily include: (i) 20% of general
tariff; and (ii) 50% tariff on the value of the steel and aluminum components in the steel
products. These developments have heightened geopolitical uncertainty and prompted
retaliatory trade measures from other economies, including China, the European Union,
Japan and South Korea.
Our Directors are of the view that our overseas markets are not materially impacted
directly or indirectly by the geopolitical tension, having considered the following:
. Our direct sales to the U.S. market have been limited. During the Track Record
Period, all of our sales to the United States came from sales of industrial
environmental equipment and revenue we recorded only accounted for
approximately 1.6%, 3.6%, 4.4%, 4.5% and 2.0% of our total revenue for the
years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30,
2024 and 2025, respectively. Under our typical sales agreements, transactions are
conducted on a FOB basis. This means that our U.S. customers are responsible
for arranging transportation and bearing associated costs, including any potential
tariff expenses. As such, we have effectively transferred tariff-related financial
risks to customers, minimizing direct financial impacts on our revenue and profit
margins.

. To the best knowledge of us, none of our major customers during the Track

LOGISTICS ARRANGEMENT
We generally engage third-party logistics service providers for the transportation of
our products to the relevant project sites or to our customers. We work closely with those
logistics service providers to coordinate delivery schedules, optimizing the timing and
efficiency of shipments to align with project milestones.
For our domestic projects, we handle the transportation in two ways. For our
self-manufactured PS building components, we typically engage logistics service provider
for road transportation from our production facilities to the relevant project sites. In
contrast, for outsourced PS building components, the outsourced product providers are
usually responsible for transporting those components directly to the project site. For our
overseas projects, the outsourced PS building components are usually transported by the
outsourced product provider to our production facilities. Generally, we are then responsible
for the delivery of those components, together with self-manufactured PS building
components, to the relevant project sites overseas. We typically contract logistics service
provider for the transportation of those components, which involves both domestic
container land transportation and sea transportation (including both container shipping
and bulk cargo). For our sale of industrial environmental equipment, the customers are
usually responsible for the transportation of products from our production facilities to the
project sites overseas.
Salient terms of our typical logistic contracts with third-party logistics service
providers are summarized below:
Contract term : The duration of the contract is typically determined
based on the scope of services and the transportation
requirements of each project or order. Contracts may be
signed on a per-project basis or as annual service
agreements with renewal options.
Scope of services : Transportation in the PRC: transporting products from
our production facilities to the designated construction
site through road transportation.
Transportation overseas: transporting products from our
production facilities to the designated harbor and
handling cross-border shipments, including export
procedures, customs clearances, insurance, and final
delivery to the constructions sites overseas.

WORK SAFETY
We prioritize occupational health and safety as an essential component of operational
integrity across all project sites and production facilities. We have implemented a
comprehensive work safety management system to provide a secure and compliant work
environment. Through proactive policies, safety training, and continuous monitoring, we
aim to minimize occupational hazards and promote a culture of safety awareness.

=== PAGE 287 ===
BUSINESS
Safety Management System and Training Programs
To ensure robust workplace safety, we have established detailed safety procedures and
training programs that cover various aspects of risk prevention and emergency response.
These measures are consistently enforced at both production facilities and construction
sites.
. Safety policies and compliance: Our safety management system adheres to the
PRC’s Work Safety Law and other relevant national regulations, ensuring that
our operations comply with all statutory requirements. A dedicated safety team is
responsible for monitoring compliance with these standards, under the direction
of a senior management representative. This team also reviews and updates our
safety protocols regularly to align with industry best practices and regulatory
changes.
. Training and induction: All new employees, including subcontractors, undergo a
mandatory safety induction program that covers machinery operation, hazard
identification, and emergency protocols. During the Track Record Period, we
have conducted more than 1,500 hours of safety training, underscoring our
commitment to thorough safety preparation. Additionally, periodic refresher
courses ensure that all personnel stay updated on safety procedures, especially
when new risks or operational changes are introduced. Training programs are
tailored to each site’s specific requirements, with specialized courses offered for
high-risk tasks to enhance safety awareness and skills.
. Risk assessments and preventative measures: Before commencing any project, our
safety officers conduct thorough risk assessments to identify and mitigate
potential hazards. These assessments guide the development of site-specific
safety plans, including safety equipment requirements, proper handling
procedures, and emergency response strategies. Regular safety audits and
reviews ensure that these measures remain effective throughout the project
lifecycle.
. Safety equipment and monitoring: All personnel are provided with personal
protective equipment specific to their roles, including helmets, gloves, safety
harnesses, and other essential gear. At production facilities and construction sites,
clear safety signage highlights hazard zones and machinery handling instructions.
Safety officers conduct routine inspections to verify compliance with equipment
usage, site protocols, and operational safety standards, documenting findings and
recommending improvements as needed.

=== PAGE 288 ===
BUSINESS
Incident Reporting and Investigation
Our Group has implemented a standardized protocol for reporting and handling
workplace accidents. In the event of an incident, immediate reporting is required to ensure
timely and coordinated response efforts.
. Immediate reporting and response: All injuries or safety incidents are reported
promptly to the designated safety officer, who logs critical details and initiates an
incident response plan. If necessary, emergency services are mobilized, and the site
is secured to prevent further risks.
. Investigation and corrective measures: Following an incident, an in-depth
investigation is conducted to determine root causes. Our safety and
management teams review the findings to identify necessary corrective measures
and implement strategies to prevent recurrence. Any significant incidents are
reviewed at the executive level to reinforce accountability and improve safety
oversight.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, our Group had
not recorded any significant safety violations or workplace accidents resulting in severe
injuries or fatalities. However, a fatal accident occurred on November 6, 2021, at one of our
project sites in Guangdong Province, with administrative penalties imposed within the
Track Record Period.
The November 2021 accident
On November 6, 2021, at one of our project sites in Zhanjiang, Guangdong Province,
an accident occurred. A worker hired by our labor subcontractor fell to their death after
detaching the safety harness from the lifeline, a violation of established safety protocols.
Following the incident, the Zhanjiang Economic and Technological Development Zone
Emergency Management Bureau (湛江經濟技術開發區應急管理局) (the ‘‘Authority’’)
conducted a thorough investigation. The Authority’s findings concluded that the accident
resulted from two main factors:
. Direct cause: The immediate cause of the accident was the worker’s unauthorized
removal of the safety harness, which directly breached the safety protocols in
place.
. Indirect cause: The investigation also revealed deficiencies in oversight.
Specifically, our on-site safety personnel failed to enforce strict adherence to
safety protocols, and the project team leader did not adequately supervise the
worksite, leading to further lapses in safety enforcement.
– 278 –

=== PAGE 289 ===
BUSINESS
According to the Work Safety Law of the People’s Republic of China (中華人民共和國
安全生產法) (‘‘Work Safety Law’’), all entities engaged in production and business activities
within the PRC are subject to this law, who are legally responsible for workplace safety at
construction sites. In accordance with the Work Safety Law, our Group is legally
responsible for ensuring workplace safety at the construction site. Meanwhile, according to
the Measures for the Administration of Construction Subcontracting of Building and
Municipal Infrastructure Construction Projects《( 房屋建築和市政基礎設施工程施工分包管
理辦法》) (‘‘Construction Projects Measures’’), the contractor of subcontracted projects is
responsible for the safety of the construction site and shall manage the safety production of
the subcontractor. In accordance with the Work Safety Law and the Construction Projects
Measures, our Group, who has subcontracted the labor services to the subcontractor, is
subject to administrative responsibilities. Notwithstanding the contractual clauses with our
labor subcontractor purporting to exclude our liability for any issues arising from the
subcontractor’s workforce management, such indemnification provisions cannot discharge
us of our statutory oversight obligations under the Work Safety Law and the Construction
Projects Measures.
On August 15, 2022, the Authority classified the incident as a ‘‘general accident (一般
安全事故)’’ under the Work Safety Law, which is the least severe category under the
relevant laws and regulations. In line with this, an administrative penalty of RMB530,000
was imposed on our corresponding subsidiary. Furthermore, the Authority issued
administrative penalties to two of our senior management members, Mr. Zhu Lezhong
and Mr. Hong Shanzao, in the amounts of RMB67,368 and RMB34,402, respectively. The
aforementioned penalties have been fully paid by Mr. Zhu, Mr. Hong and us, respectively.
As advised by our PRC Legal Advisers, the incident did not have a material and adverse
impact on our production and business operations.
After the accident, the subcontractor assumed full liability for compensating the
deceased worker’s family, and we were not held accountable for any portion of the
settlement. Under the terms of our labor subcontracting agreement, we were entitled to
claim indemnification from the subcontractor for the fines imposed on us. However,
following negotiations with the subcontractor and considering our longstanding
cooperative relationship as well as the project’s ongoing operation requirement, we
determined not to pursue any financial compensation from the subcontractor for the
penalties incurred.
– 279 –

=== PAGE 290 ===
BUSINESS
In response to this incident, we immediately took corrective actions to strengthen our
safety oversight:
. Strengthened safety protocols and supervision: We refined our safety protocols to
reinforce compliance with mandatory safety equipment usage, specifically
addressing harness and lifeline requirements.
. Enhanced training programs: Targeted safety training sessions have been
implemented for all personnel at high-risk sites, with emphasis on PPE usage
and safety procedures for working at heights. These sessions are now mandatory
for all workers and site supervisors.
. Regular safety audits and compliance monitoring: We have introduced weekly
safety audits and compliance checks at all high-risk project sites. Site managers
are now required to submit safety reports online, on a daily basis, which are
reviewed by the risk management team to ensure timely corrective actions.
Our Directors, in consultation with our PRC Legal Advisers, have concluded that the

management practices. As advised by our PRC Legal Advisers, during the Track Record

received any administrative penalties related to work safety that would materially affect its
compliance with applicable safety laws and regulations.

. Incident reporting and communication: Any serious incident triggers immediate

response strategies and to reinforce preventative practices.

range of the weighted average full-cost mark-up rate for comparable companies (i) during
the three-year period from 2021 to 2023 was 1.99% to 7.27%, with a median value of
3.38%. The full-cost mark-up rate of USAS Suzhou in 2024 was 3.43%, which fell within
the inter-quartile range; and (ii) during the three-year period from 2022 to 2024 was 2.05%
to 4.56%, with a median value of 3.32%. The full-cost mark-up rate of USAS Suzhou for
the six months ended June 30, 2025 was 3.34%, which fell within the inter-quartile range.
Therefore, the Transfer Pricing Consultant concluded that the transfer pricing of our
intra-group transactions in 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2025 complied with the
arm’s length principle.
IMPACT OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted global industries, including the PS building
market, with supply chain interruptions, labor shortages, and production delays. Our
operations in the PRC were minimally impacted due to robust supplier relationships that
ensured a steady supply of materials and the strategic location of our projects in industrial
zones, which were less affected by travel restrictions. This stability allowed us to maintain
construction schedules and meet customer expectations without major disruptions, even
during the height of the pandemic. Internationally, while regional restrictions required
some project adjustments, our resource reallocation and adaptability demonstrated our
operational flexibility. Strong relationships with key customers also provided resilience, as
they continued awarding us new projects despite global uncertainty, ensuring a steady
business pipeline throughout the pandemic. In 2022, due to international travel restrictions,
the overseas demand for our industrial environmental equipment declined. As a result, the
revenue from our industrial environmental equipment in 2022 was RMB31.8 million. After
the pandemic situation improved in 2023, the revenue of our industrial environmental
equipment business category rebounded to RMB69.4 million.

Key Proprietary Technologies
Our technology portfolio focuses on delivering advanced PS building subcontracting
services with precision, durability, and adaptability to complex customer needs. Below is an
overview of our core proprietary technologies, each tailored to support robust performance
across a variety of applications.
PS building system product design and integration technology
Our comprehensive range of PS building components, including primary structures,
secondary structures, enclosure systems, and accessories, is supported by advanced
structural and detailed design technologies. With a proprietary database of nearly a
thousand standardized structural detail nodes, we ensure seamless integration of these
components to meet diverse building requirements. This systematic approach enhances the
quality and efficiency of design, production, and construction.
Patented products and technologies
We have registered a number of patents that form the foundation of our proprietary
technical portfolio, reinforcing our competitiveness in the industry. Key examples include:
. LS-III Standing Seam Roof System (LS-Ⅲ直立鎖縫屋面系統): Featuring 12
patents, this system meets the national Class 1 waterproof standard and FM1–315
wind uplift certification. Our associated photovoltaic roofing system, namely the
BIPV systems which combines our LS-III roof with integrated solar modules,
supports on-site power generation for distributed energy systems and owns three
additional patents.
– 287 –

=== PAGE 298 ===
BUSINESS
. Curvet Dual-Wave Arch Warehouse Series (Curvet雙波拱形倉系列產品): With
five patents registered, this high-performance storage facility for root crops like
potatoes is energy-efficient and addresses gaps in the PS building applications of
agricultural storage.
. V-Shaped Pulse Dust Removal Equipment and Technology (V型脈衝除塵裝備產
品與技術): Offering superior dust removal efficiency, enhanced self-cleaning
capabilities, extended lifespan, and reduced costs. Several related patents are
under application.
3D modeling and pre-punching technology
Our pre-design and 3D modeling capabilities enable a factory-based pre-punching
process for primary and secondary structure components. This innovation minimizes
on-site welding, improves assembly efficiency, and enhances installation precision, ensuring
high-quality outcomes.
Systematic PS building construction process and technologies
We owned four invention patents in PS building construction and have developed
standardized construction techniques, installation procedures, and quality management
processes. Notably, our Overall Lifting Method for the Roof Structure of Portal Frame
Prefabricated Steel Structure Factory Buildings (門式鋼架鋼結構廠房屋面主體結構整體吊
裝工法) received the Shanghai Municipal Engineering Methodology Award for 2014.
Information technology systems
To support our PS building operations, we have integrated, customized and upgraded
the ERP system, combining technical and management software into this unified platform.
This customized system ensures real-time, effective control over all operational processes,
enhancing overall efficiency and productivity.
Collaborative Research and Development Projects

academic institutions, research organizations, and industry partners to commit ourselves to
the technological advancements. These partnerships grant us access to research and allow us
to leverage external expertise to complement our own capabilities.

Baosteel cooperation
In partnership with Baosteel, a longstanding supplier, we have advanced the
application of high-strength duplex steel within our LS-III roofing system. This
collaboration, formalized under the Meilian-Baosteel High-Performance Steel Building
Joint Laboratory, focused on researching the wind resistance of LS-III roofs using

Tongji University partnership
In collaboration with Tongji University, we have developed a calculation method and

further developed to our Curvet Dual-Wave Arch Warehouse Series (Curvet 雙波拱形倉系

RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROLS
Effective risk management and robust internal controls are fundamental to our
operations. Our framework addresses the diverse risks associated with our project-driven
business model, covering areas such as contractual risk, operational risk, project-based risk,
and regulatory compliance. This approach ensures that we not only safeguard our assets
and operations but also maintain a proactive stance toward long-term business resilience.
Risk Management
We have implemented a comprehensive risk management framework supported by
internal guidelines, policies, and procedures designed to mitigate risks across our
operations. Our Directors and senior management oversee the formulation and execution
of these measures, ensuring the effectiveness of our internal controls and compliance with
applicable laws and regulations.
– 293 –

=== PAGE 304 ===
BUSINESS
The following sets out the key measures under our risk management and internal
control systems:
Regulatory and environmental compliance
We actively monitor and adapt to legal and regulatory changes affecting our business.
Regular audits and reviews are conducted to ensure that our operations align with PRC
laws and international standards. Our compliance efforts are supported by an
environmental management system focused on meeting legal and regulatory requirements,
minimizing waste, and promoting efficient resource use in production processes. Employees
and subcontractors receive regular training on environmental protocols and industry
standards, reinforcing a company-wide commitment to ethical and compliant practices.
During the Track Record Period, we incurred costs related to compliance with
environmental standards and experienced no material violations of applicable laws or
regulations.
Contractual risk management
As an integrated PS building subcontracting service provider, we emphasize managing
risks in commercial contracts. Each project undergoes a structured contractual risk
assessment, including clear limitations on liability for breaches. Our Legal Center ensures
contracts are carefully drafted, negotiated, and updated to reflect regulatory changes, legal
precedents, and specific project needs. This continuous review process helps us maintain
balanced risk exposure and align our practices with industry standards.
Project-based risk management
Operating in diverse geographical markets exposes us to varying regulatory, financial,
and operational risks. We conduct thorough assessments of local policies, regulatory
frameworks, and market conditions before entering new regions. When necessary, we
collaborate with local partners or establish joint ventures to navigate complex
environments, expedite project timelines, and leverage regional expertise. This approach
ensures compliance with local laws and effective risk mitigation.
Financial and credit risk management
Our financial risk management framework is designed to monitor project payment
schedules, control credit exposure, and safeguard liquidity. Payment schedules are tied to
key project milestones and strictly enforced to minimize late payments. In cases of delayed
payments, we reserve the right to suspend work to protect financial stability and cash flow.
These measures ensure our operations remain resilient and financially secure.

Among the ongoing legal proceedings, one arbitration of which we were the defendant
involves a contract dispute with a relatively significant financial implication. On May 28,
2019, we entered into a construction engineering subcontract agreement with certain
furniture retailer based in Jilin Province (‘‘Retailer X’’) for a fixed lump-sum project priced
at approximately RMB38.0 million. We received an advance payment of RMB19.0 million,
and the project commenced as scheduled. However, in June 2020, Retailer X unilaterally
instructed us to halt the project and insisted on suspending any resumption attempts.
According to the correspondence between Retailer X and us, Retailer X raised concerns
over the unpredictability of the project because they were worried about the government
policy might be changed due to COVID-19’s impact. Despite our communication efforts,
Retailer X insisted on suspending the project. Discussions to resume construction were held
in August 2022 but failed to result in an agreement due to significant corrosion on steel
components at the construction site, which arose because the general contractor failed to
maintain the project site during the suspension period. Given the substantial costs
associated with rehabilitating the corroded structure and the necessity of conducting
comprehensive tests to validate the components’ fitness for reuse post-rust removal,
Retailer X and us were unable to reach a consensus on the repair management plan,
timeline, or cost allocation.

BUSINESS
On May 12, 2023, the Retailer X initiated an arbitration against us with the Shanghai
International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission (上海國際經濟貿易仲裁委員會)
(‘‘Arbitration Committee’’), alleging contract disputes and seeking relief of approximately
RMB22.3 million. On June 30, 2023, the Shanghai Songjiang District People’s Court, at the
request of the claimant, froze approximately RMB22.3 million of our bank deposits as a
provisional measure. On September 19, 2023, we filed a counterclaim in the arbitration. As
of December 31, 2023, contract liabilities of RMB9.4 million was reclassified into other
payables in view of the termination of contract with Retailer X. As of the Latest Practicable
Date, the arbitration was still pending, with no final resolution or ruling issued. As advised
by PRC Legal Advisers, and confirmed by our Directors, the likelihood of the outcome of
the abovementioned legal proceeding materially and adversely affecting our production and
business operations is relatively small, having considered that (i) the amount in dispute was
relatively low, accounting for less than 2% of our revenue for the year ended December 31,
2024; and (ii) after reviewing the counterclaim application and supporting evidence
submitted by us to the arbitration, our PRC Legal Advisers are of the opinion that we did
not breach the relevant agreement as alleged by Retailer X. Based on the PRC Legal
Advisers’ opinion, our Directors assessed the likelihood of economic benefit outflows from
this dispute as remote. As such, we have not made any provisions with respect of this
on-going legal proceeding.
Our Directors confirm that during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest

– 301 –

=== PAGE 312 ===
BUSINESS
Environmental Sustainability
We are committed to achieving our green building vision by integrating low-carbon
design, resource-efficient construction methods and standardized environmental
management into our operations. In terms of specific technical and material advantages,
we further leverage the intrinsic environmental benefits of PS structure. Steel is a fully
recyclable material, and the structural steel products used by us can achieve a recycling rate
of nearly 100% because steel, as a metallic alloy, can be recovered and remelted into new
steel materials without loss of mechanical properties. Accordingly, PS structure
components can be entirely reclaimed and reprocessed upon the demolition of a building,
significantly reducing construction waste and life-cycle material consumption compared
with traditional reinforced concrete structures. The adoption of recyclable materials is also
an important criterion under major international and PRC green building evaluation
standards, contributing to the overall sustainability performance of steel-structure
buildings. In addition, steel-structure construction allows for higher prefabrication ratios,
which reduces on-site wet operations and lowers energy use and emissions during
construction, collectively forming a strong foundation for us to deliver green and
low-carbon building services.
Our procurement of primary steel is not for direct use in construction projects but for
processing into PS structures, which are then supplied to such projects. The processing of
primary steel into PS structure does not involve heavy manufacturing or metallurgical
operations, nor does it adopt hot-rolling procedures that typically result in significant
carbon emissions and environmental impacts. Instead, we utilize cold-forming processes,
the core energy consumption of which relates to purchased electricity and does not generate
direct greenhouse gas emissions during processing. In addition, our processing facilities are
equipped with distributed photovoltaic systems, further reducing the carbon intensity of
our operations and supporting a more sustainable production model. From a regulatory
compliance perspective, only our primary structural processing lines are required to obtain
environmental impact assessment approval and we have received such approval in 2016.
We embed environmental stewardship into our business operations, aiming to
minimize ecological impacts through energy efficiency, waste reduction, and compliance
with the PRC’s Environmental Protection Law and other relevant regulations. For the years
ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30, 2024 and 2025,
costs incurred for environmental compliance by us amounted to approximately
RMB84,400, RMB93,500, RMB108,800, RMB59,200 and RMB66,200, respectively.
