BUSINESS
Governance framework
Our governance structure is built to ensure accountability, transparency, and the
effective implementation of ESG initiatives. The Board of Directors has the ultimate
responsibility for overseeing all ESG activities and aligning them with our strategic
objectives. To support the Board, we have established an ESG Committee that drives policy
development, monitors performance, and ensures compliance with relevant regulations.
This committee collaborates with department heads and external consultants to identify
ESG risks and opportunities, ensuring a comprehensive approach to sustainable
development.
Our governance framework is further strengthened by an internal ESG Working
Group, which serves as a bridge between the Board and operational teams. The working
group coordinates the implementation of ESG initiatives, tracks progress against defined
KPIs, and provides regular updates to the ESG Committee. To enhance transparency, we
have adopted clear reporting mechanisms, ensuring stakeholders are informed of our ESG
efforts and outcomes. These processes are supported by robust internal controls, which are
regularly audited to uphold governance integrity.
We also emphasize stakeholder engagement within our governance structure. Through
regular dialog with investors, employees, customers, and other key stakeholders, we ensure
that our ESG policies address their concerns and expectations. This collaborative approach
enhances our ability to adapt to evolving market and regulatory demands while maintaining
trust and accountability across all stakeholder groups.
Professional ethics and anti-corruption
In terms of professional ethics and anti-corruption in corporate governance, we strictly
comply with relevant laws and regulations, including the Criminal Law of the People’s
Republic of China, the Company Law of the People’s Republic of China, and the
Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People’s Republic of China, strictly prohibiting the
occurrence of incidents such as bribery, extortion, fraud, and money-laundering.
We have established comprehensive policies to prevent the occurrence of illegal
behaviors such as bribery, extortion, fraud, and money-laundering, including rules and
procedures for Board meetings, terms of reference of the senior management, and articles of
association. Those policies clearly stipulate that employees must not engage in any form of
corrupt behavior. For example, they must not directly or indirectly accept rebates, cash,
physical goods, securities, gift vouchers, and other items of value provided by companies
that have business relationships with us, or participate in travel, high-end banquets, and
other activities provided by such companies, which may affect the impartiality of their duty
performance.

BUSINESS
In order to further strengthen internal control and ensure the stable, healthy, and
sustainable development of our Group, we will hold the responsible personnel accountable
for fraud, money-laundering, corruption, and other incidents of violations of professional
ethics in accordance with the laws and regulations and the relevant internal provisions.
Employees can report such incidents through the reporting hotline, reporting box, email,
letter, and other channels set up by us. Once a report is received, we will open a case and set
up an investigation team to conduct an investigation and handling. In case of any acts from
our employees violating the law, we will transfer them to the judicial authorities for
handling in accordance with the law.
Meanwhile, we provide anti-corruption trainings to enhance the professional ethics
and anti-corruption awareness of the Directors and other employees, so as to ensure the

provided one anti-corruption training to our Directors as well as related compliance

compliance advocacy.
ESG measures relating to responsible supply chain management
We regard supply chain management as an integral part of our sustainable
development strategy and are committed to building an efficient, stable and sustainable
supply chain system. This not only serves as an important cornerstone for our long-term
development, but also brings opportunities to the upstream and downstream partners for
mutual progress.
Our suppliers include raw material suppliers, labor subcontractors, and outsourced
product providers. In terms of procurement management, we adopt flexible procurement
models, including regular procurement, volume-based procurement, public bidding through
electronic platforms and centralized procurement, based on our annual production and
operational plans and raw material requirements. These procurement methods enable us to
respond effectively to market fluctuations while ensuring timely supply of raw materials and
cost control. We primarily procure from direct sales companies and distributors of steel
producers and have established cooperative relationships with reputable enterprises capable
of providing stable supply. For further details on our suppliers, please refer to ‘‘—
Suppliers’’ above.
In respect of supplier selection and evaluation, we have established a systematic
supplier management process to ensure that our suppliers, including our subcontractors,
meet standards in quality, technology and accountability. Our selection criteria include
product quality certifications (such as ISO9001), market performance, brand reputation,
development capability, product quality and price competitiveness. Furthermore, to
identify and mitigate environmental and social risks in the supply chain, we have
implemented a risk identification and monitoring mechanism covering the entire supply
chain, which includes regular assessments and classification of suppliers’ environmental and
social responsibility risks.

RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
As of the Latest Practicable Date, our Company was held as to approximately 70.84%
by Broad Vision, which was in turn held as to 70% by Mr. Chen and 30% by Ms. Chen, the
executive Directors of our Company. The Employee Shareholding Platforms, namely,
Shanghai Xianglian and Shanghai Xinlianzhan, each a limited partnership established
under the laws of the PRC, respectively holds approximately 2.15% and 2.24% in our
Company as of the Latest Practicable Date and are managed by Ms. Chen as the executive
partner. For background and biographical details of Mr. Chen and Ms. Chen, see
‘‘Directors, Supervisors and Senior Management’’ in this prospectus. As at the Latest
Practicable Date, Broad Vision, Shanghai Xianglian and Shanghai Xinlianzhan held
approximately 75.23% of the issued share capital of our Company in aggregate. For details
of the Employee Shareholding Platforms, see ‘‘History and Development’’ in this
prospectus.
Immediately upon completion of the Global Offering (assuming the Over-allotment
Option is not exercised), Broad Vision will hold approximately 56.38% of the issued share
capital of our Company, Shanghai Xianglian will hold approximately 1.71% of the issued
share capital of our Company, and Shanghai Xinlianzhan will hold approximately 1.78% of
the issued share capital of our Company.
Pursuant to the acting in concert agreement entered into between Mr. Chen, Ms. Chen
and Broad Vision on January 1, 2020 and renewed on December 10, 2024, the details of
which are provided under the section headed ‘‘History and Development — Corporate
Development and Major Changes in Shareholdings — (4) Parties Acting in Concert’’ in this
prospectus, Mr. Chen, Ms. Chen and Broad Vision agreed to act in concert by voting in the
same manner as the others on all matters at our Company’s general meetings and Board
meetings (including procuring the directors appointed by them to do so) and the scope
covers all Board and general meetings of our Company, through votes held directly or
indirectly or controlled by each of them. There is no expiry date in relation to the acting in
concert agreement which was renewed on December 10, 2024, and save for any amendments
to such agreement to ensure compliance with the applicable laws and regulations from time
to time including but not limited to the Listing Rules, there are no circumstances under
which the acting in concert agreement entered into among Mr. Chen, Ms. Chen and Broad
Vision on December 10, 2024 will terminate.
As Ms. Chen is simultaneously the executive partner of Shanghai Xinlianzhan and
Shanghai Xianglian and controls the votes of the Shares held by Shanghai Xinlianzhan and
Shanghai Xianglian, immediately upon completion of the Global Offering (assuming the
Over-allotment Option is not exercised), Mr. Chen and Ms. Chen will, in aggregate, be
entitled to control the exercise of approximately 59.87% of voting rights in our Company
through Broad Vision, Shanghai Xianglian and Shanghai Xinlianzhan. Therefore, Broad
Vision, Shanghai Xianglian, Shanghai Xinlianzhan, Mr. Chen and Ms. Chen will
collectively hold 72,184,105 shares, representing approximately 59.87% of the issued
share capital of our Company immediately upon completion of the Global Offering
(assuming the Over-allotment Option is not exercised), and will constitute a group of
Controlling Shareholders of our Company under the Listing Rules.

RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
COMPETITION AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST
As of the Latest Practicable Date, save for the interest in our Group, our Controlling
Shareholders did not have any interest in a business which competes or is likely to compete,
directly or indirectly, with the business of our Group, and which requires disclosure under
Rule 8.10 of the Listing Rules.
INDEPENDENCE FROM OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
Our Directors consider that we are capable of carrying on our business independently
of our Controlling Shareholders and their close associates after the Listing, taking into
consideration the factors below.
Management Independence
Our Board comprises seven Directors, including two executive Directors, two
non-executive Directors and three independent non-executive Directors. We believe that
our Board as a whole, together with our senior management, is able to perform the
managerial role in our Group independently from our Controlling Shareholders for the
following considerations:
(a) although both Mr. Chen and Ms. Chen are Directors of our Company as well as
the directors of Broad Vision, one of our Controlling Shareholders, Broad Vision
has no business other than holding the Shares in our Company. Furthermore, as
disclosed in the section headed ‘‘— Competition and Conflict of Interest’’, as of
the Latest Practicable Date, our Controlling Shareholders did not have any
interest in a business which competes or is likely to compete, directly or indirectly,
with the business of our Group. As such, our Directors do not consider that there
is any issue in relation to management independence arising from the overlapping
of Mr. Chen and Ms. Chen’s directorship in our Company and Broad Vision;
(b) each of our Directors is aware of his/her fiduciary duties as a Director which
require, among others, that he/she acts for the benefit of and in the best interests
of our Company and does not allow any conflict between his/her duties as a
Director and his/her personal interests;
(c) our executive Directors are responsible for formulating operation strategies and
making significant business decisions, and our daily management and operation
decisions are made by senior management, all of whom have substantial
experience in the industry in which we are engaged and will be able to make
business decisions that are in the best interest of our Group. For details of the
industry experience of our senior management, see ‘‘Directors, Supervisors and
Senior Management’’ in this prospectus;
(d) we have appointed three independent non-executive Directors with a view to
bringing independent judgment to the decision-making process of our Board;
– 314 –

=== PAGE 325 ===
RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
(e) in the event that there is a potential conflict of interest arising out of any
transaction to be entered into between our Group and a Director and/or his/her
associate, he/she shall abstain from voting and shall not be counted towards the
quorum for the voting at the relevant Board meeting; and
(f) we have adopted a series of corporate governance measures to manage conflicts of
interest, if any, between our Group and our Controlling Shareholders, which
would support our independent management. For further details, see ‘‘—
Corporate Governance Measures’’ in this section.
Operational Independence
We have full rights to make all decisions on, and to carry out, our own business
operations independently. We have our own departments specializing in the respective areas
which have been in operation and are expected to continue to operate independently from
our Controlling Shareholders and their close associates. We hold the licenses, intellectual
property rights and qualifications necessary to carry on our principal business. We also
have independent access to suppliers and customers, and have sufficient capital, facilities
and employees to operate our business independently from our Controlling Shareholders
and their close associates.
Based on the above, our Directors believe that we will be able to operate independently
from our Controlling Shareholders and their close associates.
Financial Independence
We have an independent financial system. We make financial decisions according to
our own business needs, and neither our Controlling Shareholders nor their close associates
intervene with our use of funds. We are capable of obtaining financing from third parties
without relying on any guarantee or security provided by our Controlling Shareholders and
their respective close associates. We have established an independent finance department
with a team of finance staff and an independent audit, accounting and financial
management system.
During the Track Record Period, Mr. Chen and Ms. Chen had provided personal
guarantees for the banking facilities granted to our Group. All such personal guarantees
have been released or otherwise settled in full as at the Latest Practicable Date. During the
Track Record Period, there were no outstanding loans, or advances or other non-trade
balances due to our Controlling Shareholders and their close associates.
Based on the above, our Directors believe that we are capable of carrying on our
business independently of, and do not place undue reliance on, our Controlling
Shareholders and their close associates after the Listing.

RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
CORPORATE GOVERNANCE MEASURES
Our Directors recognize the importance of good corporate governance in protecting
our Shareholders’ interests. Our Company will comply with the provisions of the Corporate
Governance Code in Appendix C1 to the Listing Rules, and has adopted the following
measures to safeguard good corporate governance standards and to avoid potential
conflicts of interests between our Group and our Controlling Shareholders:
(a) under the Articles of Association, where a Shareholders’ meeting is to be held for
considering proposed transactions in which our Controlling Shareholders or any
of their respective close associates has a material interest, our Controlling
Shareholders and their close associates will not vote on the relevant resolutions
and shall not be counted in the quorum for the voting;
(b) our Company has established internal control mechanisms to identify connected
transactions. Upon Listing, if our Company enters into connected transactions
with our Controlling Shareholders or any of their associates, our Company will
comply with the applicable Listing Rules;
(c) our Board consists of a balanced composition of executive Directors and
non-executive Directors (including independent non-executive Directors), with
independent non-executive Directors representing not less than one-third of our
Board to ensure that our Board is able to effectively exercise independent
judgment in its decision-making process and provide independent advice to our
Shareholders. Our independent non-executive Directors individually and
collectively possess the requisite knowledge and experience to perform their
duties. They will review whether there is any conflict of interests between our
Group and our Controlling Shareholders and provide impartial and professional
advice to protect the interests of our minority Shareholders;
(d) where our Directors reasonably request the advice of independent professionals,
such as financial advisers, the appointment of such independent professionals will
be made at our Company’s expenses; and
(e) we have appointed SPDB International Capital Limited as our compliance adviser
to provide advice and guidance to us in respect of compliance with the applicable
laws in Hong Kong and the Listing Rules, including various requirements relating
to corporate governance.
Based on the above, our Directors believe that sufficient corporate governance
measures have been put in place to manage conflicts of interests that may arise between our
Group and our Controlling Shareholders and to protect our Shareholders’ interests as a
whole after the Listing.

suppliers; (ii) there has not been any major incidents involving the quality or delivery of the
metal hardware and accessories as supplied by Jiangmen Jiangu; (iii) more favorable credit
terms compared to other suppliers.
The pricing of the procurement of the metal hardware and accessories from Jiangmen
Jiangu shall be determined on an arm’s length basis, taking into account (i) the price shall
not be less favorable to Guangdong Yuntong than the price at which Guangdong Yuntong
may procures identical or similar products from Independent Third Parties, and such price
shall take into account the bulk purchase discounts that Guangdong Yuntong would
otherwise receive if it procured products of similar quantity and specifications from
Independent Third Parties; and (ii) with reference to the order size required by Guangdong
Yuntong. Guangdong Yuntong will then decide whether to place purchase orders to
Jiangmen Jiangu for the procurement of such metal hardware and accessories.

INTERNAL CONTROL MEASURES
In order to ensure that the terms under relevant framework agreements for the
continuing connected transactions are fair and reasonable, or no less favorable than terms
available to or from Independent Third Parties, and are carried out under normal
commercial terms, we have adopted the following internal control procedures:
. We have adopted and implemented a management system on connected
transactions. Under such system, the Audit Committee is responsible for
reviewing compliance with relevant laws, regulations, our policies and the
Listing Rules in respect of the continuing connected transactions. Further, the
Audit Committee, the Board and various internal departments of our Company
(including but not limited to the financial department and the compliance and
legal department) are jointly responsible for evaluating the terms under
framework agreements for the continuing connected transactions, in particular,
the fairness of the pricing policies and annual caps under each agreement;
. the Audit Committee, the Board and various other internal departments of our
Company (including but not limited to the financial department and the
compliance and legal department) will also regularly monitor the fulfillment
status and the transaction updates under the framework agreements. In addition,
our management also regularly reviews the pricing policies of the framework
agreements;

of the continuing connected transactions under the framework agreements and

CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
Board Diversity
Our Company has adopted a board diversity policy (the ‘‘Board Diversity Policy’’).
Pursuant to the Board Diversity Policy, in reviewing and evaluating suitable candidates for
appointment as Directors, the Nomination Committee will consider a range of diversity
perspectives, including but not limited to gender, age, language, cultural and educational
backgrounds, professional qualifications, skills, knowledge, industry and regional
experience and/or length of service, with reference to our Company’s business model and
specific needs. Currently, the Board has a balanced mix of knowledge and skills and each
member has different industry background. In addition, the age range of the Board is
relatively wide, from 46 to 63. Currently, our Company also has one female Director on the
Board and will continue to endeavor to enhance the gender diversity of the Board. The
Board considers that the Board is in line with the Board Diversity Policy.
The Nomination Committee is responsible for reviewing the diversity of the Board,
reviewing the Board Diversity Policy from time to time, setting and reviewing measurable
objectives to implement the Board Diversity Policy and monitoring the progress in
achieving such measurable objectives to ensure that the policy remains effective. Currently,
our Company also has one female Director in the Nomination Committee and will continue
to endeavor to enhance the gender diversity of the Nomination Committee. Our Company
will (i) disclose the biographical details of each Director and (ii) report on the
implementation of the Board Diversity Policy in its annual corporate governance report.

SHARE CAPITAL
RANKING
Upon completion of the Global Offering, we would have only one class of Shares. H
Shares are ordinary Shares in the share capital of our Company. However, apart from
certain qualified domestic institutional investors in the PRC, the qualified PRC investors
under the Shanghai — Hong Kong Stock Connect or the Shenzhen — Hong Kong Stock
Connect and other persons who are entitled to hold the H Shares pursuant to relevant PRC
laws and regulations or upon approvals of any competent authorities, H Shares generally
cannot be subscribed for by or traded between legal or natural persons of the PRC.
All dividends in respect of the H Shares are to be paid by us in Hong Kong dollars or
Renminbi, or in the form of H Shares.
CONVERSION OF THE UNLISTED SHARES INTO H SHARES
Our Company has filed for a ‘‘full circulation’’ of all the existing 95,950,005 Unlisted
Shares into H Shares on a one-for-one basis, and submitted the application reports,
authorization documents of the shareholders of Unlisted Shares for which an H-share ‘‘full
circulation’’ are applied, explanation about the compliance of share acquisition and other
documents in accordance with the requirements of the CSRC.
The relevant filings of the conversion of the existing 95,950,005 Unlisted Shares held
by the existing Shareholders into H Shares on a one-for-one basis have been completed on
November 12, 2025.
After all the requisite approvals have been obtained, the following procedures will need
to be completed: the relevant Unlisted Shares will be withdrawn from the Share register and
our Company will re-register such Shares on its H Share register maintained in Hong Kong
and instruct the H Share Registrar to issue H Share certificates. Registration on the H Share
register will be on the condition that (a) our Company’s H Share Registrar lodges with the
Hong Kong Stock Exchange a letter confirming the proper entry of the relevant H Shares
on the H Share register of members and the due dispatch of H Share certificates and (b) the
admission of the H Shares to trade on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange will comply with the
Listing Rules and the General Rules of HKSCC and the HKSCC Operational Procedures in
force from time to time. Until the converted Shares are re-registered on the H Share
register, such Shares would not be listed as H Shares.

CORNERSTONE INVESTORS
THE CORNERSTONE PLACING
We have entered into cornerstone investment agreements (each a ‘‘Cornerstone
Investment Agreement’’, and together the ‘‘Cornerstone Investment Agreements’’) with the
cornerstone investors set out below (each a ‘‘Cornerstone Investor’’, and together the
‘‘Cornerstone Investors’’), pursuant to which the Cornerstone Investors have agreed to,
subject to certain conditions, subscribe, or cause their designated entities to subscribe, at
the Offer Price for such number of the Offer Shares (rounded down to the nearest whole
board lot of 300 Shares) as may be purchased for an aggregate amount of approximately
HK$51.5 million (the ‘‘Cornerstone Placing’’). The aggregate amount of the investment
contributed by the Cornerstone Investors does not include the brokerage fee, the SFC
transaction levy, the AFRC transaction levy and the Stock Exchange trading fee which the
Cornerstone Investors will pay in respect of the International Offer Shares to be subscribed
by them. The number of Offer Shares to be subscribed for by the Cornerstone Investors are
subject to the determination of the final Offer Price.
Assuming an Offer Price of HK$9.16 per Share, being the high-end of the indicative
Offer Price range set out in this prospectus, the total number of Offer Shares to be
subscribed for by the Cornerstone Investors would be 5,621,700 H Shares, representing (i)
approximately 22.9% of the Offer Shares to be issued pursuant to the Global Offering and
approximately 4.7% of our total H Share in issue immediately upon completion of the
Global Offering, assuming the Over-allotment Option is not exercised, and (ii)
approximately 19.9% of the Offer Shares to be issued pursuant to the Global Offering
and approximately 4.5% of our total H Share capital immediately upon completion of the
Global Offering, assuming the Over-allotment Option is fully exercised.
Assuming an Offer Price of HK$8.13 per Share, being the mid-point of the indicative
Offer Price range set out in this prospectus, the total number of Offer Shares to be
subscribed for by the Cornerstone Investors would be 6,334,500 H Shares, representing (i)
approximately 25.8% of the Offer Shares to be issued pursuant to the Global Offering and
approximately 5.3% of our total H Share in issue immediately upon completion of the
Global Offering, assuming the Over-allotment Option is not exercised, and (ii)
approximately 22.4% of the Offer Shares to be issued pursuant to the Global Offering
and approximately 5.1% of our total H Share capital immediately upon completion of the
Global Offering, assuming the Over-allotment Option is fully exercised.
Assuming an Offer Price of HK$7.10 per Share, being the low-end of the indicative
Offer Price range set out in this prospectus, the total number of Offer Shares to be
subscribed for by the Cornerstone Investors would be 7,252,800 H Shares, representing (i)
approximately 29.5% of the Offer Shares to be issued pursuant to the Global Offering and

CORNERSTONE INVESTORS
Our Company is of the view that the Cornerstone Placing will help raise the profile of
our Company and to signify that such investors have confidence in our business and
prospects. Our Company became acquainted with each of the Cornerstone Investors in its
ordinary course of operation through business meetings or referral by the contact of our
Company.
The Cornerstone Placing will form part of the International Offering, and the
Cornerstone Investors and their respective close associates will not subscribe for any Offer
Shares under the Global Offering other than pursuant to the Cornerstone Investment
Agreements.
The Offer Shares to be subscribed by the Cornerstone Investors will rank pari passu in
all respects with the other fully paid H Shares in issue following the completion of the
Global Offering. Immediately following the completion of the Global Offering, the
Cornerstone Investors and their respective close associates will not, by virtue of their
respective investment under the relevant Cornerstone Investment Agreement, have any
Board representation in our Company; and none of the Cornerstone Investors and their
respective close associates will become a substantial Shareholder of our Company upon
completion of the Global Offering. The Offer Shares to be subscribed by the Cornerstone
Investors will be counted towards the public float for the purpose of Rule 8.08 (as amended
and replaced by Rule 19A.13A) of the Listing Rules. The three largest public Shareholders
will hold no more than 50% of the Shares held in public hands for the purpose of Rule
8.08(3) of the Listing Rules.
Other than a guaranteed allocation of the relevant Offer Shares at the Offer Price, the
Cornerstone Investors do not have any preferential rights in the Cornerstone Investment
Agreements compared with other public Shareholders.
To the best of the knowledge, information and belief of our Company, each of the
Cornerstone Investors and its ultimate beneficial owners (i) is an Independent Third Party;
(ii) is not accustomed to take and has not taken instructions from the Company, our
Directors, Supervisors, chief executive, the Controlling Shareholders, substantial
shareholders, existing Shareholders or any of its subsidiaries or their respective close
associates in relation to the acquisition, disposal, voting or other disposition of the Offer
Shares; and (iii) is not directly or indirectly financed by the Company, our Directors,
Supervisors, chief executive, the Controlling Shareholders, substantial shareholders,
existing Shareholders or any of its subsidiaries or their respective close associates.
To the best knowledge of our Company and as confirmed by each of the Cornerstone
Investors, (i) each of the Cornerstone Investors makes independent investment decisions,

OVERVIEW
We are an integrated PS building subcontracting service provider in the industrial
sector of the PS building market. We offer integrated services for construction projects
across industries, covering project design and optimization, procurement, manufacturing
and installation. We are primarily engaged in the construction of PS buildings in the PRC,
and to a lesser extent, overseas. By leveraging our technology and expertise, we have built a
reputation in China’s industrial sector of the PS building market. According to the F&S
Report, we ranked third in China’s industrial sector of the PS building market in terms of
revenue in 2024, representing a 3.5% market share; and the top two players capturing a
market share of 35.8% and 6.5%, respectively.
For the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024, and the six months ended June 30,
2024 and 2025, our revenue was RMB1,902.8 million, RMB1,453.2 million, RMB1,523.0
million, RMB509.5 million and RMB1,424.1 million, respectively, demonstrating our
steady performance in business development and operational efficiency.

SIGNIFICANT FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Our results of operations are primarily influenced by several key factors, including
government policies guiding China’s industrial transition, the global economic downturn,
technological advancements, and the inherent characteristics of our project-based business
model. These elements shape our financial performance and drive the strategic direction of
our company.
Impact of China’s Industrial Transition, Global Expansion, and Private-Sector Client
Dynamics
China’s industrial transformation, underpinned by policies promoting innovation,
sustainability, and global integration, has spurred demand for modern industrial
infrastructure. Our expertise in PS building subcontracting services positions us to meet
these evolving requirements, particularly in sectors such as advanced production, renewable
energy, and consumer goods.
As China’s industrialization progressed, our clients evolved alongside these
transformations, driving the demand for increasingly sophisticated industrial facilities.
We have continuously adapted our services to support their growth, initially catering to
traditional industries and later expanding to meet the needs of emerging industrial sectors.
In recent years, as Chinese manufacturers have pursued overseas expansion in line with the
‘‘Belt and Road Initiative’’ and other global trade strategies, we have accompanied our
clients in venturing into international markets. This includes providing PS building
subcontracting services tailored to their overseas operations.
Our commitment to addressing client needs has remained central to our business
model, enabling us to grow alongside China’s industrial evolution and align with the
changing demands of private-sector enterprises.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Client-specific dynamics
Our private-sector clients have distinct demands and behaviors that directly influence
our financial performance, particularly in areas such as revenue recognition, receivables,
and cash flow:
. Industrial facility needs: Clients increasingly prioritize rapid construction,
scalability, and cost efficiency for production lines, warehousing, and logistics
hubs.
. General market penetration: Adoption of PS buildings varies globally, with
developed markets exhibiting higher penetration, while emerging economies
provide significant growth potential as industries modernize.
. Payment practices: Most clients operate on milestone-based payment terms, tied
to project progress. While this allows flexibility, it introduces variability in cash
flow. For instance, extended payment cycles in long-duration projects may impact
our trade and bills receivables.
Strategic expansion in Southeast Asia
Southeast Asia continues to be a major growth driver for our global expansion
strategy. Revenue from the region surged to RMB241.3 million for the year ended
December 31, 2024, accounting for 15.8% of total revenue. For the six months ended June
30, 2025, revenue from this region increased to RMB119.1 million from RMB110.2 million
for the six months ended June 30, 2024. This growth is underpinned by several factors. For
further details on PS building market in Southeast Asia, please refer to ‘‘Industry Overview
— Analysis of China’s Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market — Drivers of
Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market in Southeast Asia’’ in this prospectus.
Enabling sustainable growth and financial resilience
. Revenue diversification: As our geographic footprint expands, revenue
contributions from international markets have grown significantly. For the
years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended June 30,
2024 and 2025, overseas markets accounted for approximately 2.2%, 8.0%,
23.0%, 31.6% and 10.8% of our total revenue, respectively. This demonstrates the
success of our diversification strategy, reducing reliance on domestic markets and
leveraging emerging opportunities in global regions.
. Strategic financial management: Despite extended payment cycles from certain
projects, we have maintained robust financial discipline. We oversee the receivable
and payable management to stabilize cash flows.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Industry Characteristics and Business Model Features
Our business operates within the industrial sector of the PS building market, a sector
characterized by diverse client needs and a project-based model. While the nature of
construction projects can lead to variations in revenue and financial performance, our
ability to deliver high-quality, tailored services across a range of industries ensures that we
remain a trusted provider for repeat engagements. The dynamic requirements of the private
sector, where projects are driven by industrial upgrades, expansion, and operational shifts,
underscore the importance of our expertise in meeting diverse and evolving client demands.
Our ability to handle complex projects and meet diverse industry requirements positions us
favorably within this competitive landscape.
From a financial perspective, the project-driven nature of our operations significantly
influences key financial line items. Our customers’ payments, inherently tied to project
milestones, can fluctuate based on the timing of project initiation, progress, and
completion. Contract liabilities are often affected by upfront payments for projects, while
contract assets tend to be in line with the progression of our construction projects.
Additionally, inventories may vary depending on the production schedules of PS building
components, and work-in-progress balances can rise during intensive construction periods.
These fluctuations reflect the typical working capital cycle of the industry. Furthermore,
cash flow can be impacted by factors such as advance payments, project delays, and the
timing of milestone certifications and timing of settlement payment.
In summary, while the PS building market is influenced by cyclical factors and
operational dynamics, our comprehensive approach to addressing client needs across
project lifecycles enhances our ability to navigate these complexities.
Technological Advancements in Research and Development and Digitalization
Our research and development efforts are closely aligned with the practical needs of
our projects, driving improvements in operational efficiency and cost-effectiveness. By
focusing on applied innovation, our research and development initiatives directly support
our business operations, enhancing both project execution and revenue generation. For
instance, we have introduced a customized lifting device for on-site sheet pressing. This
innovation enables us to transport pressed sheets directly to rooftops, streamlining
workflows, reducing construction time, and ultimately lowering project costs. Similarly, our
LS-III Standing Seam Roof System, designed to improve wind resistance and thermal
insulation, eliminates the need for additional insulation and wind proofing layers
commonly required in conventional building systems. These advancements directly reduce
construction expenses, benefiting both us and our clients.
– 359 –

=== PAGE 370 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Beyond product innovation, our investments in digitalization are paving the way for
future advancements in smart construction and intelligent manufacturing. Through the
integration of digital tools, we are committed to enhance quality control, improve project
management processes, and improve operational efficiency. For example, the adoption of
automation in production and enhanced supply chain management enable us to reduce
material waste, improve cost control, and ensure the timely delivery of high-quality
products.
As we continue to expand these capabilities, we anticipate further benefits, including
cost efficiencies, enhanced quality assurance, and ultimately, stronger profit margins. These
developments position us competitively for long-term success in an evolving and
increasingly competitive market landscape.
Impact of Raw Material Price Fluctuations
Steel plate is the principal raw material used in our operations and a key cost driver in
the PS building market. The price of steel plate is subject to fluctuations influenced by
factors such as global supply and demand dynamics, market competition, and regulatory
changes, many of which are beyond our control. The cost of steel plate directly impacts our
cost of sale.
To mitigate the financial impact of raw material price volatility, we may incorporate
price adjustment clauses into our contracts for long-duration projects. These mechanisms
allow us to proportionately adjust settlement prices based on significant deviations in steel
plate prices from the baseline agreed upon at contract signing. Typically, adjustments are
triggered when price changes exceed a threshold and are calculated using mutually agreed
benchmarks or market indices. This approach helps stabilize our profit margins and ensures
equitable financial outcomes for both us and our customers.
For further details on the sensitivity analysis on the hypothetical fluctuations in raw
material costs, with other variables remaining constant, on our profit/(loss) during the
Track Record Period, please refer to ‘‘— Description of Selected Components of Statements
of Profit or Loss — Cost of Sales — Sensitivity analysis’’ below.
In summary, while fluctuations in steel plate prices remain an inherent risk in our
industry, our proactive management strategies effectively mitigate their impact. These
measures not only protect our financial stability but also strengthen our ability to deliver
consistent value to our clients.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
SEASONALITY
Our business exhibits clear seasonality due to the inherent characteristics of PS
building construction, which is influenced by the environmental and social conditions of
project locations. Weather conditions, such as extreme cold or heavy rainfall, often restrict
on-site installation activities, while major holidays like the Chinese New Year can lead to
temporary suspensions of work.
For example, the winter season in northern regions halts a portion of construction
work due to freezing temperatures, delaying project schedules. Similarly, the rainy season in
Southeast Asia, such as Thailand, slows construction progress due to safety and quality
concerns. Social factors, such as the Chinese New Year, typically result in construction
pausing for about a month. While such pauses are common, exceptions exist when we
project schedule is tight and requires continuous operations.
As our project portfolio expands, we continue to adapt to these seasonal variations,
leveraging operational flexibility to meet client needs effectively.
IMPACT OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted global industries, including the PS building
market, with supply chain interruptions, labor shortages, and production delays. Our
operations in the PRC were minimally impacted due to robust supplier relationships that
ensured a steady supply of materials and the strategic location of our projects in industrial
zones, which were less affected by travel restrictions. This stability allowed us to maintain
construction schedules and meet customer expectations without major disruptions, even
during the height of the pandemic. Internationally, while regional restrictions required
some project adjustments, our resource reallocation and adaptability demonstrated our
operational flexibility. Strong relationships with key customers also provided resilience, as
they continued awarding us new projects despite global uncertainty, ensuring a steady
business pipeline throughout the pandemic. In 2022, due to international travel restrictions,
the overseas demand for our industrial environmental equipment declined. As a result, the
revenue from our industrial environmental equipment in 2022 was RMB31.8 million. After
the pandemic situation improved in 2023, the revenue of our industrial environmental
equipment business category rebounded to RMB69.4 million.

MATERIAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ESTIMATES
We have identified certain accounting policies that are material to the preparation of

an understanding of our financial condition and results of operations, are set forth in detail

Material Accounting Policy Information
Revenue recognition
Our revenue is primarily derived from three business categories: PS building
subcontracting services, general contracting services and sales of industrial environmental
equipment. We recognize revenue when control over the service or product is transferred to
the customer. The amount recognized reflects the consideration we expect to receive,
excluding value-added tax, other sales taxes, and trade discounts.
PS building subcontracting services
Our revenue is recognized over time for subcontracting contracts related to PS building
construction, utilizing the input method. Our Group’s performance creates or enhances an
asset or work in progress that the customer controls as the asset is created or enhanced, thus
our Group satisfies a performance obligation and recognizes revenue over time, by
reference to the contract costs incurred to date relative to the estimated total contract costs
while the contract progress are highly correlated contract costs for the contracts. Invoices
are issued according to contractual terms and obligated to be paid in accordance with the
respective repayment schedules.
General contracting services
Our revenue from general contracting projects, which involve engineering,
procurement, and construction services, is also recognized over time. Our Group’s
performance creates or enhances an asset or work in progress that the customer controls
as the asset is created or enhanced, thus our Group satisfies a performance obligation and
recognizes revenue over time, by reference to the contract costs incurred to date relative to
the estimated total contract costs while the contract progress are highly correlated contract
costs for the contracts. Invoices are issued according to contractual terms and obligated to
be paid in accordance with the respective repayment schedules.
– 362 –

=== PAGE 373 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
The excess of cumulative revenue recognized over the cumulative billings to customer
is recognized as contract assets and then transferred to receivables when the rights become
unconditional. The excess of cumulative billings to customers over the cumulative revenue
recognized is recognized as contract liabilities.
Industrial environmental equipment
Our revenue from this business category is mainly represented by the design,
development, manufacture, and sale of industrial environmental equipment. Revenue is
recognized upon delivery, which occurs when customer pick up goods at our premises or
when goods are handed over to customer. Delivery occurs when the risks of obsolescence
and loss are transferred to the customer, i.e., when the goods are delivered to the customer
in accordance with the sales contract, or the acceptance provisions have lapsed or we have
objective evidence that all criteria for acceptance have been satisfied and there is no
unfulfilled obligation that could affect the customers’ acceptance of the products.
Property, plant and equipment
Property, plant, and equipment are recorded at cost, net of accumulated depreciation
and impairment losses. Depreciation is calculated on a straight-line basis over the assets’
estimated useful lives. Key categories include:
Estimated useful lives
Owned buildings 20 years
Leasehold improvements Over the lease term
Plant and machinery 3–10 years
Office equipment 5 years
Motor vehicles 5 years
Construction in progress is recorded at cost and not depreciated until completion,
ensuring that capitalized expenses reflect the asset’s readiness for use. Impairment reviews
are conducted periodically, and any gain or loss on disposal is recognized in profit or loss.
Investment properties
Properties held for long-term rental or capital appreciation are classified as investment
properties. These assets are initially recorded at cost and depreciated on a straight-line basis
over their estimated useful lives. Gains or losses on disposal are recognized in the period in
which the sale occurs.
– 363 –

=== PAGE 374 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Leased assets
For leased assets, we recognize right-of-use assets and lease liabilities at the lease
commencement date, except for leases with terms under 12 months or those involving
low-value assets. The lease liability is initially measured at the present value of future lease
payments, and the right-of-use asset is adjusted for initial direct costs. Both assets and
liabilities are subsequently remeasured if there are changes to lease terms or scope.
Intangible assets
Intangible assets, including software and patents, are amortized on a straight-line basis
over their useful lives, generally 10 years. Research and development costs are expensed as
incurred, except when they meet criteria for capitalization, such as demonstrated technical
feasibility and future economic benefit.
Financial instruments
Financial assets
Financial assets and liabilities are classified and measured at amortized cost or fair
value through profit or loss. Financial assets at amortized cost including trade and bill
receivables, deposits and other receivables, amounts due from a related company, amount
due from subsidiaries, pledged bank deposits, restricted bank balance and, cash and cash
equivalents that are held for collection of contractual cash flows where those cash flows
represent solely payments of principal and interest are subsequently measured at amortized
cost using the effective interest method. Interest income, foreign exchange gains and losses
and impairment are recognized in profit or loss. Any gain or loss on derecognition is
recognized in profit or loss
Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss are measured at fair value at the
end of each reporting period, with any fair value gains or losses recognized in profit or loss.
The net gain or loss recognized in profit or loss includes any dividend or interest earned on
the financial asset and is included in the ‘‘other gains and losses’’ line item.
Impairment loss on financial assets
Our Group performs impairment assessment under expected credit loss (‘‘ECL’’) model
on financial assets measured at amortized cost (including trade and bill receivables, deposits
and other receivables, amount due from a related party, pledged bank deposits, restricted
bank balance and cash and cash equivalents) and contract assets which are subject to
impairment assessment under HKFRS 9. The amount of ECL is updated at the end of each
reporting date to reflect changes in credit risk since initial recognition.
– 364 –

=== PAGE 375 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Employee benefits
Short-term employee benefits and contributions to defined contributions retirement plan
Short-term employee benefits are recorded as expenses when the related services are
rendered. A liability is recognized for amounts expected to be paid when our Group has a
present legal or constructive obligation arising from past service provided by employees,
and the obligation can be reliably estimated. Contributions to defined contribution
retirement plans are expensed in the period when the associated employee services are
rendered.
Termination benefits
Termination benefits are recognized at the earlier of the date our Group can no longer
withdraw the offer of those benefits or when it incurs restructuring costs that include
termination benefits.
Share-based payments
The fair value of shares granted to employees is recognized as an employee cost with a
corresponding increase in a share-based payments reserve within equity. The fair value is
measured at grant date using the income approach model, taking into account the terms and
conditions upon which the shares were granted. Where the employees have to meet vesting
conditions before becoming unconditionally entitled to the shares, the total estimated fair
value of the shares is spread over the vesting period, taking into account the probability
that the shares will vest.
During the vesting period, the number of shares that are expected to vest is reviewed.
Any resulting adjustment to the cumulative fair value recognized in prior years is
charged/credited to the profit or loss for the year of the review. On vesting date, the amount
recognized as an expense is adjusted to reflect the actual number of shares that vest (with a
corresponding adjustment to the share-based payments reserve).
Material Accounting Judgments and Estimates
Our consolidated financial statements require management to make critical judgments,
estimates, and assumptions that impact the reported amounts of revenue, expenses, assets,
and liabilities. These judgments and estimates are based on historical experience, industry
practices, and reasonable expectations of future events. The most material accounting
policies involving estimates and judgments are detailed below.

=== PAGE 376 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Critical judgments in applying accounting policies
Revenue recognition of contract revenue
Our Group recognize revenue from provision of PS building subcontracting service as
subcontractor and general contracting services over time by measuring the progress towards
complete satisfaction of the relevant performance obligation. We measure progress by
comparing actual costs incurred to the total expected costs for each project, which best
reflects the transfer of control to the customer over time. Management routinely revises cost
estimates as each project advances; however, total contract costs and revenue may
ultimately vary from these estimates, affecting the revenue and profit recognized.
Principal versus agent consideration (principal)
Our Group engages in provision of PS building subcontracting services as
subcontractor and general contracting services. Our Group concluded that our Group
acts as the principal for such transactions as it controls the specified good before it is
transferred to the customer after taking into consideration indicators such as our Group is
primarily responsible for fulfilling the promise to provide the PS building or completed
construction projects to our customers. Our Group has inventory risk. When our Group
satisfies the performance obligation, our Group recognizes the revenue in the gross amount
of consideration to which our Group expects to be entitled as specified in the contracts.
Key sources of estimation uncertainty
Provision of ECL for contract assets and trade and bills receivables
Our Group works on PS building subcontracting services as subcontractor and general
contracting services to customers before the customers pay consideration or before
payments are due, contract assets are recognized for the earned considerations that are
conditional. Contract assets are stated at cost less impairment. In assessing the
recoverability of the contract assets, our Group regularly reviews and consider
forward-looking information that may impact the customers’ ability to repay the
outstanding balances in order to estimate the expected credit losses for the impairment
assessment. The provision of ECL is sensitive to changes in estimates.
Except for the major customers and debtors with material outstanding balance or
credit-impaired and a major customer of our Group which assesses ECLs on individual
basis, our Group uses provision matrix to calculate ECLs for trade and bills receivables.
The provision rates and matrix are based on our Group’s historical default rates from
debtors with similar loss patterns taking into consideration forward-looking information
that is reasonable and supportable available without undue costs or effort. At every
reporting date, the historical observed default rates are reassessed and changes in the
forward-looking information are considered. The provision of ECLs is sensitive to changes
in estimates.

Recognition of deferred tax assets
As of December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024, and June 30, 2025, deferred tax assets of
approximately RMB21.6 million, RMB15.4 million, RMB17.3 million and RMB17.8
million, respectively, in relation to unsecured tax losses, allowance for credit losses of
financial assets and other temporary differences were recognized in the consolidated
financial statements, respectively. Estimating the deferred tax assets to be recognized
require a process that involves determining appropriate tax provisions, forecasting future
years’ taxable income and assessing the ability to utilize tax benefits through future
earnings and tax structuring. In cases where the actual future profits generated are less than
expected, a material reversal of the deferred tax asset may arise, which would be recognized
in profit or loss for the period in which such a reversal takes place. Any expected changes in
assumptions and estimates in tax regulations could also affect the recoverability of these
deferred tax assets in the future.
We are required to recognize deferred tax liabilities for taxable temporary differences
relating to investments in certain subsidiaries, unless we are able to control the timing of the
reversal of the temporary difference and such temporary difference is more likely to be
reversed in the foreseeable future, in which case the recognition of deferred tax liabilities is
not required. Deferred tax liability have not been recognized for the taxation that would be
payable on the undistributed profits of certain subsidiaries which were under certain
jurisdictions as we are of the view that it is able to fully control the timing of the reversal of
the temporary difference arising from dividend distribution of the subsidiary and that
subsidiary will not make any profit distribution in the foreseeable future.
Impairment of goodwill
Determining whether goodwill is impaired requires an estimation of the recoverable
amount of the cash generating units (the ‘‘CGUs’’) to which goodwill have been allocated,
which is the higher of value in use or fair value less costs of disposal. The value in use
calculation requires our Group to estimate the present value of the future cash flows
expected to arise from the CGUs containing goodwill using suitable discount rates, growth
rates for budgeted revenue and operating expenses and related cash inflows and outflows
patterns. Where the actual future cash flows are less than expected, or change in facts and
circumstances which results in downward revision of growth rates for budgeted revenue or
upward revision of discount rates or budgeted operating expenses, or change in related cash
inflows or outflows patterns, an impairment loss may arise. Furthermore, the estimated
cash flows and discount rates are subject to higher degree of estimation uncertainties due to
uncertainty on how the volatility or disruptions in energy, financial, foreign currency or
commodity markets may progress and evolve. For details on the recoverable amount
calculation, please refer to Note 22 to the Accountants’ Report as set out in Appendix I to
this prospectus.

These interconnected business categories create synergies that fuel the sustained growth of
our Group.

PS building subcontracting services
PS building subcontracting services are the cornerstone of our business, specializing in
PS building subcontracting. This business category integrates design, manufacturing,
on-site installation, and quality assurance to deliver comprehensive subcontracting services
tailored to diverse industrial project requirements.
For the year ended December 31, 2023, PS building subcontracting services
contributed revenue of RMB1,293.9 million, representing 89.0% of total revenue,
compared to RMB1,770.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2022. For the year
ended December 31, 2024, revenue was RMB1,240.5 million, accounting for 81.5% of total
revenue, compared to RMB1,293.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2023. For the
six months ended June 30, 2025, revenue was RMB1,247.3 million, accounting for 87.6% of
our total revenue, compared to RMB442.2 million for the six months ended June 30, 2024.
For further details on analysis on the fluctuation, please refer to ‘‘— Period to Period
Comparison of Results of Operations’’ below.
General contracting services
In addition to our core PS building subcontracting services, we have expanded into
general contracting services. As a general contractor, we oversee the entire project lifecycle,
including project implementation, construction of primary structures, quality control,
scheduling, safety, and budget management. We collaborate with subcontractors to ensure
efficient project execution while leveraging our expertise in PS buildings.

For the year ended December 31, 2023, general contracting services contributed
revenue of RMB89.9 million, compared to RMB100.3 million for the year ended December
31, 2022. For the year ended December 31, 2024, revenue rose to RMB182.5 million,
representing 12.0% of our total revenue, compared to RMB89.9 million for the year ended
December 31, 2023. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, revenue further rose to
RMB141.5 million from RMB21.1 million for the six months ended June 30, 2024. Given
the complementary role of general contracting services in supporting PS building
subcontracting service business category, the number of projects in this category remains
low (typically in the single digits) and project cycles are relatively long. As a result, natural
project completions can lead to significant fluctuations in reported figures, although the
underlying business remains stable.
Industrial environmental equipment
Our industrial environmental equipment business category was established to address
the rising demand for specialized products in industrial manufacturing environments. This
business category primarily focuses on the MFAS line, which currently generates the vast
majority of our revenue.
During the Track Record Period, revenue from sale of industrial environmental
equipment was predominately derived from overseas orders. Revenue from this category
surged to RMB69.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2023, accounting for 4.8% of
our total revenue, up from RMB31.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2022. For the
year ended December 31, 2024, revenue from this category was RMB100.0 million,

December 31, 2023. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, revenue from this category
decreased to RMB35.3 million, contributing 2.5% of total revenue, from RMB46.2 million
for the six months ended June 30, 2024. For further details on the analysis of fluctuation,
please refer to ‘‘— Period to Period Comparison of Results of Operations’’ below.

Due to the project-based nature of our operations, the average gross profit margin of a
particular region in a given year during the Track Record Period can be influenced by one
or several projects carried out in that region during the year. This results in fluctuations in
gross profit margins across different regions from year to year. For instance, we recorded a
relatively low gross profit margin in Southwest China for the year ended December 31, 2023
of 11.7%. This was mainly because we undertook a large project of constructing a smart
factory for a client in Guangxi Province. The total contract value of this project exceeded
RMB100.0 million, but it had a relatively low gross profit margin, so as to impact the
overall gross profit margin in Southwest China in 2023. For the year ended December 31,
2023, we achieved a relatively high gross profit margin of 25.8% in Thailand. This was
mainly due to the fact that the number of projects we had in that year was relatively small,
and the gross profit margin of each individual project had a significant impact on the
overall gross profit margin. For the year ended December 31, 2023, our gross profit margin
in United States increased to 9.5% from 1.3% for the year ended December 31, 2022,
primarily driven by the increase of overseas order of our industrial environmental
equipment previously constrained by the pandemic. For the year ended December 31, 2024,
our gross profit margin from United States further increased to 21.4% primarily because we
provided industrial environmental equipment with high gross margin to a long-term
cooperative customer in the region, in order to meet their stringent requirements for the
specific product. Gross profit margin for ‘‘others’’ remained relatively high at 52.7%,
45.5%, 56.7% and 11.7% for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023 and 2024 and the six
months ended June 30, 2025, respectively. High gross profit margin was primarily
attributable to our sales to a Canadian customer. We provided PS building components
manufactured by us to this customer without undertaking installation services. Leveraging
our product quality and long-standing cooperative relationship, we have maintained a
relatively high gross profit margin. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, gross profit
margin for ‘‘others’’ decreased to 11.7% from 43.0% for the six months ended June 30,
2024. This was primarily because this category’s revenue composition during the period was
dominated by a few large-scale projects with lower margins. Although the overall revenue
increased due to the higher contract value of these individual projects, the overall gross
profit margin decreased.

Research and Development Expenses
Research and development expenses reflect costs incurred in our continuous efforts to
enhance construction and manufacturing technology and to develop sustainable products
and services. For the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended
June 30, 2024 and 2025, our research and development expenses amounted to RMB40.3
million, RMB28.8 million, RMB20.5 million, RMB7.4 million and RMB9.3 million,
respectively. These expenses primarily include salaries for research and development
personnel, materials used for experimental projects, and applicable overhead. The research
and development expenses are closely tied to the nature and scope of our research and
development projects. Expenses directly supporting project-specific research and
development are later reclassified as project costs, while costs for general-purpose
product development are recorded as research and development expenses. Overall,
changes in research and development expenses reflect adjustments in resource allocation
based on the progress and focus of our innovation initiatives.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Income Tax Expenses
We are subject to income tax on profits arising from the jurisdictions in which our
entities operate, primarily the PRC. For the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024,
and the six months ended June 30, 2024 and 2025, our income tax expenses included both
current and deferred tax provisions, based on estimated assessable profits and applicable
tax rates.
For the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024, and the six months ended June 30,
2024 and 2025, our Group’s effective tax rate was 21.3%, 24.7%, 10.1%, 29.6% and 17.5%,
respectively. Our higher effective tax rates compared to the preferential income tax rate of
15% for the year ended December 31, 2022 and 2023 was mainly because only our Company
was entitled for a preferential enterprise income tax rate of 15% while our subsidiaries in
the PRC are subject to normal enterprise income tax rate of 25%. Our Group’s effective tax
rate increased to 24.7% for the year ended December 31, 2023 from 21.3% for the year
ended December 31, 2022, primarily driven by the recognition of deferred tax assets
resulting from applying the preferential income tax rate of 15%. This one-off effect
significantly impacted the overall tax rate for the year. For the year ended December 31,
2024, the effective tax rate decreased to 10.1% from 24.7% for the year ended December 31,
2023, mainly reflecting tax effect of deductible temporary differences previously not
recognized of approximately RMB13.8 million. As of December 31, 2024, we had unutilized
tax losses of approximately RMB47.3 million. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, our
effective tax rate was 17.5% compared to 29.6% for the six months ended June 30, 2024,
primarily because our Company was qualified as high-technology enterprise and was
entitled to a preferential income tax rate of 15%.
PRC enterprise income tax
In accordance with the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law (‘‘CIT Law’’), the statutory
income tax rate for enterprises in the PRC is 25%. During the Track Record Period, our
PRC subsidiaries calculated their income tax expenses based on this rate.
. PRC enterprise income tax provision: For the years ended December 31, 2022,
2023, 2024, and the six months ended June 30, 2024 and 2025, our provision for
PRC Enterprise Income Tax was RMB20.6 million, RMB14.2 million, RMB9.0
million, RMB5.4 million and RMB14.1 million respectively. These amounts
include adjustments for under-provisions from prior years where applicable. In
addition, since our Company was qualified as a ‘‘High and New Technology
Enterprise’’, we were eligible for a preferential income tax rate of 15% for the
period from 2023 to 2025.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
. Deferred tax: For the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2023, deferred tax
provision amounted to RMB3.2 million and RMB6.1 million, respectively. For
the year ended December 31, 2024, we recorded deferred tax credit of RMB1.9
million. For the six months ended June 30, 2024 and 2025, we recorded deferred
tax credit of RMB0.4 million and RMB0.6 million, respectively. These
adjustments reflect temporary differences and the utilization of tax benefits
resulting from the unused tax losses.
Thailand tax considerations
In accordance with Thailand’s Enterprise Income Tax Law, the statutory tax rate is
20%. During the Track Record Period, we recorded a tax provision of approximately
RMB787,000 for the year ended December 31, 2024 in view of having assessable profit in
Thailand during the year.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, our Group has
fully complied with all applicable tax regulations. There are no ongoing tax disputes or
unresolved tax issues with the relevant tax authorities.
Malaysia tax considerations
In accordance with Malaysia Income Tax Act, the statutory tax rate is 17%. No
Malaysia Enterprise Income Tax has been provided during the Track Record Period as we
did not derive any estimated assessable profit in Malaysia during the Track Record Period.
PERIOD TO PERIOD COMPARISON OF RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Six Months Ended June 30, 2024 Compared to Six Months Ended June 30, 2025
Revenue and gross profit
For the six months ended June 30, 2025, our revenue increased by 179.5% to

LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL RESOURCES
Our liquidity and capital resources are critical to support our operations, growth, and
financial stability. We primarily rely on cash generated from operating activities,
supplemented by bank borrowings. These sources enable us to meet working capital
needs, invest in new projects, and sustain our business growth. However, liquidity risk
remains an inherent challenge, as fluctuations in working capital, project timelines, and
external financing conditions can impact our ability to generate sufficient cash flow to meet
obligations when due. As of December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024 and June 30, 2025, we had cash
and cash equivalents of RMB50.1 million, RMB90.1 million, RMB110.9 million and
RMB177.5 million, respectively.
Working Capital Statement
Our Directors confirm that, and the Sole Sponsor concurs that, taking into account the
financial resources presently available to our Group, including our internal resources and
the estimated net proceeds of the Global Offering, our Group has sufficient working capital
for our present requirements for at least the next 12 months from the date of this
prospectus. Our Directors confirm that there were no material defaults in payment of trade
and non-trade payables and borrowings, and/or breaches of financial covenants during the
Track Record Period and up to the date of this prospectus.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
In view of our net operating cash outflows for the year ended December 31, 2024, we
plan to improve our operation cash flow position by (i) enhancing our credit verification
and risk management measures, including (a) performing assessment on customers’
financial position, business operations, land ownership status and decision-making
structure at the early stage of engagement; (b) closely following up on the operational
and financial conditions of major customers and debtors. We require our business
department to maintain regular communications with the client during project execution.
Once they learn of any situations that may affect our customers’ business operations or
payment approvals, we will proactively communicate with the other party, including but
not limited to conducting on-site consultations at the client’s company; and (c) performing
regular reconciliation with our customers and debtors and follow-up with them on overdue
trade receivables as a reminder as well a measure to express commercial pressure; (ii) closely
monitoring the certification process to speed up the billing and collection process, and, in
turn, the operational cash inflow. For example, for our projects with Customer A, we have
established a dedicated task team comprising personnel from sales, commercial, project,
finance, design and production functions. This team tracks contract milestones and
prepares the required documentation, generally three days ahead of the scheduled payment
node. Upon completion of milestones, payment application documents are submitted on the
same day in most of the circumstances, with daily follow-up on the approval process and
invoice issuance. After invoicing, the finance personals would track payment status on a
daily basis, which has allowed us to receive milestone payments from Customer A’s projects
typically within one month; (iii) closely monitoring the collection status of our trade
receivables and actively following up with our customers and debtors for settlement. For
example, our finance department holds weekly meetings with project managers and sales
personnel to update collection progress using an internally maintained receivables tracking
table. This cross-functional communication ensures timely identification of overdue
payments and allows us to assign accountability and follow up more effectively; (iv)
negotiating with our suppliers for more favorable credit terms; and (v) utilizing our banking
facilities to cover any potential shortfall in our cash flow position.

Contract Assets and Contract Liabilities
Contract assets represent our right to consideration from customers in exchange for
the provision of services and products transferred to our customers that is not yet billed.
Contract assets primarily arise when we provide PS building subcontracting services and
general contracting services to our customers but our right to payment for the construction
work performed is still conditional. Contract assets will be transferred to trade and bills
receivables when the rights become unconditional, typically when we obtain the
certification of the completed construction work from our customers. Retention
receivables included in contract assets represent our right to consideration for work
performed and not yet billed because it is conditional subject to a quality assurance period
as stipulated in the relevant contracts. Contract liabilities primarily arise when we receive
advance payment from our customers, which will be recognized as revenue in the future
when we preform obligations under the relevant contracts.
The movements of our contract assets and contract liabilities during the Track Record
Period primarily reflect the progression of our construction contracts, with variations in
project completion stages and milestones.

billed as trade receivables. Given the stability and credibility of these clients, we do not

As of June 30, 2025, our inventories amounted to RMB134.4 million, reflecting an
increase of 39.2% from RMB96.6 million as of December 31, 2024, reflecting the increased
procurement of materials in line with the increased construction activities. As of December
31, 2024, our inventories amounted to RMB96.6 million, reflecting an increase of 33.0%
from RMB72.6 million as of December 31, 2023. This increase was primarily due to the
accumulation of materials and goods in transit related to the progress of ongoing projects at
the reporting date. Specifically, the high level of inventory of goods in transit, with a
balance of RMB32.7 million as of December 31, 2024, was primarily due to the fact that
many of our projects only commenced construction in the fourth quarter. As of December
31, 2023, inventories decreased by 24.0% from RMB95.5 million as of December 31, 2022.
This decline was mainly attributable to the consumption of raw materials for projects
completed during the year and adjustments in inventory levels aligned with project
schedules.
Inventories are measured at cost, and provisions are made for impairment based on
expected net realizable value. Inventory turnover is closely monitored to ensure alignment
with project schedules.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Our Directors are of the view that there is no material recoverability issue for
inventories on the following basis:
. Given the project-driven nature of our operations, the turnover of our inventory
is closely aligned with project progress, with stock levels varying according to
specific project timelines. During the Track Record Period, we maintained a
relatively stable and low inventory turnover days at 24 days, 25 days, 23 days and
17 days for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, 2024, and the six months
ended June 30, 2025, respectively;
. We have a comprehensive inventory management system in place, including the
goods delivery management procedures, raw materials warehouse management
procedures, finished goods warehouse management procedures, and finished
goods inventory operation manual, to offer detailed and comprehensive guidelines
for warehouse personnel in the effective management of inventory;
. Our finance team organizes comprehensive inventory inspection of the materials
in each warehouse on a quarterly, semi-annul and annual basis. The warehouse
management conducts spot checks of the materials on a monthly basis. Our
ERP-based system facilitates real-time monitoring of materials, tracking their
journey from procurement through on-site use, which has enhanced
accountability and optimized inventory management; and
. In accordance with HKAS 2, we had made sufficient loss provision for inventories
of nil, RMB1.3 million, RMB0.9 million and RMB1.0 million as of December 31,
2022, 2023, 2024, and the six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively.
Based on the aforementioned, we believe that sufficient provision had been made
accordingly during the Track Record Period.
