FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Movements of our trade and bills receivables were influenced by fluctuations in project
activities and payment schedules during the Track Record Period. As of June 30, 2025, our
trade and bills receivables decreased to RMB441.8 million from RMB522.0 million as of
December 31, 2024. This decrease was primarily attributable to the collection of trade and
bill receivables outstanding as of December 31, 2024 during the six months ended June 30,
2025, which exceeded the uncollected amount of newly issued invoices in the same period.
Our trade and bills receivables increased to RMB522.0 million as of December 31, 2024
from RMB451.7 million as of December 31, 2023, primarily because a significant number of
projects commenced in the second half or the fourth quarter of 2024, resulting in some trade
and bills receivables remaining outstanding as of the end of the year. As of December 31,
2023, our trade and bills receivables amounted to RMB451.7 million, reflecting an increase
of 30.3% from RMB346.6 million as of December 31, 2022 mainly because mainly because
(i) we had more projects reaching billing milestones at the end of 2023 due to the different
construction and billing schedules of our project pipelines; and (ii) a large amount of trade
and bills receivables were accumulated and carried forward to 2023.
Provision for impairment for trade and bills receivables increased to RMB64.4 million
as of December 31, 2023 from RMB43.8 million as of December 31, 2022, primarily due to
(i) the increase of the gross carrying amount of trade and bills receivables as of December
31, 2023; and (ii) the rise of credit risks for certain trade and bills receivables as we initiated
legal proceedings against certain customers. Provision for impairment for trade and bills
receivables further increased to RMB69.1 million as of December 31, 2024, primarily in line
with the increase in gross carrying amount. The provision was decreased to RMB67.7
million as of June 30, 2025.
The majority of our trade and bills receivables arise from credit terms provided to
customers. We implement stringent measures to manage receivables, including periodic
review of overdue balances by senior management. These efforts ensure robust credit risk
control.

relating to Customer R and the project owner, the project was suspended since December
2019. In 2023, as we had not received any notice of resumption, we initiated arbitration
proceedings against the relevant party. As of the Latest Practicable Date, the litigation was
still in progress. For details on this dispute, please refer to disclosure below; and (ii) in 2018,
we commenced two PS building subcontracting projects with a state-owned enterprise,
whose internal financial procedures involved numerous steps so that the payment schedule
was relatively slow. In 2024, we instituted arbitration proceedings against this customer and
were successful in obtaining an award in our favor. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we
had collected all the amounts due in respect of these two projects.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
The trade and bills receivables aged over two years increased from RMB20.8 million as
of December 31, 2023 to RMB32.5 million as of December 31, 2024, primarily because: (i)
in 2021, we carried out a PS building subcontracting project in Guangdong Province with
Customer N. The project was completed and passed inspection in 2023 and the buildings
have already been put into operation. In January and March 2025, we initiated one lawsuit
and one arbitration proceeding against Customer N, respectively. As at the Latest
Practicable Date, these proceedings were still in progress. For details, please refer to
disclosure below and ‘‘Business — Legal Compliance and Proceedings — Legal
Proceedings’’; (ii) in 2021, we carried out a PS building subcontracting project with a
state-owned enterprise, whose internal financial procedures involved numerous steps so that
the payment schedule was relatively slow. In 2024, we initiated arbitration proceedings
against such customer, and as of the Latest Practicable Date, the arbitration was still in
progress; and (iii) in 2019, we carried out a PS building subcontracting project in Thailand
with certain customer. During the project execution, the project owner requested additional
construction of hanging structures. The general contractor subcontracted this part of the
work to a third-party on its own initiative, but a dispute arose between us during the
settlement process. In 2024, we filed a lawsuit against the customer, and as of the Latest
Practicable Date, we were awarded in favor of the first-instance judgment.
The trade and bills receivables aged over two years decreased to RMB27.8 million as of
June 30, 2025 from RMB32.5 million as of December 31, 2024, reflecting our enhanced
efforts in collecting payments from customers. The trade and bills receivables of RMB5.0
million, which have been aged for over four years, are the subject of ongoing litigation. We
have successfully obtained a freeze on the counterparty’s bank account, which contains
sufficient funds to cover the full amount of these outstanding receivables. Due to the high
probability of recovery enabled by this enforcement measure, the amount remains classified
as receivables from an auditing standpoint. For further details regarding the ongoing legal
proceedings, please refer to the section headed ‘‘Business — Legal Compliance and
Proceedings — Legal Proceedings’’ in this prospectus.

to our suppliers, was in line with the changes of trade and bills receivables during the Track
Record Period. We will adjust our payment schedules with our suppliers depending on the
status of settlement of our trade receivables and our liquidity position through amicable
negotiation. We recorded relatively shorter trade and bills payables turnover days for the
year ended December 31, 2022, primarily because we completed a substantial amount of
construction work during that year, and we received progress payments from customers in a
timely manner. Similarly, for the six months ended June 30, 2025, we commenced and
carried out significant construction work and received progress payments from customers in
a timely manner. As a result, our payments to suppliers were relatively quick. In
comparison, for the years ended December 31, 2023 and 2024 during the relevant period to
better manage our liquidity position, we typically utilized the full credit terms offered by
our suppliers and engaged friendly negotiations with certain major suppliers to extend the
payment terms with them.

Gross Profit Margin
Our gross profit margin increased from 12.7% for the year ended December 31, 2022 to
14.8% for the year ended December 31, 2023, primarily because we secured a group of
large-scale PS building subcontracting projects in South China with total contract sum of
approximately RMB376.6 million with construction area exceeding 640,000 square meters.
In an effort to expand our market share, we secured these projects at a relatively lower gross
profit margin. Our gross profit margin decreased from 14.8% for the year ended December
31, 2023 to 12.5% for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to a substantial
increase in revenue from the general contracting business category, which had relatively
lower margin. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, our gross profit margin decreased
slightly to 10.2% from 11.9% for the six months ended June 30, 2024, primarily attributable
to the significant increase in revenue from our PS building subcontracting business
category, coupled with the relatively lower gross profit margin of this business category
during the period. For details, please refer to’’ — Period to Period Comparison of Results
of Operations’’ above.

FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT
We are exposed to various financial risks that could impact our financial position,
including credit risk, interest rate risk, liquidity risk, and currency risk. Below is an outline
of these risks and our strategies for managing them.
Credit Risk
Credit risk refers to the potential for financial loss if a customer or counterparty fails
to meet their contractual obligations. We are primarily exposed to credit risk through trade
and bills receivables, deposits, and other receivables. Our customer base consists
predominantly of established, creditworthy third parties, and we implement a rigorous
credit verification process for all customers trading on credit terms.
We actively monitor our receivable balances to effectively manage exposure to
potential bad debts. Our finance team regularly evaluates the financial condition of our
debtors and reviews aging receivables to ensure appropriate action is taken for overdue
balances. In addition, we have established a credit risk grading framework based on the
financial health and repayment histories of major customers and debtors.
Financial assets are assessed for impairment using a lifetime ECL model for
credit-impaired assets. For performing assets, we assess ECL using either a 12-month or
lifetime approach, depending on the risk of default. During the Track Record Period, no
impairment losses were recognized for deposits, other receivables, or amounts due from
related parties.
Our major bank balances are held with reputable institutions that have strong credit
ratings, and we do not anticipate any material loss from non-performance by these
institutions.
Interest Rate Risk
Interest rate risk arises from the potential impact of changes in interest rates on the fair
value or future cash flows of financial instruments. We are exposed to cash flow interest
rate risk from floating-rate instruments, such as bank balances, while fixed-rate instruments
expose us to fair value interest rate risk.
– 442 –

=== PAGE 453 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Currently, we do not have a formal policy to hedge interest rate risk but actively
monitor our exposure. As of December 31, 2022, 2023 and 2024 and June 30, 2025, our
primary exposure to interest rate risk was related to fixed-rate bank borrowings and lease
liabilities. While fluctuations in interest rates may affect the fair value of these fixed-rate
instruments, we consider the impact to be immaterial, given the relatively stable interest
rate environment.
Liquidity Risk
Liquidity risk represents the risk that we may encounter difficulties in fulfilling our
financial obligations when they become due. We manage liquidity prudently by ensuring
that we maintain adequate cash and cash equivalents, as well as sufficient credit facilities to
meet both short-term and long-term obligations. Our finance team actively monitors
liquidity needs and compliance with lending covenants, enabling us to meet our obligations
without incurring significant losses.
As of June 30, 2025, our financial liabilities included trade and bills payables, other
payables and accruals, amounts due to related parties, bank borrowings, and lease
liabilities. The contractual undiscounted cash flow obligations of these liabilities are
primarily due within one year or on demand. Based on our current liquidity position, we
believe we have sufficient financial resources to meet these obligations as they arise.
However, ongoing monitoring ensures we can quickly address any potential liquidity gaps.
For details, please refer to Note 47(c) to the Accountants’ Report as set out in Appendix I
to this prospectus.
Currency Risk
We are exposed to currency risk due to certain financial assets and liabilities, as well as
certain contracts, being denominated in foreign currencies. This exposes us to potential
exchange rate fluctuations, which could impact our financial results. While we do not
currently have a formal foreign currency hedging policy, our management regularly
monitors foreign exchange exposure and assesses potential risks. If our exposure to foreign
currency risk increases significantly, we will evaluate and implement appropriate hedging
strategies to mitigate this risk.
INVESTMENT POLICIES
Our Group generally invested in bank principal-guaranteed wealth management
products during the Track Record Period. We have established a set of investment policies
and internal control measures in respect of investing in financial assets which include:
. Clear investment objectives and principles: we aim to preserve and grow our
capital under controllable risk levels while maintaining sufficient liquidity to
support our operational needs. Our investment decisions are guided by the
principles of compliance, security, liquidity, reasonable return, and diversification
across asset classes, tenors and counterparties.
– 443 –

=== PAGE 454 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
. Permitted investment scope and restrictions: we allow investment in fixed income
instruments, including government bonds, policy bank bonds, high-rated
corporate bonds and bank-issued wealth management products. Equity and
derivative investments are allowed on a limited basis. We do not invest in
non-standard debt assets or bonds rated below AA. Exposure to any single wealth
management product is limited to no more than 10% of our total assets. High-risk
derivatives such as leveraged products or OTC (over-the-counter) options require
approval from the Board.
. Investment proposal and approval mechanism: We have implemented a tiered
investment approval structure based on the nature and size of the investment.
Investment proposals are initiated by the responsible personnel in the Finance
Department and submitted for approval in accordance with the authorization
level set out in our investment policy. For small-scale investments, defined as
principal-guaranteed bank products not exceeding 5% of our net assets, may be
approved by the head of the Finance Department. For medium-scale investments,
such as those exceeding 5% of net assets or involving non-principal-guaranteed
products, require collective approval by the Investment Committee. For
large-scale or high-risk investments, including those involving 10% or more of
our net assets or any derivative instruments, must be submitted to the Board for
approval.
. Internal control and monitoring: we maintain segregation of duties among
investment, execution, fund transfer and accounting teams. Personnel are not
permitted to concurrently hold responsibilities for both investment and risk
control functions. Internal audit conducts quarterly compliance reviews, and
external auditors perform annual audits. Investment performance and risk reports
are regularly submitted by the Finance Department to the management and the
Board and major risk events must be reported in a timely manner, generally within
two hours.
. Contingency measures: we have established contingency measures to address
liquidity stress and credit events, including access to emergency financing and
early warning systems for risk exposures, to safeguard the security and stability of
our financial asset portfolio.
Our investment policies are reviewed and updated annually by the Board and may be
subject to interim adjustments in response to significant market changes. All personnel
involved in investment activities are required to sign non-disclosure agreement and
compliance commitments.

DIVIDEND
We allow for dividend distributions to shareholders in cash or shares, in accordance
with our articles of association. We do not currently have a formal dividend policy or any
pre-determined dividend distribution ratio. Any final dividend declaration is subject to
shareholder approval before implementation. In making any dividend distribution, our
Board shall also consider various factors, including, among others, retained surplus and
distributable reserves, operating capital requirements, capital expenditure requirements and
future expansion plan, liquidity position, macroeconomic conditions, business cycles,
potential business impacts, and other internal or external factors affecting financial
performance. There is no guarantee that dividends will be presented or announced at any
given time.

REASONS FOR THE LISTING
Our decision to pursue the Listing reflects our commitment to strengthening our
market position, enhancing operational capacity, and fostering sustainable growth:
. Access to Capital for Strategic Growth: The Listing is anticipated to secure
substantial funding to execute our growth strategies effectively. A key focus
includes the expansion of our production capacity through a balanced approach
that optimizes in-house core capacities and integrates outsourced resources. This
sustainable strategy ensures efficient utilization of resources while supporting the
scaling of our core PS building subcontracting service business category. Beyond
domestic enhancements, the proceeds are expected to support global expansion.
By establishing new facilities and acquiring advanced manufacturing technologies,
we aim to improve operational efficiency and scalability to address growing
market needs.
. Enhancing Market Visibility and Credibility: As a publicly listed company, we
anticipate enhancing our brand visibility, credibility, and reputation in the global
market. This elevated profile is likely to instill greater trust among existing and
potential customers, particularly in international markets, and reinforce our
position in China’s industrial sector of the PS building market. Furthermore, the
Listing will position us to pursue strategic acquisitions and investments, providing
access to a more transparent and fair market valuation of the targets.
. Diversifying Funding Sources: The Listing is expected to provide access to
diversified funding channels, reducing reliance on traditional debt financing. This
diversification enhances financial flexibility, enabling us to respond swiftly to new
opportunities and market demands.
. Strengthening Corporate Governance: The Listing is also anticipated to support
the adoption of enhanced corporate governance practices. As a publicly listed
company, we plan to ensure greater transparency and accountability, building
investor confidence and fostering sustainable shareholder value creation.
In general, the Listing represents a transformative step in our growth journey,
reflecting our strategic objectives of driving innovation, expanding our market presence,
and creating long-term value for stakeholders.

FUTURE PLANS AND USE OF PROCEEDS
We believe that our expansion of production capacities in the PRC is supported by
sufficient demand, having considered: (i) although the overall growth of the construction
market is anticipated to decelerate compared to historical levels, the penetration rate of
prefabricated buildings in the PRC remains markedly lower than that in developed
countries such as the United States and Japan. This situation indicates significant potential
for future growth. Propelled by escalating labor costs and supportive government policies,
the penetration rate of prefabricated buildings in the PRC is forecast to keep rising. Within
the prefabricated building market, PS buildings, owing to their natural compatibility with
industrial facilities, are witnessing an increasing penetration rate, making this the
sub-segment with the most rapid growth. Moreover, within the PS building market, the
rapid development of new energy and advanced manufacturing sectors has been driving
strong demand for industrial buildings. According to F&S Report, the PS building market
is expected to expand from RMB448.8 billion in 2025 to RMB555.1 billion in 2029, with a
CAGR of 5.3%. Specifically, the industrial sector of PS building market will have a CAGR
of 9.4%, significantly outpacing other sectors; (ii) within the industrial sector of PS building
market in the PRC, integrated PS building subcontracting projects stand out as the
fastest-growing category. According to the F&S Report, in future, as the PS building
market in the PRC matures and performance requirements become more stringent, the
integrated PS building subcontracting project is expected to continue growing from
RMB31.6 billion in 2025 to RMB53.4 billion in 2029, with a CAGR of 14.0%, higher than
the 6.5% of general contracting project and the 9.3% of other subcontracting project within
the industrial sector of the PS building market; (iii) we currently have an annual production
capacity of 51,880 tons of PS building components, which is not sufficient for growing
needs from our customers. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, the utilization rate of
our PS building components has reached 158.7%. Moreover, during the Track Record
Period, we delivered a total of approximately 530,000 tons of PS building components
across all projects, with approximately 206,000 tons manufactured in-house and the
remaining outsourced to outsourced product providers. Therefore, there is an imperative
need for us to further expand our production capacity to meet the increasing demands of
construction projects from our customers; and (iv) we also plan to allocate partial expanded
production capacity in the PRC to our overseas projects, with a strategic focus on Southeast
Asia.
We believe we possess a competitive edge in the industrial sector of the PS building
market. This stems from several key factors: (i) we operate as an integrated PS building
subcontracting service provider, providing customers with comprehensive services spanning
project design and optimization, procurement, production, and installation; (ii) we have
built a long-standing relationship with leading enterprises across a wide array of industries
and certain of them have maintained business relationships with us for over 20 years; (iii)
the extensive industry experience of our management team empower us to promptly
capitalize on market opportunities. Currently, we are actively expanding into Southeast
Asian market, leveraging its rapid economic growth and rising demand of PS buildings; and
(iv) we have been actively exploring diversified end-use applications for PS buildings, as
exemplified by our Curvet Dual-Wave Arch Warehouse Series used in the agricultural
storage applications field. This addressed a critical gap in China’s agricultural
infrastructure in the industrial sector of the PS building market. For further details on
our competitive strengths, please refer to ‘‘Business — Strengths’’ in this prospectus.

(b) Advanced Equipment Procurement
Approximately 16.0% (HK$26.3 million) of the net proceeds will be allocated to
procure and integrate advanced manufacturing technologies to enhance our production
capabilities.
This initiative will focus on strategic investments in cutting-edge equipment to support
the expansion of our production capabilities. Funds will be directed towards acquiring
high-speed, automated machinery for the PS building components production line,
enhancing both production efficiency and product quality. Investments will also be made
in our current production lines, including the acquisition of welding machines, painting
equipment, and laser cutting machines to improve precision and surface quality.
Additionally, compressors, sandblasting equipment, and overhead cranes will be
introduced to optimize production processes and material handling.
These investments align with our strategic commitment to adopting intelligent
manufacturing practices. The integration of such technologies will enhance production
precision, streamline workflows, and enable real-time data-driven decision-making. We
plan to progressively allocate funds from 2025 to 2029 to achieve this goal.
(c) Overseas Expansion
Approximately 6.7% (HK$11.0 million) of the net proceeds will be allocated to
support our international expansion in Southeast Asia. This initiative focuses on
establishing a production facility in Thailand with an annual production capacity of
15,000 tons of PS building components, which is expected to commence the initial
production by end of 2026. This initiative will enable us to meet the growing demand for PS
buildings in the region.
The establishment of the new production facility will involve land leasing, facility
construction and purchase of major machinery and equipment. We expect to establish the
new production facility by the following timeframe:
. Land acquisition/leasing : By first quarter of 2026
. Commencement of the
expansion/construction : By second quarter of 2026
. Completion of the expansion/
construction : By end of 2026
The establishment of a new production facility in Thailand may be subject to various
regulatory approvals and licenses, including Factory License, Construction and Building
Permits, Environmental Impact Assessment and other industry-specific licenses and
registrations as applicable. The approvals and licenses requirements may change due to
– 452 –

FUTURE PLANS AND USE OF PROCEEDS
different stages of the project. As advised by our Thailand Legal Advisers, there is no legal
impediment for us which are currently identified to prevent obtaining these approvals and
licenses at this stage.
The total capital expenditure for the establishment of the new production facility is
estimated to be approximately RMB25.0 million (equivalent to approximately HK$27.5
million).
According to the F&S Report, the market for PS buildings in Southeast Asia is
expected to grow at a CAGR of 12.2% from 2025 to 2029, reaching US$2.2 billion by 2029.
Key countries such as Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia and Thailand are experiencing
heightened demand for efficient and scalable construction services, creating significant
opportunities for market penetration. The PS building market is Southeast Asia is currently
fragmented, with the overall market concentration being less than 2%. For further details
on the competitive landscape in Southeast Asia, please refer to ‘‘Industry Overview —
Analysis of China’s Prefabricated Steel Structure Building Market — Market Status
Analysis of Prefabricated Steel Structure Building in Southeast Asia’’ in this prospectus.
Leveraging our design and production capabilities, we plan to establish the production
facility locally to scale our operations in Southeast Asia.
We plan to fund the construction of this production line through net proceeds
generated from the Global Offering, cash generated from operating activities, bank
borrowings, or equity and debt fund raising. This initiative reflects our commitment to
fostering regional economic development through job creation, technology transfer, and
sustainable construction practices.
(ii) Funding Initial Costs for New Projects
Approximately 26.7% (HK$43.8 million) of the net proceeds will be allocated to
finance upfront costs associated with new projects.
We generally incur a substantial amount of up-front costs during the initial stage of
our construction projects, mainly including cost of materials and other operational cost,
representing approximately 15% to 45% of the total contract value of the respective
project. After signing the agreement with customers, we are typically entitled to receiving
advance payment, generally ranging from 20% to 30% of the total contract value of the
respective project, which is in line with industry practice. We will commence the
procurement of raw materials, contracting with outsourced product providers and the
arrangement of in-house production capacity, incurring up-front costs. According to the
agreement with customers, we are entitled to receive progress payments upon achievement
of certain key milestones as stipulated in the agreements, which would enable us to start
billing at an agreed percentage of the total amount of work we performed. In addition, we
are usually required to provide a defect liability period ranging from one to two years, and
retention money (generally no more than 5% of the settlement payment value) will only be
released to us upon its expiration. The advance payments received by us may be insufficient
to meet the funding need of our up-front costs. Consequently, we generally need to finance
this gap before we receive the progress payment per project milestones from our customers.
– 453 –

=== PAGE 464 ===
FUTURE PLANS AND USE OF PROCEEDS
During the Track Record Period, we funded such gap of up-front costs mainly with our
working capital and bank borrowings. According to F&S, such payment arrangements are
common practice in our industry.
Our Directors are of the view that it is not practical to allocate our net proceeds from
Global Offering to our construction projects on hand or potential construction projects
with tenders submitted as of the Latest Practicable Date as the upfront expenditure of these
projects is expected to be incurred and paid before the expected Listing Date, taking
account into the expected construction schedule of these projects. Therefore, we intend to
allocate approximately 26.7% of our estimated net proceeds, or HK$43.8 million
(equivalent to approximately RMB39.9 million) to fund the up-front costs of our
potential construction projects in the future. We believe our potential projects will be of
similar nature and type to our historic construction projects and will be selected through
our project identification and selection processes. Our Directors and management are
committed to monitoring the market dynamics in the PS building industry, capturing the
business opportunities which are favorable to the expansion of our Group, and using their
best efforts to secure profitable and high quality projects for us.
In the event that the net proceeds allocated for funding upfront costs are insufficient to
fully cover the requirements of the projects we successfully secure, we plan to bridge the
funding gap through cash generated from operating activities, bank borrowings, or equity
and debt fund raising.
(iii) Sales and Marketing Development
Approximately 12.3% (HK$20.2 million) of the net proceeds will be allocated to
support sales and marketing development, encompassing the establishment of sales and
operational teams and the commercialization of our agricultural storage products. These
investments aim to strengthen market presence, improve customer engagement, and capture
emerging business opportunities.
. Approximately 10.3% (HK$16.9 million) of the net proceeds will be dedicated to
establishing and expanding sales and operational teams. We plan to build overseas
teams in Southeast Asia, such as Thailand and Malaysia, focusing on expanding
our presence in key international markets and addressing the growing demand for
PS buildings. These teams will enhance localized customer engagement, improve
responsiveness to market needs, and provide on-the-ground support for executing
strategic projects.
. Approximately 2.0% (HK$3.3 million) of the net proceeds will be allocated to the
commercialization of agricultural storage and APC products. This initiative will
focus on promoting awareness. Funds will support market research to better
understand regional needs, refine product and service offerings, and identify
potential markets. Resources will also be directed toward targeted promotional
activities, including participation in industry exhibitions and conferences, as well
as creating materials to highlight the advantages of our products and services.

(iv) Strategic Acquisitions and Investments
Approximately 9.3% (HK$15.3 million) of the net proceeds will be reserved for
selective acquisitions and investments aimed at strengthening our supply chain and
enhancing our technical capabilities. When presented with favorable opportunities, we may
employ various investment formats, including acquisition to acquire controlling stake,
investing in partial interests or alliance with other companies to form joint venture. The
number of companies we acquire will depend on the availability of suitable opportunities
and our financial resources at such time. The focus will be on investing companies with
expertise in PS building components, in particular, the upstream material and prefabricated
components manufacturing companies, which are integral to improving the efficiency,
quality, and sustainability of our PS building subcontracting services.
We plan to target companies that are in a stable development stage, demonstrating a
consistent track record of growth and operational excellence. The ideal candidates will be
(i) led by experienced senior management teams with at least ten years of relevant industry
expertise, ensuring that the companies possess the leadership and strategic vision necessary
to integrate seamlessly into our operations. Additionally, we will focus on companies with
management experience between ten to 15 years, an operation of five to ten years and/or an
annual revenue of approximately RMB50.0 million or above. These acquisitions are
expected to streamline our supply chain by enhancing procurement, production, and
distribution efficiencies while also incorporating advanced technologies and specialized
expertise into our operations. As advised by F&S, considering the highly fragmented nature
of the industry and ample market participants of over 2,000, there are sufficient target
companies in the market. Based on the view of F&S and our understanding of the market,
our Directors are of the opinion that there are sufficient target companies in the market.
We believe that the strategic acquisition and investment may: (i) increase our business
scale by integrating both the production capacity and the customer base of the acquired
companies; (ii) optimize our supply chains by sourcing our materials and prefabricated
components at more competitive prices; and (iii) enable us to share the latest information
and technologies within the industry, which in turn, will enhance our operational efficiency
and quality of services offered to our customers.
As of the Latest Practicable Date, we have not identified any specific strategic
investment or acquisition targets.

FUTURE PLANS AND USE OF PROCEEDS
(v) Research and Development Investments
Approximately 9.0% (HK$14.8 million) of the net proceeds will be allocated to
enhancing our research and development capabilities, focusing on the improvement of our
products and technologies. This investment will be divided into three key initiatives:
. Approximately 3.7% (HK$6.1 million) will be allocated to developing a
digitalized factory, by incorporating advanced IIoT technologies and machinery
in our current production facility. This includes the procurement and installation
of IoT devices such as sensors, smart meters, and wireless communication
modules to enable real-time monitoring of critical parameters like temperature,
humidity, pressure, and operational time. These devices enable us to further
enhance operational efficiency and product quality. The establishment of a robust
wireless network will ensure secure, stable data transmission, facilitating seamless
communication between machines and systems, and driving intelligent
manufacturing processes.
. Approximately 4.1% (HK6.7 million) will be used to upgrade our existing product
lines and technologies, as well as to develop new innovative products.
. Approximately 1.2% (HK$2.0 million) will be directed towards upgrading our
current ERP and Office Automation (OA) systems. These enhancements will
streamline workflows, improve process integration, and lay a stronger foundation
for future digital operations, enhancing efficiency across the organization.
Despite the decrease research and development expenses incurred by us during the
Track Record Period, we believe that research and development are of importance to our
operation and development, primarily because: (i) we need to consistently develop and
adopt innovative construction services and products for our customers to respond to their
various needs; and (ii) we need to improve our operational efficiency and reduce our costs
so as to maintain or enhance our competitiveness in the pricing.
(vi) Working Capital and General Corporate Purposes
Approximately 5.0% (HK$8.2 million) will be allocated for working capital and
general corporate purposes to support our day-to-day operations and maintain financial
flexibility.
In the event that the designated net proceeds are insufficient to fully fund the
aforementioned purposes, we intend to utilize internal resources or equity debt financing to
address any shortfalls. Conversely, should there be surplus funds, these will be applied
toward other projects consistent with our strategic objectives.

commercial and investment banking, brokerage, funds management, trading, hedging,

ordinary course of their various business activities, the Syndicate Members and their
respective affiliates may purchase, sell or hold a broad array of investments and actively
trade securities, derivatives, loans, commodities, currencies, credit default swaps and other
financial instruments for their own account and for the accounts of their customers. Such
investment and trading activities may involve or relate to assets, securities and/or
instruments of our Company and/or persons and entities with relationships with our

hedging purposes in connection with our Group’s loans and other debt. In relation to the
Shares, the activities of the Syndicate Members and their affiliates could include acting as
agent for buyers and sellers of the Shares, entering into transactions with those buyers and
sellers in a principal capacity, including as a lender to initial purchasers of the Shares
(which financing may be secured by the Shares) in the Global Offering, proprietary trading
in the Shares, and entering into over the counter or listed derivative transactions or listed or
unlisted securities transactions (including issuing securities such as derivative warrants
listed on a stock exchange) which have as their underlying assets, assets including the
Shares. Such transactions may be carried out as bilateral agreements or trades with selected
counterparties. Those activities may require hedging activity by those entities involving,
directly or indirectly, the buying and selling of the Shares, which may have a negative
impact on the trading price of the Shares. All such activities could occur in Hong Kong and
elsewhere in the world and may result in the Syndicate Members and their affiliates holding
long and/or short positions in the Shares, in baskets of securities or indices including the
Shares, in units of funds that may purchase the Shares, or in derivatives related to any of
the foregoing.
In relation to issues by Syndicate Members or their affiliates of any listed securities
having the Shares as their underlying securities, whether on the Stock Exchange or on any
other stock exchange, the rules of the stock exchange may require the issuer of those
securities (or one of its affiliates or agents) to act as a market maker or liquidity provider in
the security, and this will also result in hedging activity in the Shares in most cases.

STABILIZATION
Stabilization is a practice used by underwriters in some markets to facilitate the
distribution of securities. To stabilize, the underwriters may bid for, or purchase, the
securities in the secondary market, during a specified period of time, to retard and, if
possible, prevent a decline in the initial public market price of the securities below the offer
price. Such transactions may be effected in all jurisdictions where it is permissible to do so,
in each case in compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, including
those of Hong Kong. In Hong Kong, the price at which stabilization is effected is not
permitted to exceed the offer price.
In connection with the Global Offering, the Stabilizing Manager, or any person acting
for it, on behalf of the Underwriters, may over-allocate or effect transactions with a view to
stabilizing or supporting the market price of our Shares at a level higher than that which
might otherwise prevail in the open market for a limited period after the Listing Date.
However, there is no obligation on the Stabilizing Manager or any persons acting for it to
conduct any such stabilizing action. Such stabilizing action, if taken, will be conducted at
the absolute discretion of the Stabilizing Manager or any person acting for it and may be
discontinued at any time, and is required to be ended on the 30th day after the last day for
lodging applications under the Hong Kong Public Offering.
– 477 –

=== PAGE 488 ===
STRUCTURE OF THE GLOBAL OFFERING
Stabilization action permitted in Hong Kong under the Securities and Futures (Price
Stabilizing) Rules of the SFO includes (i) over-allocating for the purpose of preventing or
minimizing any reduction in the market price of our Shares, (ii) selling or agreeing to sell
our Shares so as to establish a short position in them for the purpose of preventing or
minimizing any reduction in the market price of our Shares, (iii) purchasing, or agreeing to
purchase, our Shares pursuant to the Over-allotment Option in order to close out any
position established under (i) or (ii) above, (iv) purchasing, or agreeing to purchase, any of
our Shares for the sole purpose of preventing or minimizing any reduction in the market
price of our Shares, (v) selling or agreeing to sell any Shares in order to liquidate any
position established as a result of those purchases, and (vi) offering or attempting to do
anything as described in (ii), (iii), (iv) or (v) above.
Specifically, prospective applicants for and investors in Shares should note that:
. the Stabilizing Manager (or any person acting for it) may, in connection with the
stabilizing action, maintain a long position in the Shares;
. there is no certainty as to the extent to which and the time or period for which the
Stabilizing Manager (or any person acting for it) will maintain such a long
position;
. liquidation of any such long position by the Stabilizing Manager (or any person
acting for it) and selling in the open market may have an adverse impact on the
market price of the Shares;
. no stabilizing action can be taken to support the price of the Shares for longer
than the stabilizing period which will begin on the Listing Date and is expected to
expire on Thursday, January 22, 2026 being the 30th day after the last day for
lodging applications under the Hong Kong Public Offering. After this date, when
no further action may be taken to support the price of the Shares, demand for the
Shares, and therefore the price of the Shares, could fall;
. the price of the Shares cannot be assured to stay at or above the Offer Price by the
taking of any stabilizing action; and
. stabilizing bids or transactions effected during the stabilizing action may be made
at any price at or below the Offer Price, which means that stabilizing bids or
transactions effected may be made at a price below the price paid by applicants
for, or investors in, the Offer Shares.
Our Company will ensure or procure that an announcement in compliance with the
Securities and Futures (Price Stabilizing) Rules of the SFO will be made within seven days
of the expiration of the stabilization period.

Following any over-allocation of Shares in connection with the Global Offering, the

PRICING AND ALLOCATION
Our Company and the Sole Overall Coordinator (for itself and on behalf of the
Underwriters) will determine the Offer Price and sign an agreement on the Price
Determination Date, when market demand for the Offer Shares will be determined. The
Price Determination Date is expected to be on or around Wednesday, December 24, 2025
and in any event, not later than 12:00 noon on Wednesday, December 24, 2025.
The Offer Price will not be more than HK$9.16 per Offer Share and is expected to be
not less than HK$7.10 per Offer Share, unless otherwise announced, as further explained
below. If you apply for the Offer Shares under the Hong Kong Public Offering, you may be
required to pay the maximum price of HK$9.16 per Offer Share (subject to application
channels), plus brokerage of 1.0%, SFC transaction levy of 0.0027%, Stock Exchange
trading fee of 0.00565% and AFRC transaction levy of 0.00015%, amounting to a total of
HK$2,775.71 for one board lot of 300 Shares.
If the Offer Price, as finally determined in the manner described below, is lower than
HK$7.10, we will refund the respective difference, including brokerage, SFC transaction
levy, Stock Exchange trading fee and AFRC transaction levy attributable to the surplus
application monies (subject to application channels). We will not pay interest on any
refunded amounts. For more details, please refer to the section headed ‘‘How to Apply for
Hong Kong Offer Shares’’ in this prospectus.
The International Underwriters will be soliciting from prospective investors
indications of interest in acquiring Offer Shares in the International Offering. Prospective
professional and institutional investors will be required to specify the number of Offer

Introduction
We report on the historical financial information of USAS Building System (Shanghai)
Co., Ltd. (美聯鋼結構建築系統（上海）股份有限公司) (the ‘‘Company’’) and its subsidiaries
(together, the ‘‘Group’’) set out on pages I-4 to I-110, which comprises the consolidated
statements of financial position of the Group and the statements of financial position of the
Company as at 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and 30 June 2025, and the consolidated
statements of profit or loss and other comprehensive income, the consolidated statements of
changes in equity and the consolidated statements of cash flows, for each of the years ended
31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and the period ended 30 June 2025 (the ‘‘Track Record
Period’’), and material accounting policy information and other explanatory information
(together, the ‘‘Historical Financial Information’’). The Historical Financial Information set
out on pages I-4 to I-110 forms an integral part of this report, which has been prepared for
inclusion in the Document of the Company dated 18 December 2025 (the ‘‘Document’’) in
connection with the initial listing of shares (the ‘‘Listing’’) of the Company on the Main
Board of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (the ‘‘Stock Exchange’’).
Directors’ responsibility for the Historical Financial Information
The directors of the Company are responsible for the preparation of the Historical
Financial Information that gives a true and fair view in accordance with the basis of
preparation set out in Note 2 to the Historical Financial Information, and for such internal
control as the directors of the Company determine is necessary to enable the preparation of
the Historical Financial Information that is free from material misstatement, whether due
to fraud or error.
Reporting accountants’ responsibility
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Historical Financial Information and
to report our opinion to you. We conducted our work in accordance with Hong Kong
Standard on Investment Circular Reporting Engagements 200 ‘‘Accountants’ Reports on
Historical Financial Information in Investment Circulars’’ issued by the Hong Kong
Institute of Certified Public Accountants (the ‘‘HKICPA’’). This standard requires that we

was subsequently delisted on 10 December 2024. The address of the Company’s registered office and principal
place of incorporation is 208 Jiangtian Road East, Songjiang Industry Park, Songjiang District, Shanghai,
China,201613.TheultimateparentoftheCompanyisBroadVisionInternationalGroupLimited(incorporated
inHongKong)andtheultimatecontrollingpartyareMr.BrianB.Y.ChenandMs.AngelaChenMah,whoare
also the Chairman and Director of the Company, respectively.
TheGroupisprincipallyengagedin(i)prefabricatedsteelstructurebuilding(‘‘PSbuildingsubcontracting
services’’); (ii) general contracting services; and (iii) industrial environmental equipment.
2 BASIS OF PREPARATION OF HISTORICAL FINANCIAL INFORMATION
The Historical Financial Information has been prepared in accordance with all applicable HKFRS
AccountingStandardswhichcollectivetermincludesallapplicableHongKongFinancialReportingStandards,
Hong Kong Accounting Standards, (‘‘HKASs’’) and Interpretations issued by the HKICPA. Further details of
the material accounting policy information are set out in Note 3.
TheHKICPAhasissuedanumberofnewandrevisedHKFRSAccountingStandards.Forthepurposeof
preparingthisHistoricalFinancialInformation,theGrouphasadoptedallapplicablenewandrevisedHKFRS
AccountingStandardstotheTrackRecordPeriod,exceptforanynewstandardsorinterpretationsthatarenot
yeteffectivefortheTrackRecordPeriod.Therevisedandnewaccountingstandardsandinterpretationsissued
but not yet effective for the Track Record Period are set out in note 48.
TheHistoricalFinancialInformationalsocomplieswiththeapplicabledisclosureprovisionsoftheRules
Governing the Listing of Securities on the Stock Exchange.
The accounting policies set out below have been applied consistently to all periods presented in the
Historical Financial information.
TheHistoricalFinancialInformationispreparedinRenminbi(‘‘RMB’’)andallvaluesareroundedtothe
nearest thousand (RMB’000) except when otherwise indicated.
3 MATERIAL ACCOUNTING POLICY INFORMATION
(a) Basis of measurement
ThefunctionalcurrencyoftheCompanyisRMB,whichisthesameasthepresentationcurrencyof
the Historical Financial Information.
The measurement basis used in the preparation of the Historical Financial Information is the
historical cost basis, except for the certain financial assets that are measured at fair value.

APPENDIX I ACCOUNTANTS’ REPORT
(b) Use of estimates and judgments
The preparation of Historical Financial Information in conformity with HKFRS Accounting
Standardsrequiresmanagementtomakejudgments,estimatesandassumptionsthataffecttheapplication
of policies and reported amounts of assets, liabilities, income and expenses. The estimates and associated
assumptionsarebasedonhistoricalexperienceandvariousotherfactorsthatarebelievedtobereasonable
under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis of making the judgments about carrying
values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources. Actual results may differ
from these estimates.
The estimates and underlying assumptions are reviewed on an ongoing basis. Revisions to
accounting estimates are recognized in the period in which the estimate is revised if the revision affects
onlythatperiod,orintheperiodoftherevisionandfutureperiodsiftherevisionaffectsbothcurrentand
future periods.
Judgments made by management in the application of HKFRS Accounting Standards that have
material effect on the Historical Financial Information and major sources of estimation uncertainty are
discussed in Note 4.
(c) Subsidiaries and non-controlling interests
Subsidiaries are entities controlled by the Company. The Company controls an entity when it is
exposed to, or has rights to, variable returns from its involvement with the entity and has the ability to
affectthosereturnsthroughitspowerovertheentity.Thefinancialstatementsofsubsidiariesareincluded
intheHistoricalFinancialInformationfromthedateonwhichcontrolcommencesuntilthedateonwhich
control ceases.
Intra-group balances and transactions, and any unrealised income and expenses (except for foreign
currency transaction gains or losses) arising from intra-group transactions, are eliminated. Unrealised
lossesresultingfromintra-grouptransactionsareeliminatedinthesamewayasunrealisedgains,butonly
to the extent that there is no evidence of impairment.
For each business combination, the Group can elect to measure any non-controlling interests
(‘‘NCI’’)eitheratfairvalueorattheNCI’sproportionateshareofthesubsidiary’snetidentifiableassets.
NCI are presented in the consolidated statements of financial position within equity, separately
from equity attributable to the equity shareholders of the Company. NCI in the results of the Group are
presented on the face of the consolidated statements of profit or loss and other comprehensive income as
anallocationofthetotalprofitorlossandtotalcomprehensiveincomefortheyearbetweenNCIandthe
equity shareholders of the Company.
ChangesintheGroup’sinterestsinasubsidiarythatdonotresultinalossofcontrolareaccounted
for as equity transactions.
When the Group loses control of a subsidiary, it derecognises the assets and liabilities of the
subsidiary,andanyrelatedNCIandothercomponentsofequity.Anyresultinggainorlossisrecognized
in profit or loss. Any interest retained in that formersubsidiary is measured at fair value when control is
lost.
IntheCompany’sstatementsoffinancialposition,interestsinsubsidiariesarestatedatcostlessany
impairmentloss,unlessitisclassifiedasheldforsale(orincludedinadisposalgroupclassifiedasheldfor
sale).

(d) Property, plant and equipment
Property,plantandequipmentarestatedatcostlessaccumulateddepreciationandanyaccumulated
impairment losses.
The cost of property, plant and equipment includes its purchase price and the costs directly
attributable costs of bringing the asset to the working condition and location for its intended use.
Expenditure incurred after items of property, plant and equipment have been put into operation, such as
repairs and maintenance, is normally charged to profit or loss in the period in which it is incurred. In
situations where it can be demonstrated that the expenditure has resulted in an increase in the future
economicbenefitsexpectedtobeobtainedfromtheuseofanitemofproperty,plantandequipment,and
wherethecostoftheitemcanbemeasuredreliably,theexpenditureiscapitalizedasanadditionalcostof
that asset or as a replacement.
Depreciationiscalculatedtowrite-offthecostofitemsofproperty,plantandequipment,otherthan
construction in progress, less their estimated residual values, if any, using the straight-line method over
their estimated useful lives as follows:
Estimated useful lives
Owned buildings 20 years
Leasehold improvements Over the lease term
Plant and machinery 3–10 years
Office equipment 5 years
Motor vehicles 5 years
Residual value, useful lives and depreciation method are reviewed, and adjusted if appropriate, at
the end of each reporting period during the Track Record Period.
Construction in progress represents machinery and other assets under construction or installation,
which is stated at cost less any impairment losses. Cost comprises the direct costs of construction,
installation, testing as well as borrowing costs capitalized during the period of construction.
Capitalisation of these costs ceases and the construction in progress is transferred to the appropriate
classofproperty,plantandequipmentwhensubstantiallyalltheactivitiesnecessarytopreparetheassets
for their intended use are completed. No depreciation is provided in respect of construction in progress
until it is completed and ready for its intended use.
An item of property, plant and equipment is derecognized upon disposal or when no future
economic benefits are expected from its use or disposal. Any gain or loss on disposal or retirement of an
itemofproperty,plantandequipmentisdeterminedasthedifferencebetweenthenetsaleproceedsandits
carrying amount of the item and is recognized in profit or loss.
(e) Investment properties
Property that is held for long-term rental yields or for capital appreciation or both, and that is not
occupied by the Group, is classified as investment property.
InvestmentpropertycompriseslandheldunderoperatingleasesandbuildingsownedbytheGroup.
Landheldunderoperatingleasesareclassifiedandaccountedforasinvestmentpropertywhentherestof
the definition of investment property is met. The operating lease is accounted for as if it were a finance
lease.
– I-19 –

=== PAGE 532 ===
APPENDIX I ACCOUNTANTS’ REPORT
Investmentpropertiesareinitiallymeasuredatcost,includinganydirectlyattributableexpenditure.
Subsequent to initial recognition, investment properties are stated at cost less subsequent accumulated
depreciationandanyaccumulatedimpairmentlosses.Depreciationisrecognizedsoastowriteoffthecost
of investment properties over their estimated useful lives and after taking into account of their estimated
residual value, using the straight-line method.
An investment property is derecognized upon disposal or when the investment property is
permanently withdrawn from use and no future economic benefits are expected from its disposals. Any
gainorlossarisingonderecognitionoftheproperty(calculatedasthedifferencebetweenthenetdisposal
proceeds and the carrying amount of the asset) is included in the profit or loss in the period in which the
property is derecognized.

(ii) Impairment loss on financial assets
The Group recognizes loss allowances for expected credit loss (‘‘ECLs’’) on trade and bills
receivables, contract assets, other financial assets measured at amortized cost and debt investment
measured at FVTOCI.
ECLs are probability-weighted estimate of credit losses. Credit losses are measured at the
differencebetweenthecontractualcashflowsdueinaccordancewiththecontractandthecashflows
that the Group expects to receive, discounted at an approximation of the original effective interest
rate.
The ECLs are measured on either of the following bases: (1) 12 months ECLs: these are the
ECLsthatresultfrompossibledefaulteventswithinthe12monthsafterthereportingdate:and(2)
lifetimeECLs:theseareECLsthatresultfromallpossibledefaulteventsovertheexpectedlifeofa
financial instrument. The maximum period considered when estimating ECLs is the maximum
contractual period over which the Group is exposed to credit risk.

The Group measures loss allowances for trade receivables and contract assets using a
simplified approach and has calculated ECLs based on lifetime ECLs. The Group has established a
provision matrix that is based on the Group’s historical credit loss experience, adjusted for
forward-looking factors specific to the debtors and the economic environment.
For other debt financial assets, the Group applies the general approach and the ECLs are
recognized based on the 12-month ECLs. However, when there has been a significant increase in
credit risk since origination, the allowance will be based on the lifetime ECLs.
Depending on thenature of thefinancial instruments, theassessment of a significant increase
increditriskisperformedoneitheranindividualbasisoracollectivebasis.Whentheassessmentis
performed on a collective basis, the financial instruments are grouped based on shared credit risk
characteristics, such as past due status and credit risk ratings.
ECLs are remeasured at each reporting date to reflect changes in the financial instrument’s
credit risk since initial recognition. Any change in the ECL amount is recognized as an impairment
gain or loss in profit or loss. The Group recognizes an impairment gain or loss for all financial
instruments with a corresponding adjustment to their carrying amount through a loss allowance
account.
For internal credit risk management, the Group considers an event of default occurs when
information developed internally or obtained from external sources indicates that the debtor is
unlikelytopayitscreditors,includingtheGroup,infull(withouttakingintoaccountanycollaterals
held by the Group).

Afinancialassetiscredit-impairedwhenoneormoreeventsofdefaultthathaveadetrimental
impact on the estimated future cash flows of that financial asset have occurred. Evidence that a
financial asset is credit-impaired includes observable data about the following events:
(a) significant financial difficulty of the issuer or the borrower;
(b) a breach of contract, such as a default or past due event;
(c) the lender(s) of the borrower, for economic or contractual reasons relating to the
borrower’s financial difficulty, having granted to the borrower a concession(s) that the
lender(s) would not otherwise consider;
(d) it is becoming probable that the borrower will enter bankruptcy or other financial
reorganization; or

difficulties.

(l) Income tax
Income tax expense comprises current tax and deferred tax. It is recognized in profit or loss except
totheextentthatitrelatestoabusinesscombination,oritemsrecognizedindirectlyinequityorinother
comprehensive income.
Current tax comprises the estimated tax payableor receivable on thetaxable income or loss for the
year and any adjustments to the tax payable or receivable in respect of previous years. The amount of
current tax payable or receivable is the best estimate of the tax amount expected to be paid or received
that reflects any uncertainty related to income taxes. It is measured using tax rates enacted or
substantively enacted at each reporting date. Current tax also includes any tax arising from dividends.
Current tax assets and liabilities are offset only if certain criteria are met.
Deferred tax is recognized in respect of temporary differences between the carrying amounts of
assets and liabilities for financial reporting purposes and the amounts used for taxation purposes.
Deferred tax is not recognized for:
— temporary differences on the initial recognition of assets or liabilities in a transaction that is
not a business combination and that affects neither accounting nor taxable profit or loss and
does not give rise to equal taxable and deductible temporary differences;
— temporarydifferencesrelatedtoinvestmentinsubsidiariestotheextentthattheGroupisable
to control the timing of the reversal of the temporary differences and it is probable that they
will not reverse in the foreseeable future; and
— taxable temporary differences arising on the initial recognition of goodwill.

4 CRITICAL ACCOUNTING JUDGMENTS AND KEY SOURCES OF ESTIMATION UNCERTAINTY
IntheapplicationoftheGroup’saccounting policies, thedirectors oftheCompany arerequiredtomake
judgments, estimates and assumptions about the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities that are not readily
apparent from other sources. The estimates and associated assumptions are based on historical experience and
other factors that are considered to be relevant. Actual results differ from these estimates.
The estimates and underlying assumptions are reviewed on an ongoing basis. Revisions to accounting
estimatesarerecognizedintheperiodinwhichtheestimateisrevisediftherevisionaffectsonlythatperiodorin
the period of the revision and future periods if the revision affects both current and future periods.
Critical judgment in applying accounting policies
The following is the critical judgment, apart from those involving estimations (see below), that the
directors have made in the process of applying the Group’s accounting policies and that have the most
significanteffectontheamountsrecognizedanddisclosuresmadeintheHistoricalFinancialInformation.
(i) Recognition of contract revenue
The Group recognizes revenue from provision of PS building subcontracting services and general
contracting services over time by measuring the progress towards complete satisfaction of the relevant
performance obligation. The progress is determined based on the Group’s efforts or inputs to the
satisfaction of a performance obligation relative to the total expected inputs to the satisfaction of that
performance obligation by reference to the proportion of the actual costs incurred relative to the total
expectedcontractcosts,thatbestdepicttheGroup’sperformanceincreatingorenhancinganassetunder
the customer’s control. Notwithstanding that the management reviews and revises the estimates of total
costincurredandexpectedtobeincurredforeachindividualprojectasthecontractprogresses,theactual
outcome of the contract in terms of its total revenue and costs may be higher or lower than the estimates
and this will affect the revenue and profit recognized.

Key sources of estimation uncertainty
In addition to information disclosed elsewhere in the Historical Financial Information, other key
sources of estimation uncertainty that have significant risks of resulting in material adjustments to the
carrying amounts of assets and liabilities within next twelve months period are as follows:
(i) Provision of expected credit losses (‘‘ECLs’’) for contract assets and trade receivables
The Group works on PS building subcontracting services and general contracting services to
customers before the customers pay consideration or before payments are due, contract assets are
recognized for the earned considerations that are conditional. Contract assets are stated at cost less
impairment. In assessing the recoverability of the contract assets, the Group regularly reviews and
consider forward-looking information that may impact the customers’ ability to repay the outstanding
balances in order to estimate the expected credit losses for the impairment assessment. The provision of
ECL is sensitive to changes in estimates.
TheGrouprecognizedcontractassetsofRMB312,993,000,RMB297,193,000,RMB352,498,000and
RMB607,246,000 as at 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and 30 June 2025, respectively.
Except for Customer A which is the major customer to the Group and debtors with material
outstandingbalanceorcredit-impairedwhichassessesECLsonindividualbasis,theGroupuseprovision
matrix to calculate ECLs for trade and bills receivables. The provision rates and matrix are based on the
Group’s historical default rates from debtors with similar loss patterns taking into consideration
forward-looking information that is reasonable and supportable available without undue costs or effort.
At every reporting date, the historical observed default rates are reassessed and changes in the
forward-looking information are considered. The provision of ECLs is sensitive to changes in estimates.
The Group recognized gross carrying amount of trade receivables of RMB328,564,000,

Income tax provision of the Group in respect of operations in the PRC has been calculated at the
applicable tax rate on the estimated assessable profits for the year/period, based on the existing legislation,
interpretation and practices in respect thereof.
Pursuant to the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law (the ‘‘CIT’’), the CIT is unified at 25% for the years
ended 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended 30 June 2025.
Under the relevant regulations of the CIT Law, the Company located in the PRC is qualified as
high-technologyenterpriseandwasentitledtoapreferentialincometaxrateof15%fortheyearsfrom2024to
2025.
Under the relevant regulations of the CIT Law, research and development expenses incurred by the
Company located in the PRC for development of new technologies, new products, and new processes, which
have not resulted in intangible assets recognized in the current period, are subject to a 100% deduction in
accordancewithregulations,withanadditional75%,100%and100%deductionforresearchanddevelopment
expenses. If intangible assets are formed, they are amortized at 175%, 200% and 200% of the cost of the
intangible assets for the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024 respectively.
Pursuant to Thailand Enterprise Income Tax Law (the ‘‘EIT’’), the EIT is unified at 20% for the years
ended 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended 30 June 2025.
Pursuant to Malaysia Income Tax Act (the ‘‘ITA’’), the ITA is unified at 17% for the years ended 31
December 2022, 2023, 2024 and the six months ended 30 June 2025. No Malaysia Enterprise Income Tax has
been provided in the Historical Financial Information as the Group did not derive any estimated assessable
profit in Malaysia during Track Record Period.
NoHongKongprofitstaxhasbeenprovidedintheHistoricalFinancialInformationastheGroupdidnot
derive any estimated assessable profit in Hong Kong during Track Record Period.
TheGroupisoperatingincertainjurisdictionswherethePillarTwoRulesareeffectiveorenactedbutnot
effective. However, as the Group’s estimated effective tax rates of all the jurisdictions in which the Group
operates are higher than 15%, after taking into account the adjustments under the Pillar Two Rules based on
management’s best estimate, the management of the Group considered the Group is not liable to top-up tax
under the Pillar Two Rules.

TheCompanyhasadoptedashareawardscheme(‘‘theScheme’’)on12September2023forthepurposeto
attract and retain the best available personnel, to provide additional incentive to selected employees of the
Group(the‘‘Participants’’) andtopromotethesuccessof thebusinessof theGroup. TheSchemeshall bevalid
and effective from the date of adoption with a five-year vesting period (‘‘Vesting Period’’). Pursuant to the
Scheme,theCompanymaygrantrestrictedsharesoftheCompanytoParticipants,andcessationofrestrictionis
subjecttotherelevantemployeecontinuehis/heremploymentwiththeGroupwithalock-upperiodduringthe
Vesting Period.
To implement the Scheme, Shanghai Xinlianzhan Corporate Management Partnership (Limited
Partnership) (‘‘Shanghai Xinlianzhan’’) was established as a limited partnership on 11 May 2023 as the
employeeawardsplatformtoholdtheunderlyingawardedsharesoftheCompanyandcontrolledbyMs.Angela
Chen Mah (‘‘Ms. Chen’’) as executive partner of Shanghai Xinlianzhan. The source of the underlying awarded
shares (shares of the Company) shall be ordinary shares allotted by the Company (Note 36). After the shares
allotment, the Participants would indirectly hold the shareholding of the Company through Shanghai
Xinlianzhan. The shares of Shanghai Xinlianzhan are granted to the Participants at grant price of RMB3.60,
and 1 share of Shanghai Xinlianzhan represents the indirect holding of 1 share of the underlying awarded
shares.ParticipantsshallnottransfertherespectiveinterestinShanghaiXinlianzhanwithoutthepriorapproval
by the board of directors and shareholders of the Company. A Participant shall not have any interest or rights
(including the rights to receive dividends) in the awarded shares prior to the vesting of the awarded shares.
As at 31 December 2023, 2024 and 30 June 2025, the Scheme contained outstanding restricted shares of
2,150,005 shares of the Company.
At the end of Vesting Period, awarded shares of the Company granted to the Participants of the Scheme
will bevested andbecome unrestricted in various vesting periods. During the lock-upperiod, should any terms
as stated under Agreements for departing employees’ in Appendix VI of this prospectus, the Participant shall
transfer his/her interest in Shanghai Xinlianzhan by the terms as listed.

(d) Information of supplier finance arrangements
DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,theGroupenteredintosupplierfinancearrangementswithbanks.
Participation in the supplier finance arrangements is at the suppliers’ own discretion. When the supplier
receives the bank bill, they have the discretion to either hold it until maturity or redeem it prematurely.
Interest shall be incurred upon the supplier’s collection of early payment from the banks, which is
generally calculated based on the period from the early redemption date to the maturity date and the
agreed-upon interest rate. Consequently, the interest incurred by the supplier is contingent upon their
independent choice. In all cases, the Group shall settle the original invoice by paying the banks on the
invoice due date or at a later date as agreed with banks. In the consolidated statements of financial
position, the Group has presented the payables to the banks under these arrangements as ‘‘trade and bill
payables’’ (Note 30), and ‘‘bank borrowings’’ (Note 34) amounting to RMB20,747,000 and
RMB12,674,000 as at 31 December 2022, RMB43,366,000 and RMB19,706,000 as at 31 December
2023, RMB83,534,000 and RMB41,420,000 as at 31 December 2024 and RMB961,000 and
RMB38,614,000 as at 30 June 2025 respectively.
Under these arrangements, certain liabilities are presented as part of ‘‘trade and bill payables’’ due
to their similar nature and function with the Group’s trade payables to suppliers. The Group shall settle
with the banks with an averaging 81 days, 79 days, 81 days and 75 days of payment terms as at 31
December2022,2023,2024and30June2025respectively,comparedtotheoriginalpaymenttermsoffered
bythesuppliersaveraging77days,74days,70daysand68daysaftertheinvoicedateasat31 December
2022, 2023, 2024 and 30 June 2025, respectively.
Certainliabilitiesarepresentedaspartof‘‘bankborrowings’’duetotheirnatureandfunctionofthe
liabilities being substantially different from the Group’s trade payables to suppliers. In particular, the
Group benefits from extended payment terms, averaging 159 days, 181 days, 180 days and 176 days after
the invoice dates as at 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and 30 June 2025, respectively, compared to the
original payment terms averaging 81 days, 79 days, 81 days and 78 days after the invoice dates, as at 31
December 2022, 2023, 2024 and 30 June 2025, respectively.
Changesintheseliabilities mainly resultfrom purchases ofgoods andservices andsubsequentcash
settlements. During the Track Record Period, the portion of liabilities presented as bank borrowings
under supplier finance arrangements of RMB19,882,000, RMB31,501,000, RMB42,221,000 and
RMB43,395,000 for the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and six months ended 30 June 2025
respectively. There were no other significant non-cash changes in these liabilities.

47 FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT
The Group and the Company’s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks which comprise credit
risk,interestraterisk,liquidityriskandcommoditypricerisk.TheGroup’soverallriskmanagementfocuseson
the unpredictability of financial markets and seeks to minimize potential adverse effects on the Group’s
financial performance. Risk management is carried out by key management under the policies approved by the
board of directors. The Group does not have written risk management policies. However, the directors of the
Companyidentifyandevaluaterisksregularlyandformulatestrategiestomanagefinancialrisks.Generally,the
Group employs a conservative strategy regarding its financial risk management. As the directors consider that
the Group’s exposure to financial risk is kept at a minimum level, the Group has not used any derivatives or
other instruments for hedging purposes. The most significant risks to which the Group is exposed to are
described below:
(a) Credit risk
The Group’s credit risk is primarily attributable to trade and bills receivables, contract assets,
deposits and other receivables, amounts due from a related party, restricted bank balance, pledged bank
deposits and cash and cash equivalents.
– I-90 –

=== PAGE 603 ===
APPENDIX I ACCOUNTANTS’ REPORT
The Company’s credit risk is primarily attributable to trade and bills receivables, contract assets,
deposits and other receivables, amounts due from subsidiaries, pledged bank deposits, restricted bank
deposits and cash and cash equivalents.
TheGroupandtheCompany’smaximumexposuretocreditriskwhichwillcauseafinanciallossto
the Group due to failure to discharge an obligation by the counterparties is the carrying amount of the
respective recognized financial assets as stated in the consolidated statements of financial position and
statements of financial position of the Company at the end of each reporting period. The Group and the
Companydonotholdanycollateralorothercreditenhancementstocoverthecreditrisksassociatedwith
its financial assets.
Trade and bills receivables, and contract assets arising from contracts with customers
In order to minimize credit risk, the management of the Group and the Company has
delegatedateamtoberesponsibleforthedeterminationofcreditlimits,creditapprovalsandother
monitoring procedures to ensure that follow-up action is taken to recover overdue debts. In
addition, the management of the Group and the Company review the recoverable amount of each
individual debt at the end of each reporting period to ensure that adequate provisions for
impairmentlossesaremadeforirrecoverableamountsontradeandbillsreceivableandthecontract
assets.
The Group has concentration of credit risk on the trade and bills receivables from the largest
customer amounted to approximately RMB156,398,000, RMB243,638,000, RMB326,160,000 and
RMB296,203,000 representing 37.6%, 41.4%, 47.7% and 58.1% of total financial assets at
amortized cost as at 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and 30 June 2025, respectively. The Group
monitors the level of exposure to ensure that follow up actions and/or corrective actions are taken
promptly to lower the risk exposure.
Other than the concentration of credit risk mentioned above, the Group does not have any
othersignificantconcentrationofcreditrisk.Tradeandbillsreceivablesandcontractassetsconsist
of a large number of customers, spread across diverse industries and geographical areas.
The Group and the Company always recognize lifetime ECL for trade and bills receivables,
and contract assets. In respect of trade and bill receivables, individual credit evaluation are
performed for those debtors with material outstanding balance or credit-impaired, the Group and
the Company measure the ECLs by performing impairment assessment under the ECL model on
remainingtradeandbills receivablesandthecontractassetscollectively basedonsharedcreditrisk
characteristics by reference to the Group and the Company’s internal credit rating.
Deposits and other receivables
The Group measures the loss allowance equal to 12-month ECL of other receivables. For
those balance expected to be significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition, the Group
apply lifetime ECL based on aging for classes with different credit risk characteristics and
exposures.

Bank acceptance bills receivables, restricted bank balances, pledged bank deposits, cash and cash
equivalents
The credit risk for bank acceptance bills receivable, restricted bank balance, pledged bank
deposits and bank balancearelimitedbecausethe counterparties arebanks withhigh credit ratings
assigned by international credit-rating agencies. There has been no history of default in relation to
thesebanks.TheGroupandtheCompanyperformsimpairmentassessmentonthesebalancesunder
12-months ECL model. The management of the Group and the Company considers the risk of
default is regarded as low based on the average loss rate by reference to credit rating assigned by
international credit-rating agencies. As at 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024 and 30 June 2025, the
Group and the Company assessed that the ECL for bank acceptance bills receivables, restricted
bank balance, pledged bank deposits and cash and cash equivalents were insignificant.
Amounts due from subsidiaries of the Company
The management of the Company regularly monitors the business performance of the
subsidiaries. The Company credit risks in the balance are mitigated through the Company’s power
and influence to participate in the relevant activities and operation of the subsidiaries and
overriding repayment on demand.
